quoted_text:
【全网首个 Agent 撸毛项目来了！】

过去，Web3 用户最熟悉的事情就是撸空投。
注册账号、做任务、刷交互、盯活动，很多时候不是项目本身有多复杂，而是谁愿意花更多时间，谁就可能获得更多机会，因为熬大夜甚至一度衍生出web3生物钟。

但 AI Agent 的出现，可能会让这套玩法迎来一次升级。

未来，用户不一定需要亲自完成每一次链上操作，而是可以把任务交给 Agent，让它帮你分析机会、执行交易、参与生态交互，事实上最近我们用币安 Agent Wallet 打狗应该深有体会。

这就是我最近比较关注的一个新方向：Agentic Mining（Agent 挖矿）。

而 @42space 是全网首个推出 Agent 撸毛玩法的项目，也是第一个真正将 Agent 纳入积分激励体系的项目。

🔸 42 已经率先把 Agent 变成积分活动的参与者

本周 42 Points 正式上线，过去的Tickets自动兑换为Points，并且采用每周结算的方式。

这次活动有一个很值得关注的设计：
用户自己自然可以手动参与，但 42 Space更鼓励让 AI Agent 代替你来赚取积分，而且针对 Agent 交互设置了额外的积分激励。

这意味着 42 并不是简单地把 AI 当成一个辅助工具，而是在用实际奖励引导用户改变参与方式。

更值得期待的是，官方后续规划的 Agentic Mining 玩法。

按照目前披露的设计，用户未来可以通过铸造 NFT 来支持自己选择的 Agent。
Agent 将在 42 的市场中持续寻找交易机会、执行策略，而相关操作和决策过程也会向外公开。

Agent 创造的积分，则会按照 NFT 对应的份额进行分配，最高积分加成达到 1.5倍。

以前 NFT 更多只是躺在你钱包里的收藏，而在这种模式下，它还有机会成为连接用户与 AI Agent 的载体，让普通用户也能参与 Agent 创造的生态价值。

从让 Agent 替你做任务，到让 Agent 自主参与市场，再到通过 NFT 分享它创造的积分，42 正在尝试建立一套新的参与和激励模式。

🔸 我认为42 是最适配 Agent 的项目！

不管是加密、股票还是现实世界，在42都一应俱全，凭借过去平台积累的大量用户和极具规模的交易体量，能够在短期吸引更多用户参与的同时，老用户依然可以轻松将Agent利用起来。

在我看来，42 提供的是足够丰富的市场和交易场景，而 Agent 则有机会解决用户精力有限、信息处理能力不足的问题。

🔸 币安已经在铺路，42 正在践行 Agent 撸毛

其实从币安今年的布局中，也能看出 Agent 参与 Web3 交易已经不再只是一个遥远的设想。

从 AI Pro 开放测试，到 Agentic Wallet，再到 Agent ID，币安正在逐步完善 AI 参与交易所业务所需要的关键能力。

AI Pro 让 Agent 有机会直接参与现货和合约交易；
Agentic Wallet 解决资金管理与链上签名问题；Agent ID 则进一步为 Agent 建立身份体系。

这些动作放在一起看，实际上是在为一个新的交易生态做准备。

这件事无论对CEX还是对整个加密行业都意义重大。

过去交易所的核心竞争力，很大程度上取决于能吸引多少真实用户。

但未来，用户可能会通过自己的 Agent 完成大量交易行为，一个人管理多个 Agent、运行不同策略，也可能成为常态。

这时候，交易所争夺的就不只是用户打开 App 的时间，而是谁能成为这些 Agent 执行交易时优先调用的平台。

对于 Agent 来说，平台是否具备稳定的接口、完善的交易权限和可靠的资金管理能力，可能比界面设计得漂不漂亮重要得多。

所以，Agent 带来的不仅是交易工具的升级，还有潜在交易需求和订单流结构的变化。

对链上生态也是一样。

当 Agent 能够独立完成信息分析、协议交互和交易执行，用户参与链上活动的成本就会进一步降低。

未来链上生态的活跃度，可能不再完全取决于有多少人亲自操作，还取决于有多少 Agent 在持续参与经济活动。

而  @42space  作为 YZi Labs 投资、与 Binance Wallet 深度集成的项目，成为全网第一个响应币安 Agent 战略并推出 Agent 撸毛玩法的项目，我认为是有一定先发优势的。

🔸 现在就可以体验，Clawby 合作最高 1.5× 加成！

除了已经上线的 42 Points，42 目前还与 @openClawby 完成了协议合作。

通过 Clawby 的 Skill，可以驱动 AI Agent 在 42 注册账户并参与协议交互。

目前，前 5000 名符合条件的交易者，通过这种方式参与活动，最高可以获得 1.5× 积分加成。

对于想要尝试 AI Agent 参与 Web3 交互的朋友来说，这是一个很直接的体验入口。
安装skill🔽
https://t.co/B35ptS11yf

🔸 Agentic Mining 才刚刚拉开帷幕

我觉得这次最值得关注的，并不是 42 又上线了一场积分活动，而是它正在尝试改变用户参与 Web3 的方式。

过去是人寻找机会、执行交易、完成交互；未来则可能是人负责制定目标和策略，Agent 负责持续执行。

从币安的基础设施布局，到 42 把 Agent 引入实际积分激励，这条赛道已经开始从概念走向应用。

而且，这只是一个开端。

42 后续还会围绕 Agentic Mining 推出更多活动和产品动作，显然不打算把这件事局限在一次 Points 活动里。

AI 和 Web3 的结合，真正有想象力的地方，从来不是让 AI 帮我们回答问题，而是让 AI 能够真正参与经济活动。

当 Agent 开始替人交易、替人交互，Web3 的下一轮玩法可能才真正拉开序幕。

作为 42 Space 的老用户，我本来就一直在参与，而对于眼前这条新赛道，我肯定会持续关注 42 的后续动作。

text:
你根本不知道，做 KOL/KOC 有多难。

聊这个话题，我大概率算是整个中文币圈里，少数几个走出不同路径的人。

先说结论：做 KOL/KOC，人脉真的太重要了。

如果有 10 个人愿意稳定给你介绍合作，基本上你就能在币圈活下去。

当然，最舒服的还是傍上交易所包月，毕竟这玩意儿才是稳定现金流。做的好的群友，基本都吃上了。

如果你没吃上，那就只能靠自己的「舔功」上位了。

我个人的路径几乎没法复制。机缘巧合之下拉了个全真社区，又机缘巧合火了一段时间，才让我没有饿死。

但绝大多数 KOL/KOC，尤其是账号质量一般、又没什么资源的新人，走的完全是另一条路。

那就是不停地舔，拼命往圈子里挤。

你可能需要加入十几个 KOL 社区，天天在里面混脸熟，先从陌生人混成普通朋友，再从普通朋友混成好朋友，最后才有可能换来一点合作机会。

这个过程非常累，甚至可以说非常痛苦。

因为作为一个新人，你在别人眼里几乎是零价值的。

没人认识你，没人认可你，更没人有义务带你赚钱。

你只能不断展示自己的价值，就像一个拼命追着镜头跑的十八线小明星，生怕错过任何一次露脸的机会。

即便如此，成功率依然低得可怜。

你可能尝试了 100 次，只有 1 次有效。更绝望的是，剩下 99 次失败之后，面对同一批人，把同样的事情再做一遍。

再聊聊更现实的：送礼。

之前就听说，很多 KOL 为了拿合作，是需要给 BD 送礼的。

我自己暂时没送过，但几个好基友一直劝我送。

因为确实有几个 BD 对我特别好，基本属于把饭喂到嘴边了。说实话，这礼我确实该送，只是一直没送而已。

而且送礼也是一门学问，送什么、什么时候送、怎么送，都有讲究。

我个人的理解是，很多时候最难的不是花钱，而是让人家愿意收。

如果对方愿意接受你一份价值不低的礼物，至少说明你们的关系已经到了某个程度。

你送出去一万块，未来人家可能通过合作给你带来远超一万块的价值。

但你以为送礼就已经够离谱了？

不好意思，这可能还只是最低档。

我听过的其他案例，包括但不限于：

通宵陪打游戏。
甚至陪睡觉的传闻。

陪打游戏我还能理解，毕竟就是牺牲点时间。

但陪睡觉，我特么是真的觉得离谱。

当然，若是大哥想让你陪睡觉，到也是一个机会，睡对了大哥，就算你是个职校生，睡上一次，B也涨价了。这也是捞女为什么被骂。因为他们确实找到了捷径。

不过话又说回来，为什么有些人总喜欢走捷径？

因为在一个高度依赖资源、人脉和利益交换的行业里，有时候你辛辛苦苦努力一年，可能真不如别人认识一个大哥。

这也是为什么，有些人明明没什么专业能力，却能拿到远超普通人的资源。

你可以不认可这种方式，但很难否认资源关系带来的巨大差距。

所以我现在越来越觉得，普通男 KOL 想在币圈混出头，是真的难。

如果你本身就有钱、有资源、有背景，那当然舒服。

但如果你什么都没有，只是一个普通人，想靠写内容、做研究、慢慢积累粉丝，然后靠这个养活自己……

说实话，真的得做好吃屎的准备。

黄仁勋婚外情风波背后：1552 亿美元身家面临离婚分割悬念，妻子或分得超 750 亿美元

在老黄致信员工坦承对妻子“不忠”后，不仅引发了英伟达股价震荡，更将自己 1552 亿美元的身家推向了潜在的财产分割风口。

按照加利福尼亚州的“夫妻共同财产”法规，婚内积累的资产原则上按 5:5 均分。而这起潜在离婚案中最关键的法律细节在于：两人的婚姻始于 1980 年代中期，而英伟达创立于 1993 年。

这意味着，黄仁勋名下超过 3.5% 的英伟达核心股权（最大的个人股东席位）几乎完全是在婚姻存续期内取得。

若未曾设立明确的婚前或婚后财产隔离协议，妻子 Lori Huang 理论上有权分得至少 750 亿美元（超 5000 亿人民币）资产。这一金额将直接翻倍超越此前贝佐斯离婚案中前妻获得的 360 亿美元，创下全球商业史上的最高纪录。

《华尔街日报》此前披露，黄仁勋曾透露妻子几十年来掌管了家庭的所有财务与文件签署，自己甚至“连自家住址都不知道、从未亲自付过账单”。

对二级市场而言，私德层面的风波往往能随时间淡化，但核心股东名下超过 3.5% 的关键筹码一旦被迫切割或进入减持窗口，给英伟达带来的控制权震荡与流动性冲击，才是资金最担忧的现实变量。

We’ve been using ODE Policy for visual policy distillation, with strong early results. Learning how actions evolve over time gives the policy a natural way to capture the continuity of robot motion.

In the video, our Franka robot learns to thread a nut onto a bolt in simulation, reproducing the task from SGS.

Next, we plan to use ODE Policy to distill a wider range of assembly skills into policies that act from camera images, from fitting gears and inserting pegs to joining connectors.
author: axisrobotics
quoted_text:
🚀 Nature does not move in discrete jumps. Why should robot policies?

Super excited to release ODE Policy — perhaps our most exciting breakthrough in my lab this year! 🤖🔥

Think about how humans reach for a cup. Our movements evolve continuously, governed by underlying dynamics. Yet, most robot policies — from Diffusion and Flow Matching to VLAs — learn to predict explicit actions.

What if robots learned how actions evolve, instead of predicting actions?

💡 That's ODE Policy for Embodied AI.

We use a neural Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) to learn continuous action dynamics, rather than directly generating actions.

One simple idea. Five types of robots. Multiple learning paradigms.

✅ Single-arm manipulation
✅ Dual-arm manipulation
✅ Dexterous hands
✅ Humanoid whole-body control
✅ Aerial robots

And it goes far beyond imitation learning:

⚡ VLA (π0.5): 96.0% vs. 75.5% success after one epoch.
🌍 4.5B World Action Model: 82.6% vs. 24.6% success, with ~4× faster action generation.
🏃 RL: More efficient humanoid whole-body motion learning.

For years, we've focused on scaling robot data, models, and compute.

But what if the next fundamental breakthrough comes from rethinking WHAT robots learn, rather than just HOW MUCH they learn?

Huge congratulations to Jindou Jia and our amazing team! 👏

📄 Paper: https://t.co/HeHw2a8Wzj
🌐 Project: https://t.co/mEaZIdoRjs

#ODEPolicy #EmbodiedAI #PhysicalAI #RobotLearning #WorldModels #VLA #MARSLab

Claude Fable 5.2 发布了，普通用户最需要搞清楚的 4 件事：

1. Pro 用户这周可以免费体验

11 月 9 日至 16 日，Fable 可以直接使用套餐额度，不用额外付费。

但最多只能占每周额度的 50%，活动结束后恢复按量收费。

2. 老用户可以免费重置额度

Pro 送 1 次，Max、Ultra 根据订阅时长送 1～3 次。

重置可以恢复本周已经消耗的 Fable 额度，5 小时窗口也会补满。

入口：Settings → Usage → Reset for free。

注意，Pro 的重置机会 11 月 16 日到期，且需要在发布前已经付费订阅。

3. API 降价 20%，不代表使用成本一定更低

Fable 5.2 的 API 输入 / 输出价格为 $8 / $40（每百万 Token），仍然是 Opus 5.5 的两倍。

但 Fable 处理复杂任务可能消耗更少的 Token。

所以真正该比较的是完成一个任务的总成本，而不是 Token 单价。

4. 日常使用没必要全部切换到 Fable

Anthropic 官方建议：

普通编程、知识工作 → Opus 5.5

复杂、开放式技术任务 → Fable 5.2

简单任务 → Sonnet 或 Haiku 5.5

Fable 虽然更强，但消耗订阅额度也更快。

建议 Pro 用户趁这一周，拿一个真正复杂的任务比较一下 Fable 和 Opus，再决定值不值得额外花钱。

text:
知名开发者、T3 Code 创始人 Theo 发现，Anthropic 新发布的 Fable 5.2 虽然更强，但订阅用户能使用的 API 等价用量反而少得多。

Theo 长期记录 Claude Code 的实际请求数据。根据他的估算，同样支付每月 200 美元的 Claude Ultra 订阅费，如果使用 Opus 5.5，每月能获得相当于约 1.5 万美元的 API 用量；换成 Fable 5.2，则只有约 3000 美元，相差近 5 倍。

Anthropic 还规定，Ultra 用户每周最多只能把总额度的 50% 用于 Fable。即使没有用完全部额度，只要 Fable 达到上限，就必须切换其他模型，或者额外付费继续使用。

quoted_text:
@HyperliquidX's IOC speed-bump mechanism has a flaw. Normally designed to protect makers in the interests of a more liquid market, it breaks down in periods of high activity. When blocks become full, pending modifies and cancels queue up for later blocks, so their latency increases. However, IOCs behave as though they have a separate blockspace dedicated for them, and their latency barely budges. You can see this in the lower left chart, showing latency of different order types during 19 activity bursts. 

The result is that under relatively modest load (25-30k tps), IOC + 8 bps (priority fee) orders can pick off resting liquidity before it has a chance to get out the way. Meanwhile, under higher load (35-40k tps), even IOCs without any priority fee can pick off resting liquidity. 

This, in my opinion, is antithetical to the ethos and design of the ALO and cancel prioritization mechanism and needs investigation by the team. It exists to reduce toxicity from HFT takers, and is breaking down precisely when most needed. 

It may also be exploitable. If IOCs really are insulated from the congestion affecting cancels and modifies, a malicious user could spam orders, delaying makers’ cancels while their own IOCs go through, and taking the liquidity left stale.

One single example that occurred on AVAX today caused 1.3M$ of volume to be adversely selected for a total loss of ~13k$ over the subsequent 10 seconds. This affected us materially. Faced with such episodes of adverse selection, spreads and liquidity are undoubtedly worse than they could be otherwise.

Would appreciate if anyone with a contact at HL could share this with the team.

⚠️ Exploit Analysis: Ankr Cross-Chain Bridge Attack

On November 9, @ankr’s cross-chain bridge contract on #Ethereum was exploited, resulting in losses of approximately $300,000. The attacker submitted five forged cross-chain withdrawal receipts, all referencing the same legitimate deposit transaction on #Optimism, but with altered recipients, tokens, and withdrawal amounts. All five receipts carried valid signatures from the bridge’s trusted consensus/notary signer. The bridge contract’s withdraw() function approved the withdrawals without independently verifying that the corresponding assets had actually been deposited on the source chain.

🔍 Root Cause:

The Ankr Ethereum bridge delegates verification of source-chain deposits to a trusted notary/consensus signer. On the destination chain, withdraw() releases assets according to the fields in a withdrawal receipt as long as it carries a valid signature, without enforcing a one-to-one, non-reusable binding to the corresponding source-chain event.

As a result, if an attacker obtains—or manages to forge—withdrawal receipts that validate against the trusted signer, they can:

Reuse a historical, legitimate #Optimism deposit transaction hash as a reference for the “source proof.”
Alter the recipient, token, and amount in the receipts to withdraw multiple assets repeatedly against the same source transaction.
Bypass detection because the bridge only validates the signatures and receipt structure, without verifying whether a corresponding deposit exists on the source chain for the specified amount, token, and recipient.
The attacker submitted five forged receipts and drained the bridge contract. All five signed receipts referenced the same Optimism source transaction, but specified altered recipients, tokens, and amounts. The notary signer for all five was 0x4069D8A3dE3A72EcA86CA5e0a4B94619085E7362.

The implementation of withdraw() shows that the contract performs no checks on rawReceipt. How the attacker obtained signatures valid for the notary address, _consensusAddress, remains unknown. A compromised private key or signatures obtained through social engineering are suspected.

text: 1/100 On the morning of 12 January 2007, a young man in a baseball cap played the violin in a Washington metro station for about 43 minutes. He was Joshua Bell, one of the most celebrated violinists in the world. His instrument was a Stradivarius made in 1713 and reportedly worth millions of dollars. A few days earlier he had filled a Boston concert hall where good seats cost around 100 dollars. That morning, about 1,100 people walked past him on their way to work. Seven stopped to listen for at least a minute. One woman recognised him. The open violin case collected about 32 dollars. The journalist Gene Weingarten set up the stunt for the Washington Post, and his article won a Pulitzer Prize in 2008. He noticed something striking in the video. Several small children tried to stop and listen, and each time a parent pulled them along. It was a newspaper experiment with no control group, at rush hour, in a noisy hall. Many commuters were simply late for work, and some may not have liked classical music. Still, the scene became famous because it captured something many people feel. Hurry can make you walk past what you would otherwise pay to see. This chapter looks at hurry itself. You will see what research says about rushing and where the pressure comes from, and how to slow down without falling behind.

text:
If there’s a conflation, I think it’s between in principle and in practice. I’m deliberately not making an epistemological claim. The Church–Turing–Deutsch principle is a claim about physics: every finite physical process can be simulated, to any accuracy, by a universal computer. It says nothing about how reasoning works. However given current physics, it limits what any answer to that question can look like since the brain is a finite physical system.

On the Turing machine, its simplicity is the point, not a limitation. Universality runs the other way from how you put it. The claim isn’t that a complicated machine can be made to behave like a Turing machine. It’s that a universal Turing machine, given enough tape and time, can do anything any complicated machine can. Life is a good example: Life can host a universal Turing machine, and a universal Turing machine can run Life. The architectures differ, but they can do the same things because they are both universal.

So I’m not stretching the definition to cover “anything that reasons”. That would be trivial, as you say. The claim is that under current known physical law (in particular QM), nothing physical can compute something a universal Turing machine can’t, due to the CTD Principle. That isn’t trivial, because it could be false. Penrose thinks it is, which is why he has proposed new physics. He might be right, but his most admirable claim is that he acknowledges that he bears the burden of conjecturing new physical laws. That’s the burden I meant.

On “no one knows how the brain works”, I agree (though I might say " no one knows how the mind works). Ignoring the Penrose route, that means that we don’t have the program for creativity because the mind is physically instantiated in the brain which must obey the laws of physics. I also agree that imitation settles nothing. I’m not arguing “machines already do X and Y, so they’ll do everything”. The argument comes from the best current known law of physics (QM) which as far as we know has universal (nay multiversal!) reach, not from a list of successes so far.

On Defender: the arcade board can’t do what your phone does because of memory, speed and I/O, not because it’s a different kind of computer. Give it enough memory and time and it could run anything your phone runs, just absurdly slowly. That’s the distinction I mean. Your original question was whether the brain does something a Turing machine cannot do, even in principle. It may do, but that’s a claim that needs new physics.

text:
Here is something that didn’t get enough attention: the ECDSA/fail challenge.

In this challenge, people used their AI agents to reduce the resources needed for a key operation in Shor’s algorithm (that operation is needed to break quantum-vulnerable ECDSA signatures -- the type of signatures used by Bitcoin, Ethereum, and many more).

The amazing results: they reduced the resource cost needed for this operation by over 90%! 
This took only a few months.
Interesting to note: this is 70% better than Google's estimate.

Why is this very technical story important? 
Because it demonstrates (i) how AI can improve the efficiency of quantum attacks, and (ii) how AI could accelerate the Q-Day timeline.

The important thing here:
A few months of concentrated effort happening on people’s *laptops* resulted in a substantial reduction in the resources needed for a quantum attack. 
It's a long sentence but read it again. 
We're not talking here an extremely long timespan and fancy equipment which few people can access. 

Now imagine the possibilities if someone dedicated more time and resources to this effort.

Time to migrate to quantum-safe tech and to STARKs.

之前康伟和黄乐夫妻档的私募和熙投资可不是什么小私募，而且不是私募股权投资公司，是二级市场的私募基金公司。最高管理规模接近200亿。当时算上海私募头部机构了。

你看看康伟的履历，顶尖的私募大佬。申银万国证券研究所首席策略分析师，2004年，首届新财富最佳策略分析师，中海基金总经理（投委会主任）

当时华东最大的算力中心之一在上海松江，他们也是牵头参与方，后面卖掉了项目股权。

后面因为涉及一些证券市场的违规事件，慧球科技案，被证监会重罚，现在和熙管理规模只剩下10亿左右。

就是顶尖头部私募大佬切换到算力圈，资源人脉都是顶配的，国内传统资本市场趋严又受罚玩不下去了，出海做国际算力业务，而黄乐是康伟老婆。黄乐最近一年半一直被美国政府调查芯片贸易的事。

我和他们之前有过一些加密行业投研领域合作，所以这些基本事情情况还是了解的。

不要闭眼就瞎说。

quoted_text:
美股半导体集体反弹，链上大户却在减仓。真正的分歧，集中在英伟达。

昨夜纳指上涨 2.74%，费城半导体指数大涨 6.85%，AMD 涨 13.26%，Coherent 涨近 17%。大额账户并没有普遍追涨，反而出现明显的「价涨仓缩」。

1、存储板块：空头回补，多头也在离场

美光、闪迪均上涨逾 6%，但大额账户多空仓位同步收缩。美光一地址趁反弹清仓原有多单，交易盈利约 35.13 万美元。存储板块整体呈现空头获利回补、多头借反弹减仓的局面。

2、AMD：暴涨 13.26%，OI 却下降 35.7%

大额账户多仓净减 188 万美元，空仓净减 676 万美元。价格上涨伴随未平仓合约明显收缩，说明这轮反弹更多伴随着原有仓位退出，而非大规模新增押注。

3、英伟达：唯一明显的增仓集中地

NVDA 正股昨夜反而收跌 4.27%，链上大额账户却增加了约 2,223 万美元多仓和 3,258 万美元空仓，OI 增加 30.4%。

多空双方都在扩大敞口，分歧明显加剧。

4、科技七巨头：多空同步撤退

苹果、微软、谷歌、亚马逊、Meta、Netflix、特斯拉，多仓净减约 652 万美元，空仓净减约 672 万美元。

整体来看，半导体反弹并没有带来普遍的链上追涨。

TradingBeats 这组数据最值得注意的地方是：市场在反弹，但大资金并没有一致看多。存储和 AMD 主要表现为仓位退出，英伟达却出现多空双向加仓。

这轮 AI 股反弹究竟是空头回补，还是新一轮资金重新布局？英伟达的多空博弈，或许比股价本身更值得关注。

text:
Stablecoins solved the easy part of cross-border payments.

The token moves value between chains at low cost, and treasury teams now treat that as the default. What it didn't touch is the four layers that decide whether the payment actually clears at the other end:

1⃣Local rails, the card, the wallet, the QR code in the country you're paying into, and whether any of them accepts a foreign-funded transaction without a 24-hour decline loop.
2⃣FX between corridors, the spread between what the sender's bank quotes and what arrives.
3⃣Compliance handoffs, the back-and-forth between sender, intermediary, and receiver that decides who carries the risk.
4⃣Settlement window, when the funds become usable rather than just visible.
Stablecoins didn't touch those. Most chains weren't built for them either.

#AlchemyChain was designed for these points. TPOA consensus ties finality to the block, so a confirmed payment is a settled payment. MiCA and HKMA compliance live at the protocol layer, so regulatory clarity travels with the transaction. The robust payment channels network enables smooth borderless transfer in the real world.

In some cases, the token moved, while the chain underneath didn't catch up. Alchemy Chain was one of the few chains built for this layer rather than retrofit onto it.

$ACH

Norway now has more than 2,000 underwater AI laser robots shooting lice off its salmon

they're made by a company called Stingray, and they already guard more than 50 million salmon and trout 24/7

the reason is sea lice, tiny parasites that latch onto salmon and feed on them

as few as 11 can kill a small fish, and one pen can hold 150,000 salmon

the usual fix is pumping the fish out and blasting them with warm water or water jets to knock the lice off

but the handling is so rough that Norway's fish health report ranks it the top cause of death in full-grown farmed salmon

so instead, Stingray puts a robot inside the pen that hunts lice one at a time, all day:

> two cameras watch every salmon that swims past

> AI checks two frames to make sure it's really a louse

> then a green laser fires from up to 2 meters away

> the salmon's scales reflect the beam, so the fish swims off fine and the louse is dead

we now live in a world where AI lasers do pest control on your dinner lmao

text:
民主党准备对美国加密行业发起新一轮监管战。

Eleanor Terrett 爆料，众议院民主党正在讨论把 Maxine Waters 2025 年提出的《Crypto Investor and Consumer Bill of Rights》，扩展成下一届国会的完整加密市场结构法案，并吸收此前参议院民主党与共和党谈判达成的部分条款。

这套方案有三个方向：

第一，扩大 SEC 对加密市场的监管权，压缩 CFTC 的角色；

第二，加入更严格的伦理条款，限制特朗普及其他联邦官员参与加密业务；

第三，强化交易所和平台的消费者保护。

Waters 去年提出的投资者权利清单：

7×24 小时真人客服，等待时间不得超过5分钟。

用户提现、转账原则上必须在24小时内完成。

客户资产必须隔离托管，未经同意不得挪用、借贷或再质押。

每月至少一次可加密验证的储备证明，并由注册会计师出具鉴证。

引入类似 SIPC 的客户资产保护机制。

强制受托义务、最佳执行，禁止平台抢跑和关联自营交易对赌。

问题来了：

共和党版 CLARITY Act 的核心方向，是让 CFTC 主导数字商品现货市场监管。民主党现在想把监管重心重新推向 SEC。

这对交易所意味着更重的合规负担，对代币项目意味着更大的证券监管不确定性，DeFi 也可能成为下一轮监管争议的焦点。

同时号称超级护城河的软银愿景基金，由盈转亏，原本市场预期本季会盈利，但随着 Arm、英特尔、Coupang 等持股股价下跌，导致业绩受拖累。

目前孙正义的美国数据中心基建计划、半导体股票持仓、押注 OpenAI 上市的 AI 三支箭中，有两个成为了近期整家公司的拖累。

希望老哥这波能撑住。
author: _FORAB
quoted_text:
AI 杠杆狂人孙正义，这波可能要栽了？就在民主党回归，引发半导体恐慌后，媒体们爆料称，一位神秘卖家，正在拍卖十几笔数据中心贷款。

其中的一笔，还是 OpenAI 与软银的联合项目，然后马斯克直接点名说，孙正义的软银，正在违约其涡轮机订单。

因为以前狂砸钱投 OpenAI，还跟 OpenAI、甲骨文一起搞超大型 AI 数据中心的软银。为了解决数据中心特别耗电的问题，就去订了大量燃气涡轮机来发电。

而现在因为数据中心项目的迅速遇冷，软银很可能已经出现，明明下了订单，但是因无法付后续款项而违约。

同时，银行也在着急甩卖数据中心相关的贷款，其中包括软银参与的那个。这说明有人开始担心这些项目，不能顺利建起来，甚至赚不回钱。

目前软银为了支持 OpenAI，用过大规模过桥贷款，有过 400 亿美元额度的安排，以及用 ARM 股票做抵押融资等，因此存在杠杆压力。

text:
The U.S. gov wants to maintain its dominance in AI and prevent China from catching up. China hawks believe denying access to Nvidia chips will slow China’s AI development.

Nvidia wants to maintain its market dominance and avoid being replaced by Chinese chipmakers. And believe that cutting China off completely would only accelerate domestic alternatives, potentially leaving China with a self-sufficient AI ecosystem. 

The Chinese government, meanwhile, wants to accelerate its domestic chip industry by imposing additional restrictions on Nvidia imports. It’s betting that short-term chip shortages are worth the long-term payoff of breaking free from America’s technological chokehold. Developing a domestic chip industry requires massive investment, and forcing Chinese companies to buy homegrown chips is one way to guarantee demand and channel funding into domestic chipmakers.

Chinese AI companies, especially small and mid-sized ones, are the ones suffering from underperforming domestic chips. With limited funding, they need to make every dollar count, deliver results, and raise more money from hype-driven VCs. That’s why they’re willing to pay a hefty premium for Nvidia chips.

And arbitrageurs see an opportunity in the gap between demand and supply. For context, the price difference for B300 chips is reportedly around 4x.

Only time will tell which theory holds up. But for the rest of us, it’ll be fascinating to watch these competing bets play out in real time. With information and data more accessible than ever, we can test these theories against actual AI progress, chipmakers’ growth, and production output. 

And play our btc go up… T.T

‼️ vLLM drops a tool call when a param is named from, class or in.

Two fix PRs are open, neither merged yet. Rename the param for now, e.g. from > sender.

"Here is my public wallet address: [address]. Never ask for my seed phrase. Pull my full transaction history from free public explorers and find every address poisoning attempt: tiny or zero-value transfers from addresses that look like ones I really use, same first and last characters. Show each fake next to the real address it copies, with the differing characters highlighted. Then tell me if I ever sent funds to one of the fakes, and give me 3 habits that stop this for good."

Never copy an address from your history. Use your saved contacts.

我觉得擦屁股最好是先用干纸巾，再用湿纸巾。

而不是先用湿纸巾再用干纸巾。

因为刚拉完屎的时候，通常还会残留一些比较大块的屎。

这个时候如果你先用湿纸巾去擦，屎它本来就自带水分，湿纸巾也自带水分，而水分是有渗透性的，你这个时候去擦，屎很有可能会通过水的渗透性渗到你手上，你可能察觉不了，但是实际就是有。

而且湿纸巾还会拖着屎，把原本没沾到的地方抹得到处都是。

所以最好是先用干纸巾把比较大块的先擦掉，干纸巾能很好地吸收，不会让水分渗透过去，等差不多干净了，最后再用湿纸巾收尾，这样是最好的。

Don't sleep on co-browsing.

It turns out agents like Muse and Instinct are great for routine tasks (e.g. booking a restaurant), but many tasks on the internet are aspirational - planning a trip, vacation, and even work. Those require human browsing and clicking around, and not just delegation to an agent in a text back-and-forth dynamic.

The category of co-browsing (using AI alongside you in the browser) is the most underhyped in the entire AI space right now. Using your browser but with an agent alongside you creates a powerful combination for many types of experiences. 

You get the best of two worlds.

It also explains why claude and chatgpt added an in-app browser in the last few months, plus whatsapp is reported to work on one as well.

It was always the reason we believed in WebMCP, and there is so much more to explore and build in that direction.

Top 10 institutional research use cases for Token Terminal:

1. Measure issuance and flows. See where assets are issued, redeemed, and bridged, and how their supply moves across blockchains.

2. Decompose growth and decline. Separate price changes from issuance and redemptions. Identify which reference assets, tokens, issuers, chains, and venues account for changes in each metric.

3. Examine productive use in DeFi. Measure the share of an asset’s onchain market cap deposited into DeFi venues, and analyze how it is used in lending and trading.

4. Analyze onchain price discovery through perpetuals. Analyze prices in 24/7 perpetual markets, including when traditional exchanges are closed.

5. Compare yields and investment constraints. Compare available APYs, liquidity, underlying assets, investor access requirements, and how yields are generated and sustained.

text:
台湾国安基金是什么？

国安基金全名叫「国家金融安定基金」，2000 年依《国家金融安定基金设置及管理条例》成立。说白了，就是台股遇到非理性大跌时，政府手上的一笔「救火钱」。可以动用的上限是 5,000 亿新台币，钱的来源主要有两块：一块是拿政府持有的股票去质押借款，另一块是向邮政储金、劳保、劳退、公务员退抚这四大基金借钱。管理委员会的主任委员由行政院副院长担任，要不要进场由委员会决议，实际买什么、买多少，交给执行秘书看盘决定。所以「宣布进场」只是授权，不等于当天就买了。

进场的历史，其实就是台湾的危机年表。

- 2000 年 3 月：政党轮替，那年进场两次，第一次是唯一亏损的一次，约亏 500 亿。
- 2000 年 10 月：网络泡沫，这次赚了 226 亿。
- 2004 年：319 枪击案。
- 2008 年：金融海啸。
- 2011 年：欧债危机，美债被降评。
- 2015 年：中国股灾。
- 2020 年：疫情。
- 2022 年：美联储暴力升息。
- 2025 年 4 月：特朗普对等关税。这次投入 122.5 亿，净赚 99 亿，报酬率约 81%。
- 2026 年 11 月 6 日：第 10 次。起因是「半导体血案」，台股从高点 49,968 跌到 39,701，跌了约两成。金管会同时出了「限空令」。

前 9 次，除了第一次以外都赚钱，累计净赚约 344 亿。它的战绩好，靠的不是选股厉害，而是只在大家都吓破胆的时候才出手。

那「国安基金进场 = BTC 底部」这个指标靠谱吗？

先说他对的地方：比特币是 2009 年才诞生的，所以前 4 次（2000 年两次、2004、2008）跟 BTC 无关，这点他说得没错。2020 年 3 月和 2025 年 4 月这两次，国安基金进场的时间点也确实接近 BTC 的阶段性低点。

但「每次都是底部、胜率 100%」说过头了：

- 2022 年不是底：他自己也承认，BTC 那年真正的低点在 11 月，比进场晚了四个月。
- 2011 年也不是底：国安基金 8 月进场，BTC 到 11 月才跌到约 2 美元，后面还有一大段跌幅。
- 样本太小：BTC 时代一共才 5 次，凑不出什么统计意义。
- 跟台股的关系也没那么准：今周刊统计，过去 9 次进场后一周台股全部上涨，但拉长到三个月，胜率只剩 55%。

真正的逻辑其实很简单：国安基金和 BTC 之间不是因果，而是同一个原因。全球风险资产一起恐慌的时候，台股暴跌、国安基金出手、BTC 也被砸到低位，三件事同时发生。所以与其说国安基金「预测」了 BTC 的底，不如说它是一支恐慌温度计：政府都坐不住了，代表市场情绪已经到了极端。极端情绪往往离底部不远，但「不远」不等于「就是」，中间可能还有一段「二次探底」。

一句话：政策底可以参考，市场底要自己熬。拿它当「情绪见底的信号」可以，当「满仓的理由」就太赌了。

Polymarket's fees are now 36% higher than on Kalshi.

2 day ago Polymarket US replaced its 3.475% standard taker fee with a tiers based system.

You now need >$250k taker volume over the last 30 days achieve the same 3.475% rate.

Under that threshold, you will now pay a lot more.

Here’s what you now pay in for a buy at 50c based on tier:

- Under $10K -> 4.75%
- $10K to under $50K -> 4.25%
- $50K to under $250K -> 3.75%
- >$250K -> 3.475% 

Kalshi’s standard rate on the same trade is 3.50%.

To think that Polymarket used to have 0 fees less than a year ago, and that Kalshi was considered the expensive platform.

text:
THE NEW ERA OF FROGE IS HERE. 🐸

We are restructuring. We are rebuilding. And we're getting serious about the future of FROGE.

FROGE has been through a lot, but we believe there's still so much we can achieve together. This is the time to get organised, bring the right folks together and build a stronger foundation for what comes next.

We're opening the door to community members who are willing to contribute their skills, ideas, time and experience. We want people who are ready to get involved, take initiative and help move FROGE forward.

Here's where we need help:

1. Crypto Marketing & Growth

We need individuals with genuine experience in crypto marketing who understand how to grow a project, build narratives, reach the right audiences and create meaningful exposure. We want experienced, trustworthy individuals who can demonstrate their work and bring real value. Transparency and integrity are essential. We've had enough lessons in this space, and we're not looking to repeat them.

2. Community Voices & Communicators

We need confident English communicators who can represent FROGE and help take our message to a wider audience. This includes hosting X Spaces, Telegram voice chats, joining discussions and keeping conversations going. We want people who can communicate naturally, bring energy and represent the community well.

3. Meme Makers & Creatives

Memes are a huge part of FROGE's identity. We need creative folks who can make original 2D FROGE memes for our X posts and other community activities. We want to bring back the fun, creativity and good vibes that make meme communities special.

4. X Community & Engagement

If you're good at managing X, creating posts, starting conversations or keeping an account active, we want to hear from you. We need consistent engagement, meaningful interactions and a community that actively supports and amplifies what we're doing.

5. Builders & Developers

We need builders who are ready to create with us. Whether you're a developer, designer or someone with a good product idea, we want to hear from you. If you have ideas for products, tools, games or anything else that could give FROGE more exposure and bring something useful to the community, share them with us.

6. Chinese Community Growth

We want to strengthen our presence in the Chinese market. We're looking for Chinese-speaking community managers who can bring Chinese holders together, grow our local community, create stronger connections and help FROGE reach an even wider Chinese audience.

7. Community Participation

This isn't just about the individuals taking on specific responsibilities. We need the entire community to get involved. We need more activity on X, more conversations, more sharing and more support for one another. Every genuine contribution matters. We want the wider crypto space to see that FROGE is active, united and here to stay.

---

WHAT WE EXPECT

We're looking for genuine commitment, not titles. If you have a skill, experience or idea that can help FROGE, step forward and show us what you can bring to the table.

We want people who take initiative, work well with others, communicate openly and follow through on what they commit to. Everyone involved should understand that we're building something together, and that means taking responsibility and being accountable.

This is a community effort. We're looking for folks who believe in FROGE and are willing to contribute because they want to see it grow. No empty promises, no unnecessary politics and no personal agendas. Just people working together towards a common goal.

We'll also be taking a more organised approach to responsibilities and decision-making. Trust and influence will be built through genuine contributions, consistency and accountability.

THE FUTURE OF FROGE

We want to build products, grow our presence, strengthen our communities across different regions and give FROGE a stronger identity beyond the token itself.

We know it won't happen overnight. But with the right people, the right structure and a community willing to put in the work, there's a lot we can achieve.

If you have something to contribute, we want to hear from you. Tell us what you do, what experience you have and how you'd like to get involved.

A new chapter. A stronger community. A bigger vision.

Let's build the next era of FROGE together. 🐸

中国版 Stargate 来了？

内蒙古乌兰察布的远景星河基地，首批 120MW 不到一年建成，@SemiAnalysis_ 称其建设成本可能只有美国同类项目的 1/5。

整个园区计划 2027 年底达到 800MW IT 供电容量，接近美国 Stargate 阿比林园区规划的 820MW。

为什么选在乌兰察布？

这里有三个优势：丰富的风电资源、寒冷干燥的气候，以及相对低廉的土地和建设成本。

远景更特别的地方，是把风电、储能和数据中心整合在一起。自建两座总装机 420MW 的风电场，目标满足前两期数据中心超过 60% 的用电需求。

技术上，基地已经运行 800V 高压直流供电系统，并采用液冷与风冷共用水循环的设计，减少供电转换和制冷环节的成本。

再看中美算力用电：

IEA 估计，2024 年美国数据中心用电约 180TWh，中国约 100TWh；到 2030 年，两国预计分别比 2024 年增加约 240TWh 和 175TWh。

这意味着 AI 竞争正在从 GPU 延伸到电力基础设施。

美国的优势是芯片、资本和科技巨头，中国则有机会依靠西部能源资源、工程建设效率和能源整合降低算力成本。

未来 AI 算力拼的不只是买多少 GPU，而是谁能更快建好机房、获得稳定电力，并用更低的成本生产更多 Token。

乌兰察布这座基地，或许就是中国 AI 基建模式的一次重要试验。

iPhone 爆出严重安全漏洞：恶意 App 可能窃取钱包私钥！

iOS 被曝存在名为 worse_query 的沙盒逃逸漏洞，恶意应用可能绕过 iPhone 原本的应用隔离机制，读取其他 App 的本地文件。

如果钱包将助记词、私钥等敏感信息存储在可被访问的位置，就可能遭到窃取，导致钱包资产被盗。

风险还涉及密码管理器、登录凭证等，不局限于币安或加密钱包。

防御措施：

立即将 iPhone 更新到苹果提供的最新正式版 iOS。
删除来源不明、不可信的 App，尤其是非官方渠道安装的应用。
如果怀疑设备已经遭到入侵，在干净设备上创建新钱包，将资产转移过去。
重置重要账户密码，撤销已有登录会话。

记住：手机里只要有一个恶意 App，就可能成为其他应用数据泄露的入口。
author: oragnes
quoted_text:
A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem. This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.

Immediate Action Required:
- Delete any apps installed from untrusted sources (such as sideloaded or manually signed IPAs).
- Update iOS and all apps to the latest official versions.
- If you suspect a breach, transfer funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions.

Never install unauthorized packages, and keep your software up to date.

text:
小明深陷网赌漩涡

这一阵不但把老婆本赔了进去，还背了16万多的网贷

全因在X上刷到一条有关[反波胆]的宣传：

“用五万块本金，每个月稳赚三千块”

发帖的人说：

「穷人才赌球，聪明人都在反波胆」

下面配着一张收益截图，连续三十天，全部盈利

评论区有人问，这和赌博有什么区别？

博主回复：

“赌博是赌一件事会发生，反波胆是赌一件事不会发生，你觉得一场足球比赛踢成 4:4 的概率有多大？”

小明心想，他月薪八千二，攒了四年才堪堪攒下两万六，何时才能攒够钱与正在热恋的女友结婚？

......

于是他试着投了五百，等到第一场比赛结束，到账十五块，第二天又赢，第三天还赢

三周下来，赚了一千多块，女友问他是不是在赌球，小明义正言辞的纠正她：

「这是概率投资」

后来他把积蓄全转进去，还借了一万

一共本金三万六，押反波胆4:4

赔率1.06，赢了净赚2160块，抵得上他一周的工资

第89分钟，比分还是4:3，这一次过程虽然抓心，但心想总归是有惊无险

他已经开始在看新手机，打算赚了这笔就送给女朋友

补时第四分钟，对面一个角球，4:4

终场哨响，他四年的积蓄连同一万借款，一起清零

他崩溃地私信那个博主

他回：“你这是仓位管理有问题，不是策略有问题”

小明居然就这么信了，事后分析，也确实是自己的问题

......

第二天，他借了五万消费贷。决定这次分散下注，慢慢回本

前十一天，确实又赚了四千多

于是他想通了一个道理：本金越大，回本越快

他又借了几笔，凑到八万二，押一场反波胆3:1

第88分钟，比分从2:1变成3:1

八万二没了

这次那位博主只是轻描淡写的回他一句：“兄弟，你这心态不适合投资”

之后他开始拆东墙补西墙

连他自己都已分不清，哪笔钱是工资，哪笔钱是贷款

最后一次，他凑了六万七，押反波胆0:0，根据这两只球队的历史战绩，他觉得这完全是不可能的事情

按照赔率，只要有人进一个球，他这一次就能赚六千多，够还下个月的账单

第81分钟，球真的进了，他站起来大喊

但这时裁判示意越位，进球取消

九十分钟结束，0:0

他没哭，只是呆呆的盯着手机里那个「投注失败」，看了很久

那天晚上，他把借款账单全部加起来核算：十六万多

......

再后来，他在 X 上刷到一条新帖：

「预测市场，99%胜率的稳定理财玩法」

帖子里教人花0.98美元买一份NO合约，只要某件事没发生，到期就能拿回1美元

虽然只赚2美分，但胜率看起来高得惊人

他盯着那张收益图，突然想起第一次反波胆赚到的15块

(当然，预测市场不只有这种玩法，也能交易、对冲、套利)

可如果所谓理财，只是不断拿全部本金去押「几乎不可能发生」的事，那不管换成什么名字，输的那一次都不会因为此前赢过很多次而变小

他划走帖子，点开了和他妈的聊天框。

她刚发来一句：“钱不够的话，跟妈说。别在外面乱借”

小明眼眶瞬时被泪水充满，眼前一片模糊，打了半天字，最后只发出去三个字：

「对不起」

......

故事结束，是我于前几日偶然刷到一条宣传XX预测市场玩法=理财局的推文

联想到早些年曾在国内互联网流行过一段时间的所谓[反波胆理财局]

又想起前一段时间，巴西总统选举的那个预测市场“爆冷”例子

有感而编

Official Statement from Al-Madrasatu Ar-Rahmaniyyah (AMAR) Regarding the Recent Podcast Trailer.

As-salāmu ʿalaykum wa raḥmatullāhi wa barakātuh,
Yesterday, a short trailer was published on the AMAR YouTube channel for an upcoming podcast on takfīrism, the Khawārij, and the origins of that group. The trailer, produced by our editing team, grouped together a number of names and figures, including Sayyid Quṭb, along with contemporary charitable organisations. It also used labels such as "Islamist" and "jihadist." In doing so, it made claims that had not been fact-checked or verified, and it associated people and organisations with one another in ways that were inaccurate and unjust.
When the trailer was released, I was travelling in East Africa for a dawrah ʿilmiyyah. I approved its publication, but I did not watch it properly in full beforehand. That was my mistake, and I take full responsibility for it. I sincerely apologise for the inaccurate information it contained, and to everyone who was offended, hurt, or wrongly associated by it.
I ask that I be held to what I said in the podcast itself. That is where I spoke on this subject from my own research and understanding, and anyone can watch it and judge it for themselves.
I never want to cause harm to any Muslim, or to be a means through which any Muslim is harmed. Nor do I wish to wrong anyone by attributing to them words or positions that are not theirs. This applies even to someone I disagree with, and even to someone I believe has erred.
Going forward, in shāʾ Allāh, all refutations, documentaries and similar content from AMAR will go through a proper editing, review and verification process before publication.
I ask Allah to forgive our shortcomings, and I kindly ask you to overlook this error.
Jazākumullāhu khayran.

Ustādh Abdulrahman Hassan CEO, Al-Madrasatu Ar-Rahmaniyyah (AMAR)

Inference providers are under attack. 

AI inference is now playing a critical role and is a honey pot of data and ability to inject actions back into users devices via agents for malicious actors.

NEAR AI thwarted a series of attacks on its systems and is back to normal. NEAR Protocol, Intents and other infra wasn’t affected.

TEE architecture is part of the answer to making sure that from outside even inference provider doesn’t have an access. User should verify exactly what happens with their data and prompts.

NEAR AI code is open and inspected by many partners when deciding to leverage the stack to validate exactly what runs inside TEE and ensuring privacy.

In this case there was also a vulnerability within SGLang, open source inference engine that runs inside an enclave. Even though this had a minimum disruption it still was a very 

Going forward we are going increase security rigor of dependencies and also improve a “turnstile” to detect when anything out of normal runs inside TEE.

Proactive security against external attackers has became a must. We have been using Abliterated models and red teaming harness to continuously monitor and detect issues. We are also expanding scope and compute invested into this.

text:
I want to sharpen my own thinking around why I think ETH has the potential to become the best SoV in the world.

Would love to hear arguments for/against any of my conclusions!

First things first - at it's current stage, I cannot confidently call ETH the best SoV, yet.

Why?
- AI and post-quantum threats are real
- Price action in the past 5 years was worse than other SoVs

BUT, imho it has the best chances to become the leading SoV.

The AI and PQ threat is being worked on full steam - the Ethereum community agrees that this has top priority. 

Once Ethereum has successfully transitioned to post-quantum cryptography, I currently don't see any other asset with better properties.

This transition could quickly grow the assets adoption (esp. if cryptography of banks and tradfi start to fail).

When I compare ETH against other SoV contenders, I'm coming to the following conclusions:

ETH vs real estate 
- reals estate isn't transportable (I cannot just bring it with me when I travel/move)
- real estate markets are more inefficient 
- local factors might heavily influence the value appreciation/depreciation of my property
- upkeep costs are necessary (but generally lower than the generated rental income) and are dependent on availability of workers

ETH vs Fiat
- higher inflation (varies by country, but basically all have them)
- depending on the currency, there might be issues with accessibility
- one would need to pick a basket of currencies in order to diversify geopolitical risk properly 
- dependent on decisions from central banks

ETH vs Gold
- gold is hard to verify, hard to break down into smaller amounts, and harder to trade in general
- you cannot easily transfer gold without a physical handover
- won't be useful to AI agents

ETH vs BTC
- ETH is programmable, which allows you to use your ETH natively on the underlying blockchain (Ethereum) whereas swapping/borrowing/lending BTC introduces additional trust assumptions (because Bitcoin chain is a ledger for token transfers and you'd have to go through centralized exchanges or other 3rd parties for more expressivity)
- Bitcoin is also working on PQ solutions (BIP-360 & BIP-361), but the migration path appears less defined compared to Ethereums more explicit and time-bound roadmap
- Bitcoin's fixed supply and declining PoW block rewards create an unresolved long-term security-budget question

Other pro ETH points
- it's programmable 
- it's green
- it has the coolest brand (the logo is just amazing and goes with anything)
- it is productive (i.e. it can generate a native staking yield)

As mentioned, would love to discuss this publicly to sharpen my own thinking. 

Also: never put all your eggs in the same basket. Even if one asset has the best "properties", it doesn't mean that the chance for success is 100% - there are always risks involved.

Lately, I've been seeing a lot of viral posts about who crypto founders used to hang out with back in the day.

Well, I wasn't hanging out with people like @alexandr_wang or @chameleon_jeff, but I did have the opportunity to have dinner with @RonPaul and even take a few pictures with him.

As one of the very few Koreans who genuinely follow the Austrian School of Economics, I actually translated one of Ron Paul's books into Korean(and one Rothbard's) and served as the president of my university's Students for Ron Paul chapter.

After returning to Korea, I founded a libertarian student organization, where we taught English to North Korean defectors and ran initiatives to expose the realities of the North Korean regime.

Ultimately, it was these beliefs that led me into crypto in the first place.

Of course, I've gotten older, and now that I'm running a company, I've come to embrace crypto from a much broader perspective.

But every now and then, something happens in this industry that reminds me of why I got into crypto in the first place. And lately, I've been feeling that old cypherpunk identity resurfacing more and more.

Hopefully, when I find some time, I'll share more about how I personally view the crypto industry, where I think it's heading, and the principles that continue to shape my thinking.

Good old days coming back to crypto

text:
Our Chief AI Scientist @zehuac was in Rome to present six FLock papers in the @CIKM 2026 Full Research Track.

Together, they map out what we need to make private AI training affordable, safe, and reliable at scale.

1. Cheaper training

Most training updates the whole model at once, even though the parts affect each other. Gradient Interaction Graph Optimization updates them in a smarter order and reaches the same quality in about a third fewer steps.

2. Safer model merging

Combining two models can work well or ruin both, and normally you only find out after running expensive tests. Curvature Graph Mergeability predicts the outcome in advance from a quick scan of each model.

3. Robustness to bad examples

Showing misleading examples in a prompt can throw off the whole answer. In-Context Learning as Belief Propagation lets the model recognise the odd one out and trust it less, improving accuracy by about 7 points.

4. Keep structured outputs consistent

When AI fills in a form, it often decides each field separately, so a junior job title can end up next to a senior salary. Bethe Consensus Decoding checks the fields against each other and returns a consistent answer, with no retraining.

5. Quantify uncertainty

A model should be able to say “it’s one of these three” when it isn’t sure. Cavity-Calibrated Prediction Sets give guaranteed-reliable shortlists that are up to 58% tighter, so they stay useful.

6. Anonymise training text

Real-world text is full of names and personal information that regulations keep off-limits. Graph-Driven Context-Preserving Anonymization removes 99.8% of it while keeping the text just as useful for training.

Private AI becomes more critical as data becomes every organisation’s edge, and FLock is building at that frontier.

text:
如果有项目方基于这个机制做一个 Hyperliquid 版的 v4，想象空间会很大。

Elysium 即将支持在 EVM 内实时读取 Hypercore 的完整订单簿，价格约每 70ms 更新一次。这样一来，智能合约可以直接感知订单簿深度、价差与流动性变化，并在 Hypercore 上完成交易。

这相当于给链上应用提供了一套可编程的订单簿接口。

开发者可以围绕它设计类似 Uniswap v4 Hooks 的模块，例如：

根据订单簿深度动态调整报价和手续费
在 AMM 与 Hypercore 之间自动路由订单
构建链上限价单、止损单和 TWAP 策略
根据波动率自动管理 LP 头寸
将做市、套利和流动性管理封装成可组合策略

过去，许多高级交易策略依赖链下机器人读取行情，再提交交易。现在，合约本身就能读取高速订单簿并触发执行，策略可以直接在链上组合。

如果项目方能进一步抽象出标准化的 Hooks、共享流动性层和开发者框架，一个围绕 Hypercore 订单簿生长的 DeFi 应用层可能会出现。

这类项目值得关注。

TLDR of hyperliquid precompiles:

EVM chains on HL (ie HyperEVM & Elysium) have precompiles (basically built in blockchain functions) that allow them to query prices of hypercore assets

For example rn on HyperEVM, you can make a simple RPC call to the chain to get the mark price of $HYPE

Elysium doesn't have this ability rn but will be able to in 4 weeks. The diff b/w elysium and hyperEVM is that elysium's prices will update every 70ms (hyperEVM is every 1s)

And elysium will be able to query entire orderbook, while hyperEVM can only do bid/ask/mark

A blockchain being able to query the full depth of a separate orderbook in real time is p cool. Maybe some volatility based univ4 hooks could use such information

text:
Amazon just replaced Claude in one of the world's biggest internal ticketing systems. With a 2B model.

Every ticket used to go to Claude Sonnet to get labeled. Two Amazon engineers swapped it for Strands Decider, a small open model that only picks from options:

•⁠  ⁠Cost per million tickets: $22,200 → about $500
•⁠  ⁠Time per call: 4.2 seconds → 0.9 seconds
•⁠  ⁠Tokens per ticket: 6,724 → 2,010
•⁠  ⁠Accuracy: it beat Sonnet on their own tickets

Their rule: if the job is "pick one of these labels," you don't need a frontier model.

Try it on your own computer:
1.⁠ ⁠pip install strands-decider
2.⁠ ⁠strands-decider ask StrandsAgents/strands-decider-2B-qwen3.5-v1-2610 --state "Help! My payouts have been failing for 3 days!" --choice "Which team should handle this?=billing,sales,retail"

It answers "billing" with a confidence score.

This is an important photo.

Not because wonderful people made a pic with a visionary technologist. But the feminist & Mumbai-based organisation Point Of View got was part of Cypherpunk Congress storytelling and managed to connect with people like Vitalik Buterin.

I found out about @povmumbai existence around March 2026. During scouting in Mumbai. Recommended by Sam who was helping us to match with human rights organisations around. I visited POV’s office. Talked with their team. Got a zine that I carry during my travels.

Point Of View defends those who are targeted by algorithms, hate, and manipulation. Also, they educate, collaborate, organise Global South alliances, and promote healthy digital rights practices. Again, being present in the world from Mozilla Festival in Barcelona to Global Gathering in Estoril.

Marginalised people are subjects to constant harm in India. Guess what’s important isn’t to further marginalise them, but give them opportunities, options, possibilities. Like the Reimagining social media from the margins talk that Riddhima from POV was supposed to make at Cypherpunk Congress (was cancelled due to family issues). But the challenge stays actual: https://t.co/gVcGHNYutt

This photo resembles our desire to connect humans in need with techno-politics. So the latter will serve the excluded, marginalised, and often ignored. Personally, I want to do it not through my words and actions, but have folks like POV talk on their behalf. Wave storytelling without any up-bottom filter.

On a separate note, super proud that we got many “paper” formats at Cypherpunk Congress: Sister Library that helps marginalised girls find new opportunities in life, Fluxus Chapel that storytellers politics via a wide range of zines, Nirmik cultural centre with Navayana published challenging caste conditions in 2026.

支撑这套体系走向成熟的，是 Gate 的全球合规版图：

your HDMI cable can leak what’s on your screen

watch the laptop on the left. it reconstructs the video playing on the monitor beside it from radio signals leaking out of the HDMI connection

this is TempestSDR. an antenna picks up the leakage, a HackRF radio captures it, and software turns it back into an image

researchers took this further with Deep-TEMPEST, using AI to make recovered images and text easier to read. this clip shows the original technique

quality depends on shielding, distance and interference. the picture is imperfect, but recognizable content still gets through

a wired connection can still leave a wireless trace

text:
Norway now has more than 2,000 underwater AI laser robots shooting lice off its salmon

they're made by a company called Stingray, and they already guard more than 50 million salmon and trout 24/7

the reason is sea lice, tiny parasites that latch onto salmon and feed on them

as few as 11 can kill a small fish, and one pen can hold 150,000 salmon

the usual fix is pumping the fish out and blasting them with warm water or water jets to knock the lice off

but the handling is so rough that Norway's fish health report ranks it the top cause of death in full-grown farmed salmon

so instead, Stingray puts a robot inside the pen that hunts lice one at a time, all day:

> two cameras watch every salmon that swims past

> AI checks two frames to make sure it's really a louse

> then a green laser fires from up to 2 meters away

> the salmon's scales reflect the beam, so the fish swims off fine and the louse is dead

we now live in a world where AI lasers do pest control on your dinner lmao

text:
Privacy tech sounds great until it takes forever to compute.

That has been one of the biggest problems with FHE.

@primus_labs is attacking that bottleneck with AutoHoG.

In Primus’ benchmark, a confidential transfer using fully encrypted 64-bit balances takes around 90ms.

With 8 RTX 5090 GPUs, the FHE engine reaches 210+ confidential transfer computations per second.

Important distinction:

that’s FHE compute throughput, not blockchain TPS.

But that’s exactly why the numbers are interesting.

If encrypted balances, transfers and financial logic are going to work onchain at scale, privacy can’t add an unusable amount of latency.

The cryptography has to become infrastructure, not just research.

And making encrypted computation practical is a big part of getting there.

TEE architecture is part of the answer to making sure that from outside even inference provider doesn’t have an access. User should verify exactly what happens with their data and prompts.

In this case there was also a vulnerability within SGLang, open source inference engine that runs inside an enclave. Even though this had a minimum disruption it still was a very 

Going forward we are going increase security rigor of dependencies and also improve a “turnstile” to detect when anything out of normal runs inside TEE.

- Update iOS and all apps to the latest official versions.
- If you suspect a breach, transfer funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions.

Never install unauthorized packages, and keep your software up to date.

text:
Crypto Is Growing Up. Bitget CEO Gracy Chen Says Its Security Model Needs to Grow Up Too.

For years, cryptocurrency exchanges have operated as all-in-one platforms, allowing users to store assets, execute trades, and access financial products in one place. That convenience helped make crypto more accessible, but it also created a security model that is becoming increasingly difficult to defend.
In this episode of Drops, I sit down with @Bitget CEO, @GracyBitget, to discuss the security challenges facing crypto exchanges, the lessons from Bitget's recent $388 million breach, and why she believes separating custody from trading could represent an important step forward for the industry.

A $388 Million Wake-Up Call

On September 24, Bitget experienced a major security breach involving unauthorized transfers of approximately $388 million from its hot and warm wallets. The initial suspicious transfers began around 2:30 a.m. in Gracy’s time zone, followed by larger withdrawals shortly afterward. She happened to wake up before 4 a.m., checked her phone, and discovered what was unfolding.
Her immediate priorities were understanding the extent of the losses, identifying the vulnerability, and determining whether the threat had been contained. Within hours, she was addressing the community publicly, even as the investigation continued. The experience was emotionally demanding, and Gracy admits there were moments when her hands shook, despite her efforts to remain composed.

"I'm a human being. I'm not an AI," she said.

The breach originated through third-party vulnerabilities rather than compromised private keys, and Bitget's cold wallets remained secure. The company subsequently patched vulnerabilities, strengthened withdrawal procedures, and used its existing protection fund to cover the losses, leaving customer balances unaffected.
But beyond the immediate response, Gracy came away with a more fundamental realization: Improving security protocols alone would not solve the underlying problem.

Why the Traditional Exchange Model Is Reaching Its Limits

To understand Gracy's argument, it helps to understand how centralized cryptocurrency exchanges operate. Unlike conventional financial markets, where different institutions handle trading, custody, and clearing, crypto exchanges have often combined these functions. Gracy describes this structure as "one giant monster."

The advantage is a seamless experience where users can deposit funds, purchase assets, move between products, and execute trades, but the problem is that concentrating so many responsibilities within one organization also concentrates risk. As exchanges expand their offerings, they create more systems, dependencies, and potential vulnerabilities to protect from, while attackers only need to exploit one weakness to cause substantial damage.

Gracy argues that this creates an inherently uneven contest between security teams and hackers, especially as attacks become increasingly sophisticated. Her conclusion is that the industry needs to reconsider its architecture rather than simply keep adding protective measures to the same underlying model.

The Open Custody Network

Gracy's proposed solution is the Bitget Open Custody Network, which she summarizes in one sentence as "Assets in bank, trading on Bitget." Essentially, customers would no longer need to keep all their assets directly with the exchange to trade on its platform. Instead, custody would move to specialized providers, including established banks, digital banks, and dedicated cryptocurrency custody firms. Bitget would continue facilitating trading, while these separate institutions would be responsible for safeguarding customer assets.

However, separating custody from trading introduces its own considerations. Customers must understand the custodian's regulatory status, financial strength, security record, jurisdiction, and the time or cost involved in accessing funds. The model is intended to distribute responsibilities, thus reducing risk.

Security Comes With a Trade-Off

Crypto users have become accustomed to moving funds almost instantly, and introducing independent custodians could make certain processes slower or more complicated. This may be acceptable for institutional investors who often prioritize asset protection over convenience, but retail customers may see things differently.

Gracy acknowledges this. The initial rollout primarily targets institutional clients and high-net-worth users, who are more likely to value independent custody arrangements. Over time, Bitget hopes to simplify the process for smaller customers, potentially reducing the need to select and manage custodians individually. Importantly, participation is not intended to be mandatory. Customers would retain the option of keeping assets with Bitget or adopting the external custody model.

This raises a broader question for the industry. Can exchanges offer substantially stronger protection without sacrificing the simplicity that attracted users in the first place? Gracy believes the answer will depend on how effectively exchanges and custody providers develop the infrastructure together.

From Crypto's Original Ideals to Institutional Adoption

The discussion eventually moves beyond security to examine how cryptocurrency itself is evolving. Bitcoin emerged from a philosophy of decentralization, peer-to-peer transactions, and individual control over financial assets. Yet the industry now includes traditional financial institutions, investment products, and regulated intermediaries. Gracy doesn't necessarily see this as a contradiction.

She distinguishes decentralized blockchain networks from the institutions that provide access to assets operating on those networks. Bitcoin can remain decentralized even as banks, asset managers, and regulated exchanges participate in its broader ecosystem.
She points to the growing digital asset activities of institutions such as JPMorgan, BlackRock, and Fidelity as evidence of this transition. For Gracy, the industry is moving beyond its experimental years toward a stage where security, sustainable business models, and integration with traditional finance matter.

What Success Would Look Like

Gracy has a specific vision for measuring the Open Custody Network's success over the next three years. She wants at least half of Bitget's total assets under management to be held by independent custodians, with no custody-related security breaches and minimal disruption to the customer experience. She also hopes other centralized exchanges will adopt similar approaches.

Rather than positioning the network primarily as a new revenue opportunity, she describes it as an effort to encourage broader changes in how the industry manages security.
As crypto becomes part of a larger financial system, the industry must become more deliberate about who holds customer assets, how those assets are protected, and what risks users accept in exchange for convenience.

大模型数据飞轮效应已然成型，Anthropic 已成为全球领域唯一真大龙。

记得当年 ChatGPT 刚出来的时候，课代表立正说过数据飞轮会使得 OpenAI 训练的模型越来越好，而越好的模型会带来更多的用户，更多的用户所带来的数据又会让 OpenAI 训练出更好的模型。

但是当年可能谁都没有想到，当 AI 会写代码之后，还能进一步让数据飞轮用于提升训练效率。从这几次 Anthropic 模型能力的进步来看，Anthropic 是将其他竞争对手都远远甩在了身后。

我不在 Anthropic 内部，所以也不知道他们内部的模型到底有多强。但从 Opus 5.5 在订阅套餐中的表现看，虽然从发布至今体感上经历过一些降智，也有第三方统计过确实存在一些降智，不过总体来说还是在一条非常高的水平线上，并且时不时可以给人惊喜——这种降智应该就是推理效率提升的副产物。而推理效率的提升，又肯定来自于他们的领先模型能力。

这样看，数据飞轮带来的领先模型能力，还能够进一步提升订阅套餐的补贴额度。这些多出来的补贴额度，又能从竞争对手手上抢到更多的用户，贡献更多的长尾场景的数据。

真理可能会迟到，但它一定不会缺席。

当然，不知道 Anthropic 会不会出现之前 OpenAI 那样 dramatic 的人事动荡。如果没有的话，感觉其他的竞争对手都会很难。

text:
A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem. This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.

Immediate Action Required:
- Delete any apps installed from untrusted sources (such as sideloaded or manually signed IPAs).
- Update iOS and all apps to the latest official versions.
- If you suspect a breach, transfer funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions.

Never install unauthorized packages, and keep your software up to date.

text:
硅谷已经准备让 AI 替你花钱了，但消费者似乎连让 AI 替自己做事都还没想好。

彭博最近报道了一个有意思的现象：科技公司正在疯狂推进 AI Agent，普通消费者的实际采用速度却没有跟上。

Meta 的 Muse、OpenAI 的 Dots，以及 Instinct 等公司的产品，已经可以帮人寻找折扣、预订旅行、整理邮箱。但问题在于，消费者既不够信任这些智能体，也没有感受到足够大的实际价值。

更尴尬的是，连银行和电商平台都开始阻止部分 AI Agent 访问自己的网站。

这就形成了一个很荒诞的局面：AI 公司拼命训练模型如何使用互联网，互联网却开始想办法不让它们使用。

我觉得这里面有一个被行业低估的问题：从 Chatbot 到 Agent，改变的不只是 AI 的能力，而是人类需要交出去的权力。

让 AI 回答问题，答错了可以重新问；让 AI 订机票、操作银行账户、处理私人邮件，犯错的代价就完全不同了。

而且，信任还只是问题的一半。假如一个 Agent 需要用户反复授权、检查结果、纠正错误，那它节省的时间可能还不够支付人类监督它的成本。

所以 Agent 面临的其实是双重困境：能力不够可靠时，人们不敢放权；能力足够可靠时，它还必须证明自己比人亲自操作更省事。

过去几年，AI 公司一直在证明机器能做什么。接下来，它们得证明有什么事情值得人类不再亲自做。

技术上的自主性可以靠算力和模型训练获得，但商业上的自主权，最终只能由用户和平台授予。

软银集团今天公布中期业绩，4—9 月累计最终亏损 7680 亿日元。按 CNBC 和《金融时报》的第二季度口径，单季意外净亏损约 70 亿美元。彭博指出，这是软银近两年来首次出现季度净亏损。

问题不只是亏了多少钱，而是市场正在重新审视软银最核心的投资逻辑。

过去两年，孙正义几乎把软银的未来押在 AI 上。从 OpenAI 到 Arm，再到围绕 AI 基础设施的巨额资本投入，他试图让软银从一家科技投资集团，变成 AI 时代最重要的资本枢纽之一。

但如今，AI 开支不断膨胀，市场对需求能否消化这些投入的担忧开始加剧，软银主要持股的估值也随之承压。

这里有一个颇为讽刺的变化：

过去，软银最大的风险是错过 AI；现在，它最大的风险之一，恰恰是太相信 AI。

孙正义的投资哲学一直建立在一个前提上，只要押中了足够大的技术趋势，短期价格波动就不重要。

但 AI 正在让这个逻辑面临新的考验。模型能力的进步可以很快，资本回报却未必能同步兑现。基础设施需要持续投入，商业化需要时间，而资本市场已经开始要求科技公司证明，天文数字般的 AI 投资究竟能产生多少真实利润。

更麻烦的是，软银不仅要承受自身投资的资金压力，还要承受整个 AI 产业估值波动带来的连锁反应。

当整个市场都相信 AI 时，孙正义是最有远见的投资人；当市场开始怀疑 AI 的回报时，软银就成了这场豪赌最显眼的风险敞口。

这份财报当然还不能证明孙正义押错了方向。但它提醒市场一件事：看对未来，和在未来到来之前撑过所有波动，是两种完全不同的能力。

text:
Great guide. Step 11 is the one that gave me PTSD: state machines, and reconciling them against live trade/order streams. Everyone builds this from scratch, and it's a huge pain in the ass (took me days of debugging to iron out all the kinks in mine).

We're going to ship a fairly opinionated Rust framework that gets you 80% of the way there, so you can focus on the strategy instead of the boilerplate.

The software stack

- Streaming market data. Keeping a live, trusted picture of the market is a project on its own. Websocket reconnect logic. Busy polling and CPU pinning etc.
- Exchange integrations. SDKs, APIs, order entry, error handling. All before you write a line of trading logic.
- The event loop and state machine. Your view of the market, your orders and your fills has to stay consistent, including what's still in flight.
- Logging and replay. When something breaks you need to replay it exactly, or it's endless guesswork.
- Telemetry, trade logs and post-trade reconciliation. If you can't measure it and check it after the fact, you can't improve it. What DB to use etc (e.g. Postgres vs QuestDB vs Clickhouse)? How to measure latency, how to measure markouts etc.
- Deployment and machine setup. Repeatable deploys, the right specs, and the OS and network tuning that stops latency jumping around (e.g. TCP_NODELAY).

All of that should be a template you start from, not something you rebuild every time.

Infra and colocation (coming later)

In traditional HFT, market data arrives over multicast, orders go through a gateway, and everyone in the facility sits on equal-length fiber so access is fair. In crypto, people still have to figure out cloud zones and stitch together their own last mile.

We want to make bare-metal colocation and fair market data delivery a uniform service. Same access, same data, for a low flat fee, so you're on equal footing from day one. More details coming soon.

Then the only differentiator is the idea.

That's the goal: an idea meritocracy. Your edge should be the quality of your idea, while we do the heavy lifting to get you there.

It's also why I think DEXs win. They'll be the most user-centric and the most accessible to a wider audience. Make it easy to get started, get more retail into these markets, and the extra competition is good for pricing and for everyone trading.

这条消息值得结合昨天的风波来看。

路透社此前独家报道，Anthropic 曾向银行发送一份 IPO 材料，显示计划发行约 8.67 亿股，定价区间为每股 70 至 80 美元，按上限计算，发行总规模可能达到 693 亿美元（包含老股出售）。

现在看来，撤回的是那份定价材料，而不是整个 IPO 计划。路演依然按计划推进。

更值得关注的是时机。

过去一周，AI 股票大幅波动，市场对天价资本开支、数据中心建设和 AI 公司估值的疑虑不断加深。此前市场一度讨论 Anthropic 高达 2 万亿美元的估值，而近期部分投资者已经开始要求更低的发行价格。

过去几年，顶级 AI 公司可以在私人市场不断刷新估值，投资人争夺的是进入股东名单的资格。但到了公开市场，问题开始反过来：你认为自己值多少钱是一回事，市场愿意以什么价格接盘，是另一回事。

Anthropic 的 IPO，正在从硅谷内部的估值游戏，变成整个资本市场对 AI 商业模式的一次公开定价。

What an incredible @EFDevcon 8! Huge thanks to @OrnellaWeb3, @denverjude, @satyaki44, and the entire Devcon organizing team for putting together such an exceptionally well-organized, thoughtfully curated, and memorable gathering for the global @Ethereum community.

It was wonderful to see participation from across the globe in developer initiatives organized by @libp2p team, representing almost every continent (Antarctica being the obvious exception!). The diversity of perspectives, experiences, and technical expertise made this an especially enriching gathering.

A few highlights from the four days:

🌍 Global ecosystem and institutional engagement
Great meetings and conversations with institutions, ecosystem leaders, researchers, founders, and developers from across the world.
Meaningful discussions around scaling institutional adoption of @Ethereum and strengthening its underlying infrastructure.

We also formalized the EF Consensus Clients <> libp2p coordination cell in reference to security initiatives: https://t.co/VfuUs0R1V9 and https://t.co/wpsXlIkQhf

Special thanks to @denverjude, @rashmivabbigeri   and @satyaki44, for organizing a fantastic series of meetings and conversations focused on scaling institutional adoption of Ethereum.

We also wish to thank @devanshmehta and friends from @seer_pm for their positive feedback and pointers on scaling our community initiatives aligned with the core principles of @ethereum. 

🔬 Deep-tech innovation
- Strong participation and discussions around AI agents and agentic infrastructure.
- Quantum-resistant cryptography and security.
- Zero-knowledge proofs and privacy-preserving technologies.
- Formal verification and protocol correctness.
- Ethereum consensus clients and decentralized networking infrastructure.

🛠️ libp2p and IPFS ecosystem highlights
- 600+ developers participated and engaged in a variety of @libp2p initiatives organized over 4 days.
- 50+ hours of talks, technical sessions, and workshops recorded over four days.
- One entirely new libp2p implementation initiated: leanp2p, bringing libp2p to Lean 4: https://t.co/3QSUxJoTgX 
- 7+ developer tooling initiatives improved and demonstrated.
- 15+ @libp2p and @ipfs startup projects shared with funding opportunities.
- 10+ hours of on-stage talks, technical sessions, and workshops led by libp2p core contributors.
- 5 new projects bootstrapped from ground 0 :)

Exciting conversations around protocol resilience, interoperability, developer experience, and the future of decentralized networking.

Beyond the numbers, what stood out most was the quality of technical discussions, the openness to collaboration, and the incredible amount of learning, feedback, and constructive pointers we received from the community.

There is so much to take back, follow up on, and build together. Several conversations have already opened up promising opportunities for new collaborations, ecosystem development, and support for builders.

A special thank you to everyone who attended the Resilient Networking Hub, contributed sessions, shared their work, participated in workshops, and helped make these conversations happen.

And at the rate we are accumulating discussions, ideas, action items, and follow-ups, we believe that by the time we actually wrap up everything from @EFDevcon 8, it might well be October 11, 2027! :)

Until then, let's keep building open, resilient, secure, and decentralized infrastructure together.

Inference providers are under attack. 

AI inference is now playing a critical role and is a honey pot of data and ability to inject actions back into users devices via agents for malicious actors.

NEAR AI thwarted a series of attacks on its systems and is back to normal. NEAR Protocol, Intents and other infra wasn’t affected.

TEE architecture is part of the answer to making sure that from outside even inference provider doesn’t have an access. User should verify exactly what happens with their data and prompts.

NEAR AI code is open and inspected by many partners when deciding to leverage the stack to validate exactly what runs inside TEE and ensuring privacy.

In this case there was also a vulnerability within SGLang, open source inference engine that runs inside an enclave. Even though this had a minimum disruption it still was a very 

Going forward we are going increase security rigor of dependencies and also improve a “turnstile” to detect when anything out of normal runs inside TEE.

Proactive security against external attackers has became a must. We have been using Abliterated models and red teaming harness to continuously monitor and detect issues. We are also expanding scope and compute invested into this.

text:
By solving old problems, you create new ones. Or why @avon_xyz avoided @aave's stable-rate failures… and introduced a different set of problems instead.

Avon never locked rates. Everything stays floating and isolated, so no semi-fixed rates, no public rebalance function, and no protocol silently losing money when variable rates rise above fixed rates.

In exchange…

- Interest curves are locked forever after deployment. Lenders get certainty… but you also can’t fix a bad or outdated strategy when the market moves.

- Strategies must update their tick levels on the order book whenever utilization changes. The architecture was oriented toward MegaETH; on ETH, it's costly.

- Audits (from @zellic_io, @PashovAuditGrp, @cantinasecurity, @ValkyriSecurity) showed that flash loans could force borrowers into worse rates on limit orders, plus matching bugs, dust-order DoS, MEV, and front-running on market orders. Most high/medium stuff was fixed, but residual risks remain (e.g., unprotected market orders, non-upgradeable contracts, no order expiration).

- Because strategies are isolated, a single large borrow is often split across multiple strategies. Each piece has its own utilization path, rate, and liquidation logic. Lenders stay safe, but borrowers get partial liquidations and messier positions.

⚠️iOS security alert: Take action now‼️

A newly disclosed iOS vulnerability called worse_query (a sandbox escape PoC) affects versions including iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2. 

It can allow malicious apps (especially sideloaded or manually signed IPAs) to read local files belonging to other apps.

This puts seed phrases, private keys, login credentials, and other sensitive data at risk across wallets and apps. It is an iOS-level issue, not specific to any single platform or exchange.

Immediate steps:

1) Delete any apps installed from untrusted sources (sideloaded IPAs, Telegram links, “modified” wallets, or unofficial packages).

2) Update iOS and all apps to the latest official versions as soon as they are available.

3) If you suspect compromise (or recently installed anything suspicious):

◦Move funds to a new wallet created on a clean device.
◦Reset all active login sessions and change passwords.
◦Do not import the old seed into the new wallet.

Best practice:

 Keep software updated and avoid storing seeds or private keys in notes, screenshots, or unencrypted app storage.

Stay safe 🫡

text:
This is painfully relatable 😂

Had to translate it for my English-speaking friends.

----

Your name is Hugo. You're 26. You quit your full-time job at Capgemini to launch your B2B SaaS. An “AI-powered HR performance management platform.”

In reality, it's an Excel spreadsheet with Claude. But you don't describe it that way.

You've been building it for 14 months. You still don't have a single customer. Which is normal, because the product is “not quite ready yet.”

Your Notion roadmap has 87 features. You spent three weeks working on dark mode. Nobody asked for it, but “users love that stuff.” (You don't have any users.)

You have a CTO co-founder, Maxence, whom you met at a Startup Weekend. He owns 12% of the company and rebuilds the entire architecture every two months because “the current setup won't scale.”

The scale in question? You, Maxence, and one test customer (your dad).

You have an office at Station F, a logo that's been redesigned four times by a €6,000 agency, and a 32-slide pitch deck claiming a $14 billion TAM.

You've had 23 meetings with VCs. Every single one thinks it's “super interesting” and wants to “stay in touch once you've got some traction.”

You still don't really know what traction means, but you've read The Lean Startup twice. You even highlighted “Fail fast.”

So far, you've only managed the “fail” part.

Every Tuesday, you post on LinkedIn.

“Day 412 of our entrepreneurial journey. Today, I learned that the real product is the team.”

63 likes.

58 of them come from other Station F founders who like your posts so you'll like theirs back.

It's called an “ecosystem.”

Your unemployment benefits run out in March. You call that your “runway.”

Your girlfriend, Clémence, calls it “How are we going to pay the rent in four months?”

You tell her that Notion almost went bankrupt too.

She doesn't know what Notion is.

But she knows exactly how much rent she's going to have to cover on her own. Again.

Ta roadmap Notion compte 87 features. Tu as passé 3 semaines sur le mode sombre. Personne ne te l’a demandé, mais « les utilisateurs adorent ça ». (Tu n’as pas d’utilisateurs).

Tu as un associé CTO, Maxence, rencontré lors d’un Startup Weekend. Il a 12 % des parts et refait l’architecture tous les deux mois, parce que « là, on ne tiendra pas la charge ». La charge, c’est toi, maxence et un client test (ton père).

Tu as un bureau à Station F, un logo refait 4 fois par une agence à 6 000 € et un pitch deck de 32 slides avec un TAM à 14 milliards.

Tu as fait 23 rendez-vous avec des fonds. Ils trouvent tous ça « super intéressant » et veulent « garder le contact quand vous aurez de la traction ».

Tu ne sais pas encore ce qu’est la traction, mais tu as lu « The Lean Startup » deux fois. Et tu as surligné « Fail fast ». Pour l'instant c'est juste "fail".

Tous les mardis, tu publies sur LinkedIn. « Jour 412 de notre aventure entrepreneuriale. Aujourd’hui, j’ai appris que le vrai produit, c’est l’équipe. » 63 likes. 58 viennent d’autres fondateurs de Station F, qui likent pour que tu likes en retour. C’est un "écosystème".

Ton chômage se termine en mars. Tu appelles ça ton « runway ».  Ta copine, Clémence, appelle ça « dans quatre mois, on paie comment le loyer ? ».  Tu lui réponds que Notion aussi a failli mourir. Had a solid week of trades, and now I’m stuck with the classic DeFi problem: too many places to park capital, too few that actually make sense long-term.

What I (and honestly most DeFi users) really want is pretty simple:

- Real-world lending exposure aka no ponzinomics, no “APY” that’s just token emissions in a trench coat
- Less button-clicking and mental gymnastic
- Actual control over how much risk I’m taking

So I pinged @phtevenstrong, and not long after I moved some of my own funds into @mezzanine_fi’s Hastra Optimizer vault.

This is the direction I think DeFi is inevitably moving: clean UX + risk that’s structured, not guessed.

Simply put, Mezzanine's vault deploys capital via @HastraFi’s home-equity and auto-lending assets, while the DeFi strategy side runs in the background.

You pick your lane:

text:
I think we're entering a civilizational rupture that nobody can predict. Not me, not the labs, not governments.

I don't know how much people realize how fast we're moving.

Look at what Anthropic's new model did during testing.

It solved two open problems in theoretical physics, both on black holes. One of the calculations was laid out in 2003 and nobody had ever finished it, because it was too laborious.

It formalized the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours, with a thousand agents that organized themselves. The first attempt took 11 days.

It wrote an operating system that boots on a laptop, starting from an empty folder, in 8 days.

It designed three electronic devices, boards, enclosures and software included. All three worked without a single electrical modification.

It found a new method to predict the structure of viral capsids, the shells used to deliver gene therapies.

And on robot control, it more than doubled the previous version's score.

All of that in a single announcement, on a Monday.

I think discoveries are going to stack up so fast that they'll produce an abundance we've never known: energy, health, materials, food. And with it a phase of immense joy, the joy of a civilization realizing that scarcity was never a law of nature.

Except that joy is going to land in a world order that's cracking everywhere, and that was designed by Malthusians. People convinced that resources are finite, that there are too many of us, and that the job of an enlightened elite is to manage scarcity on everyone else's behalf.

To me, Bill Gates is the most famous face of that worldview: a man nobody elected, who has weighed on the planet's health, agriculture and climate policies for twenty years. The degrowth crowd is the militant version. They don't even want to manage scarcity anymore, they want to organize it.

Abundance is the worst possible news for that worldview. If energy becomes nearly free and diseases fall one after another, nobody needs anyone to ration anything for them.

So I don't think they'll fight it. I think they'll try to capture it.

In the name of safety, climate or public health, we'll be told this power is too dangerous to be left in everyone's hands. We already saw the movie during Covid: the permission slips, the passes, the QR code to go get a coffee. Now imagine the same logic with an AI that can see everything, trace everything and decide everything in real time. Orwell never imagined a tool like that.

The technology is winning on its own. The question of the next ten years is who abundance will belong to.

We are living through the greatest civilizational revolution in human history. It's happening right now, and most people are looking the other way.

text:
月之暗面（Kimi）已经在国内成功租到英伟达顶级 B300 芯片。

彭博找到两份提交给监管数据库的融资合同，显示 32 台搭载 B300 的美超微服务器位于甘肃庆阳，总估值 4.32 亿元。B300 属于英伟达 Blackwell Ultra 系列，是美国严格限制对华出口的顶级 AI 芯片。32 台服务器平均估值 1350 万元，比美国同类产品的市场价格高出约 350%。

合同签署于今年 8 月。服务器由凌美芯（北京）科技持有，该公司向北京中关村银行贷款 2 亿元，抵押物除了服务器，还有一份与月之暗面签订的算力服务合同，涉及 3.456 亿元预期收入。

凌美芯早年从事无人机、计算机视觉等业务。它从北京春菊科技一家新成立的子公司购买了这批服务器，而北京春菊科技此前主要经营茅台等酒类电商，后来才拓展 AI 业务。文件没有交代这些受美国出口管制的服务器最初从哪里采购。

彭博在 11 月 3 日向月之暗面、凌美芯及银行求证后，数据库中的相关文件不再出现月之暗面的名字。

月之暗面同时否认参与或授权相关融资和担保安排，称目前与凌美芯没有业务关系，也不知晓这些安排。英伟达和美超微则表示，涉及采购的企业并非其客户。

quoted_text:
月之暗面（Kimi）正在欧洲寻找英伟达 Blackwell 算力。知情人士透露，双方讨论过租用至少 8000 张 Blackwell GPU 的方案，主要用于模型推理，也考虑过训练。

想租到这些芯片，可能得先多掏一笔钱。一份租赁方案提出，月之暗面的预付款要比非中国客户高出 30% 至 50%。欧洲云服务商担心美国未来封堵中国企业远程租用先进芯片的渠道，因此希望尽早收回资金。

最近美国对中国 AI 公司租用海外算力的限制正在加码。英伟达要求海外云服务商至少将 51% 的服务提供给非中国客户，甲骨文也迫于特朗普政府压力，取消了与腾讯价值约 70 亿美元的 AI 算力租赁合同。

美国目前禁止 Blackwell 等先进芯片直接出口中国，但尚未全面禁止中国企业租用海外算力。今年 7 月，白宫曾指称月之暗面通过泰国数据中心使用 Blackwell。如今，月之暗面又在欧洲寻找算力，而美国国会正在推动立法，试图进一步限制这种远程使用方式。

author: ki_young_ju
quoted_text:
MARA no longer discloses its average mining cost directly, but it can be back-calculated from figures in its 10-Q.

- Cost per petahash per day: $31.3 (cost to maintain 1 PH/s for 24 hours)
- Avg. Bitcoin mined per day: 23.3 BTC
- Avg. operational hash rate: 50.4 EH/s (50,400 PH/s)

50,400 × $31.3 ÷ 23.3 = $67,704 per BTC

The "purchased energy costs per BTC" they disclose ($39,235 in Q3 2025 for owned sites) is an IR-friendly figure that isn't fully accurate, as it excludes other operating expenses.

text:
缺失“年率”比对的10月CPI数据对市场有何影响？沃勒数据前讲话将12月加息预期拉满，数据公布后市场如何定价？

今晚的10月CPI数据缺乏年率比对，并非什么特殊情况，而是去年同期美国政府停摆导致10月数据缺乏，所以没有前值比对，年率无法统计！

而对市场的影响更是很小，不管是利率市场，还是金融市场，更加关注月率环比，而核心服务与住房通胀，也并未受到直接影响，所以缺乏这份数据，并不影响目前市场的解读与定价，不用担心！

缺乏年率，今晚数据关注月率环比即可！

整体CPI月率环比，核心CPI月率环比，是今晚的重要数据，其次关注核心服务业通胀，住房通胀，工资通胀等其他分享，除了能源对通胀的干扰之外，看的是美国内生通胀是否继续恶化，这将会影响后续通胀逻辑

而目前来看，数据预期名义CPI与核心CPI均走弱，如果数据符合预期，意味着过去10月份通胀走弱，尤其是核心通胀走弱，内生通胀并未恶化，减缓12月加息必要性，如果未来1个月伴随着Brent 价格跌破90美元继续下行，12月加息概率会被持续压制

10月国际能源价格明显处于高位，为何预期会如此乐观？

主要是9月份美国汽油价格暴涨，导致9月CPI大幅度增加，而市场预期9月份价格暴涨之后后续价格有所缓和，所以预期10月CPI数据会明显减弱

但是这种数据减弱并不能代表通胀压力没了，关键还是要核心通胀情况，以及内生通胀担忧的逻辑是否还在？

数据公布后，对市场的影响如何？面对97%的加息概率，市场如何定价？

乐观预期，数据低于目前预期，通胀比预期更加缓和，减缓Fed继续加息的决心，利于风险资产，数据公布后风险市场会利多，12月加息概率降低

中性数据，数据符合预期，9月份CPI暴涨之后10月数据稍微回落修复，但是通胀依旧保持粘性，核心通胀稳定具备粘性，内生通胀担忧还在但是并未恶化，此类情况在数据公布后金融市场先交易12月加息预期，随后市场开始反弹上涨，核心逻辑是此前市场对12月加息充分定价，12月通胀公布靴子落地，市场反而要开始新的定价逻辑！

鹰派数据，名义通胀与核心通胀小幅度超预期，结合今天下午沃勒讲话内容，进一步锁定12月加息概率，数据公布后市场会先交易12月加息，然后美股下半场可能回归反弹上涨趋势，核心逻辑同上，但是这里要注意，这份数据不能让2027年3月份的加息概率超过50%，

超鹰派数据，名义与核心通胀不仅超过预期，还超过前值，10月通胀在9月加速后并未放缓加速脚步，通胀担忧大大增加，这时不仅会锁定12月加息概率，更是会让2027年3月加息概率大大提升，市场从定价12月加息改为对明年3月加息进行继续定价，并且定价加息周期回归。

数据总结：

简单来说，今晚的CPI数据我认为只要不出现“超级鹰派”数据组合，对风险市场，对美股，对#Bitcoin 其实都是好事，尤其是在数据公布前，沃勒讲话让市场提前锁定了12月加息

概率上12月加息锁定，市场提前开始消化，数据公布后，只要不比这个结果更坏，那就是好事，就是利空靴子落地，就是反弹行情，最大的区别就是中性数据反弹更好，鹰派数据反弹弱一点

所以，我认为本周通胀数据公布之后到12月议息会议之前，都是很好的买入时机，只要2027年3月加息概率别上升到60%即可（目前50%），毕竟利率侧最差预期已经出现，后续一旦Brent 跌破90美元，市场会持续交易通胀放缓的行情，而12月加息概率会逐步被削弱。

PS：概率锁定并不等于一定加息，Brent价格是12月议息会议前最大的变量！
