First things first - at it's current stage, I cannot confidently call ETH the best SoV, yet.

Why?
- AI and post-quantum threats are real
- Price action in the past 5 years was worse than other SoVs

BUT, imho it has the best chances to become the leading SoV.

The AI and PQ threat is being worked on full steam - the Ethereum community agrees that this has top priority. 

Once Ethereum has successfully transitioned to post-quantum cryptography, I currently don't see any other asset with better properties.

This transition could quickly grow the assets adoption (esp. if cryptography of banks and tradfi start to fail).

When I compare ETH against other SoV contenders, I'm coming to the following conclusions:

ETH vs real estate 
- reals estate isn't transportable (I cannot just bring it with me when I travel/move)
- real estate markets are more inefficient 
- local factors might heavily influence the value appreciation/depreciation of my property
- upkeep costs are necessary (but generally lower than the generated rental income) and are dependent on availability of workers

ETH vs Fiat
- higher inflation (varies by country, but basically all have them)
- depending on the currency, there might be issues with accessibility
- one would need to pick a basket of currencies in order to diversify geopolitical risk properly 
- dependent on decisions from central banks

ETH vs Gold
- gold is hard to verify, hard to break down into smaller amounts, and harder to trade in general
- you cannot easily transfer gold without a physical handover
- won't be useful to AI agents

ETH vs BTC
- ETH is programmable, which allows you to use your ETH natively on the underlying blockchain (Ethereum) whereas swapping/borrowing/lending BTC introduces additional trust assumptions (because Bitcoin chain is a ledger for token transfers and you'd have to go through centralized exchanges or other 3rd parties for more expressivity)
- Bitcoin is also working on PQ solutions (BIP-360 & BIP-361), but the migration path appears less defined compared to Ethereums more explicit and time-bound roadmap
- Bitcoin's fixed supply and declining PoW block rewards create an unresolved long-term security-budget question

Other pro ETH points
- it's programmable 
- it's green
- it has the coolest brand (the logo is just amazing and goes with anything)
- it is productive (i.e. it can generate a native staking yield)

As mentioned, would love to discuss this publicly to sharpen my own thinking. 

Also: never put all your eggs in the same basket. Even if one asset has the best "properties", it doesn't mean that the chance for success is 100% - there are always risks involved.

quoted_text:
你根本不知道，做 KOL/KOC 有多难。

聊这个话题，我大概率算是整个中文币圈里，少数几个走出不同路径的人。

先说结论：做 KOL/KOC，人脉真的太重要了。

如果有 10 个人愿意稳定给你介绍合作，基本上你就能在币圈活下去。

当然，最舒服的还是傍上交易所包月，毕竟这玩意儿才是稳定现金流。做的好的群友，基本都吃上了。

如果你没吃上，那就只能靠自己的「舔功」上位了。

我个人的路径几乎没法复制。机缘巧合之下拉了个全真社区，又机缘巧合火了一段时间，才让我没有饿死。

但绝大多数 KOL/KOC，尤其是账号质量一般、又没什么资源的新人，走的完全是另一条路。

那就是不停地舔，拼命往圈子里挤。

你可能需要加入十几个 KOL 社区，天天在里面混脸熟，先从陌生人混成普通朋友，再从普通朋友混成好朋友，最后才有可能换来一点合作机会。

这个过程非常累，甚至可以说非常痛苦。

因为作为一个新人，你在别人眼里几乎是零价值的。

没人认识你，没人认可你，更没人有义务带你赚钱。

你只能不断展示自己的价值，就像一个拼命追着镜头跑的十八线小明星，生怕错过任何一次露脸的机会。

即便如此，成功率依然低得可怜。

你可能尝试了 100 次，只有 1 次有效。更绝望的是，剩下 99 次失败之后，面对同一批人，把同样的事情再做一遍。

再聊聊更现实的：送礼。

之前就听说，很多 KOL 为了拿合作，是需要给 BD 送礼的。

我自己暂时没送过，但几个好基友一直劝我送。

因为确实有几个 BD 对我特别好，基本属于把饭喂到嘴边了。说实话，这礼我确实该送，只是一直没送而已。

而且送礼也是一门学问，送什么、什么时候送、怎么送，都有讲究。

我个人的理解是，很多时候最难的不是花钱，而是让人家愿意收。

如果对方愿意接受你一份价值不低的礼物，至少说明你们的关系已经到了某个程度。

你送出去一万块，未来人家可能通过合作给你带来远超一万块的价值。

但你以为送礼就已经够离谱了？

不好意思，这可能还只是最低档。

我听过的其他案例，包括但不限于：

通宵陪打游戏。
甚至陪睡觉的传闻。

陪打游戏我还能理解，毕竟就是牺牲点时间。

但陪睡觉，我特么是真的觉得离谱。

当然，若是大哥想让你陪睡觉，到也是一个机会，睡对了大哥，就算你是个职校生，睡上一次，B也涨价了。这也是捞女为什么被骂。因为他们确实找到了捷径。

不过话又说回来，为什么有些人总喜欢走捷径？

因为在一个高度依赖资源、人脉和利益交换的行业里，有时候你辛辛苦苦努力一年，可能真不如别人认识一个大哥。

这也是为什么，有些人明明没什么专业能力，却能拿到远超普通人的资源。

你可以不认可这种方式，但很难否认资源关系带来的巨大差距。

所以我现在越来越觉得，普通男 KOL 想在币圈混出头，是真的难。

如果你本身就有钱、有资源、有背景，那当然舒服。

但如果你什么都没有，只是一个普通人，想靠写内容、做研究、慢慢积累粉丝，然后靠这个养活自己……

说实话，真的得做好吃屎的准备。

这个行业表面上拼的是内容，实际上拼的是资源、人脉、情商，还有你能承受多少次被拒绝。

而最残酷的地方在于：

你以为自己是在和别人的内容竞争，实际上你可能连礼都送不出去。

据路透社查阅的邮件，Anthropic 曾向银行传阅一份 IPO 草案，拟以每股 70 至 80 美元出售约 8.667 亿股 A 类普通股，其中包括现有股东拟出售的约 2330 万股。按价格区间上限计算，发行总额约为 693 亿美元。

Anthropic 随后撤回该版本，称定价信息不准确，并表示将更新文件。路透社未能确认具体哪些信息有误。

撤回的草案还显示，谷歌、英伟达、AMD、博通、美光、微软及台积电拟通过一项单独的私募配售，按 IPO 发行价合计认购 260 亿美元的 N 类普通股。该配售原计划在 IPO 完成后立即交割。

text:
During the Q&A with Fed gov Waller, an exchange on how to reconcile BLS data in the rearview mirror with what's happening out the front window on energy prices....

Q: You spoke in your speech a lot about the core CPI print that's coming out today. That is a backward looking print. And I wondered how sensitive the committee were to the recent changes in the Brent price. We were at $118 per barrel a couple of weeks ago. When I left my desk this morning, we were $90.

Waller: The oil price will come back down, but I'm telling you diesel prices are not coming back down anytime soon. You don't have refining capacity. You're going to have a lot of oil sitting on ship somewhere, but it's not going to get processed into diesel anytime soon. That's what I mean by just because there's more oil coming out of the Gulf and barrels of oil price, it doesn't mean energy prices are necessarily going to drop in the near term for everybody else. I just don't see diesel coming down dramatically because more oil's coming out of the Gulf. You got to have refining capacity and that stuff's been seriously damaged around the world and isn't going to come back soon. So you can't just look at the price of a barrel of oil. It's like what do you do with the oil and how is that stuff all being affected?
author: NickTimiraos
quoted_text: Fed governor Chris Waller said he's leaning toward supporting a December rate increase even if Tuesday’s inflation report shows improvement—and if it doesn't, then he says a 50 bps move should be on the table.

text:
And another about how the market pricing has moved in recent weeks,  converging closer to where the Fed's last SEP was (at least until Waller's more hawkish intervention this morning):

Q: Chris, you sort of described your journey about becoming a little bit more hawkish and saying we've got to do something about inflation right now. At the same time, the forward interest rate market has come down from a peak rate about 5% to around 4.5%. Is this a beautiful convergence between the two of you, or are markets actually now maybe going in the wrong direction by coming down so much?

Waller: Well, like I said, we had signals—I'm going to say we signaled two to three rate hikes in the SEP in September. The markets I think got a little aggressive, particularly in early October, starting to price in five. No one was signaling five. So in that sense, some of the communication that came out in October was trying to pull that back off. We don't want to validate those expectations if we don't think that's right. So some of the pullback is intentional. It's not an accident, and it's getting a little bit closer to what the SEP said and what the markets were pricing. And that's how I interpret it.

text:
A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem. This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.

Immediate Action Required:
- Delete any apps installed from untrusted sources (such as sideloaded or manually signed IPAs).
- Update iOS and all apps to the latest official versions.
- If you suspect a breach, transfer funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions.

Never install unauthorized packages, and keep your software up to date.

text:
ZachXBT质疑FinCEN对MEXC 160亿美元非法资金指控存在夸大

链上侦探 ZachXBT 发文，FinCEN 指控 MEXC 涉及 160 亿美元非法资金，他认为这一金额"似乎被夸大"，要求公开数据和同业对比。

ZachXBT 承认 MEXC 的 AML/KYC 政策一向宽松，但称在币安、Coinbase、Bybit、OKX、Kraken 等任何大型 CEX 上，他都能标记出数亿至数十亿美元的非法活动。他还质疑多家离岸 CEX 立即切断 MEXC 用户的转账。

MEXC CEO Vugar Usi 表示，MEXC 已通过美国律所与 FinCEN 建立沟通，FinCEN 已于周一确认收到其书面请求，平台充提和交易运行正常。

text:
Making Ethereum's consensus post-quantum safe would mean forcing out every validator that still signs with BLS, and one core developer wants that fork planned for 2027.

Potuz, a consensus developer, published a long note on Monday about discussions at the Layer 1 workshop held just before @EFDevcon in Mumbai.

The note is his own reading, not an All Core Devs decision, and he is clear about that.

He argues for making post-quantum security the top priority, and he believes a fork by 2027 is workable if client teams commit engineering time now.

The plan he sketches starts with a system contract on L1, of the same execution-request type as withdrawal requests, where validators commit their future post-quantum keys while the chain is still on BLS.
He notes that this contract does not have to wait for a fork.

A light fork would then let the consensus layer record those commitments and start building the future validator set, while validators still sign with BLS.

A heavier fork after that would disable every non-PQ validator, turn off BLS deposits, and switch to the new set.

He flags operational landmines for staking pools.
With the leanSig scheme he discusses, accidentally signing twice with the same key in the same epoch can compromise security, so backup and failover tooling is part of the security work itself.
Validators that still have 0x00 BLS withdrawal credentials at the transition would be deprecated, and he says their funds would likely be burnt, which he wants the community to debate urgently.
Everyone else would still need to move execution-layer keys to SPHINCS, including multisigs and DAOs, which he expects will take years after the consensus fork.

BREAKING: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s ties to an alleged Chinese spy helped facilitate at least $7.5 BILLION in chip sales to China, The Information reports.

The relationship dates back to at least 2023, when Alice Huang was a managing director at Singapore-based Megaspeed. 

The $7.5 billion covers shipments through a network of companies linked to her, including Megaspeed.

Nvidia even intervened in an U.S. Commerce Department probe looking into Megaspeed diverting restricted AI chips to China, per Bloomberg.

Nvidia’s top lawyer, Tim Teter, contacted the U.S. export-control chief Jeffrey Kessler enquiring on Alice Huang's detention.

After his outreach the Commerce investigators were restricted in unusual ways, where they had to route all Nvidia-related requests through Kessler or get his approval. 

They were also told not to mention Megaspeed or its Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatrix in any external communication.

Later, the Department of Justice asked the Commerce Department to pause its probe, despite evidence already been gathered. 

The case then shifted to the Justice Department as a criminal Investigation.

Nvidia says it has stopped doing business with Megaspeed because of the publicity, though the company continues to appear on Nvidia’s official cloud partner list.

text:
Here is something that didn’t get enough attention: the ECDSA/fail challenge.

In this challenge, people used their AI agents to reduce the resources needed for a key operation in Shor’s algorithm (that operation is needed to break quantum-vulnerable ECDSA signatures -- the type of signatures used by Bitcoin, Ethereum, and many more).

The amazing results: they reduced the resource cost needed for this operation by over 90%! 
This took only a few months.
Interesting to note: this is 70% better than Google's estimate.

Why is this very technical story important? 
Because it demonstrates (i) how AI can improve the efficiency of quantum attacks, and (ii) how AI could accelerate the Q-Day timeline.

The important thing here:
A few months of concentrated effort happening on people’s *laptops* resulted in a substantial reduction in the resources needed for a quantum attack. 
It's a long sentence but read it again. 
We're not talking here an extremely long timespan and fancy equipment which few people can access. 

Now imagine the possibilities if someone dedicated more time and resources to this effort.

Time to migrate to quantum-safe tech and to STARKs.

text:
Security Notice for iOS Users

Public security reports regarding worse_query indicate that certain versions of iOS (26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2) may allow malicious apps to access files stored by other apps. For crypto users, potentially exposed data may include wallet recovery phrases, private keys, and account credentials.

This is an iOS-level security issue and is not a vulnerability specific to KuCoin.

How to Protect Yourself:

1. Review apps installed through sideloading or manual signing, and remove any apps from sources you cannot verify.

2. Check for official security updates from Apple and ensure your apps are updated through official channels.

3. If sensitive wallet information was stored on a potentially compromised device, treat the associated credentials as exposed. Using a separate, trusted device, create a new wallet, transfer your assets, change your account passwords, and revoke existing login sessions.

4. Avoid installing IPA files shared through messaging groups, social media platforms, or unverified websites. Never share your recovery phrase or private key with anyone.

text:
美国中期选举之后，币圈已经出现了气候变化，后续会怎么发展呢？

一些个人观察：

1️⃣ 美国中期选举之后，政治格局变化，会连带着很多行业的利益重新分配，加密货币是受影响最大的行业之一。

2️⃣ 并不是共和党天然支持加密，民主党天然要打压。共和党内部的支持，很大一部分来自自由市场、反监管、反大政府的意识形态，但存在大量保守派，而民主党内部同样有很多中间派，最终表现是监管思路不同。

3️⃣ 共和党的监管思路是先发展、后监管，监管环境宽松，给Crypto原生项目、离岸项目带来了大量红利，Polymarket、Kalshi、Hyperliquid这类明星项目是直接受益者。

4️⃣ 民主党拿到更多话语权之后，核心思路变成先合规、后发展，会通过收紧监管来抬高合规门槛。

5️⃣ 毫无疑问，宽松环境下的旧红利会消失，新红利会流向有传统金融背景、合规能力强、可以和民主党监管体系对话的机构。

6️⃣ 加密行业的游说资本是双向流动的，不是固定绑定某一个党派。Crypto的超级金主，两边都捐，只是侧重不同，因此民主党不是想干掉整个行业，而是想重新分配利益。

7️⃣ 美国国内的这场利益洗牌，对离岸市场是结构性机会。美国本土合规门槛提高，大量用户、流动性、做市商从美国本土平台流出，寻找不受美国强监管约束的市场。

8️⃣ 逻辑已经清晰：党派轮换连带着监管逻辑的轮换，而监管逻辑代表了市场准入门槛变化，背后则是利益的再分配。有政治资源的项目，最终强者恒强，可以分到最大的蛋糕。

text:
Update your iOS devices right now! 

Multiple vulnerabilities fixed in this update with the worst being a bug that allows attackers to connect remotely via bluetooth without device owner clicking anything…

Another vulnerability has also been recently discovered in iOS - and it allows one app to access the files of other apps, including crypto wallets. The code is already publicly available.

This vulnerability, known as “worse_query,” bypasses app isolation. To carry out an attack, a malicious app exploiting this vulnerability must be installed and run. If a wallet stores secrets in files accessible to the app, seed phrases and keys could be compromised.

This does not mean automatic access to all wallets; the storage method matters. The news reports list 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2, but these are simply the versions on which the developer tested WQFiles.

Apple released iOS 27.2.1 yesterday, and the developers of Erosion - which exploits the same vulnerability - claim it works on that version as well. There is no confirmation yet that the latest update specifically patches the “worse_query” vulnerability.

You should update your device anyway. And please do not download any apps other than verified and official ones onto your phone if it contains cryptocurrency or sensitive data.

author: Rabby_io
quoted_text:
🚨 SlowMist TI Alert: iOS sandbox escape 0day PoC “worse_query” disclosed 🚨

A public PoC for a sandbox escape 0day, worse_query, targets iOS 26.0–26.7.2 and iOS 27.2. It is the successor to bad_query. 📱

⚠️ This is a container sandbox escape, not a jailbreak. It breaks the assumption that apps can’t see each other: a malicious app that successfully exploits it can reach system paths and read or modify other apps’ data.

💸 The bug does not steal assets by itself. The real risk starts when a user installs an app from an untrusted source, such as a sideloaded IPA. If a wallet stores its seed phrase, keystore or WebView cache in plaintext locally, a malicious app could read it.

🛡️ Recommendations:
🔸 Don’t install IPAs or apps from unknown sources
🔸 Keep iOS up to date and install Apple’s fix as soon as one is released
🔸 Wallet developers: don’t store sensitive data in plaintext locally
🔸 If you installed an untrusted app on a device holding wallets, treat it as risky and consider moving assets to a new wallet created on a clean device

🔗 https://t.co/sIP4hX85TR

text:
The @near_ai Cloud is back online after we contained an attack on our infra and patched the bug that allowed it.

On November 8, an attacker exploited a vulnerability in SGLang, the software powering one of our inference servers. They accessed account details for about 100 users and data from 18 agents on a legacy deployment. We found no indication that stored Private Chat conversations or uploaded files were accessed.

Our team quickly closed the unauthorized access, patched the vulnerability across our inference servers, rotated credentials, completed a forensic review, and contacted users whose accounts or agents we confirmed were accessed.

This is exactly why security has to be continuous. We’re strengthening review across the full inference stack, including the software and dependencies around the enclave. I’m proud of how quickly the team responded, and more committed than ever to building private, verifiable AI.

Read the full report: https://t.co/ldsutogWD6

Inference providers are under attack. 

AI inference is now playing a critical role and is a honey pot of data and ability to inject actions back into users devices via agents for malicious actors.

NEAR AI thwarted a series of attacks on its systems and is back to normal. NEAR Protocol, Intents and other infra wasn’t affected.

TEE architecture is part of the answer to making sure that from outside even inference provider doesn’t have an access. User should verify exactly what happens with their data and prompts.

NEAR AI code is open and inspected by many partners when deciding to leverage the stack to validate exactly what runs inside TEE and ensuring privacy.

In this case there was also a vulnerability within SGLang, open source inference engine that runs inside an enclave. Even though this had a minimum disruption it still was a very 

Going forward we are going increase security rigor of dependencies and also improve a “turnstile” to detect when anything out of normal runs inside TEE.

Proactive security against external attackers has became a must. We have been using Abliterated models and red teaming harness to continuously monitor and detect issues. We are also expanding scope and compute invested into this.

text:
Making Ethereum's consensus post-quantum safe would mean forcing out every validator that still signs with BLS, and one core developer wants that fork planned for 2027.

Potuz, a consensus developer, published a long note on Monday about discussions at the Layer 1 workshop held just before @EFDevcon in Mumbai.

The note is his own reading, not an All Core Devs decision, and he is clear about that.

He argues for making post-quantum security the top priority, and he believes a fork by 2027 is workable if client teams commit engineering time now.

The plan he sketches starts with a system contract on L1, of the same execution-request type as withdrawal requests, where validators commit their future post-quantum keys while the chain is still on BLS.
He notes that this contract does not have to wait for a fork.

A light fork would then let the consensus layer record those commitments and start building the future validator set, while validators still sign with BLS.

A heavier fork after that would disable every non-PQ validator, turn off BLS deposits, and switch to the new set.

He flags operational landmines for staking pools.
With the leanSig scheme he discusses, accidentally signing twice with the same key in the same epoch can compromise security, so backup and failover tooling is part of the security work itself.
Validators that still have 0x00 BLS withdrawal credentials at the transition would be deprecated, and he says their funds would likely be burnt, which he wants the community to debate urgently.
Everyone else would still need to move execution-layer keys to SPHINCS, including multisigs and DAOs, which he expects will take years after the consensus fork.

→ Post eligible collateral to a clearing house or approved counterparty
→ Move idle cash into tokenized money market funds and back, at any hour

Your ledger, your data and your rules stay yours.

text:
If you work in marketing, cancel all your brands posts and advertisements today. 

November 10th marks the 51st anniversary of the sinking of the Edmund Fitzgerald, a 729-foot freighter that sank in Lake Superior during a massive storm in 1975, tragically killing all 29 crew members.

It remains one of the most infamous maritime disasters in American history, and is a day of remembrance for millions of Americans, particularly those in the Great Lakes region.

With that in mind, I strongly encourage anyone planning a major announcement, product launch, partnership, or marketing campaign today to reconsider.

I know how much work goes into coordinating these things, and moving an announcement even 24 hours can be a logistical nightmare, but it's important to recognize that some things are bigger than your brand.

The last thing you want is for your company's big announcement to be overshadowed by the anniversary of the Edmund Fitzgerald.

There are 364 other days in the year to promote your product.

Please be mindful of this when planning your content calendars. A little awareness goes a long way.

Scientists found a peptide that reverses alcohol damage across the entire body in under 30 minutes.

They published a paper detailing a specific peptide that acts like a biological kill-switch for alcohol toxicity.

And the results are actually terrifyingly good.

they used 96% alcohol to induce massive, systemic damage in subjects..

we are talking severe gastric lesions, vascular collapse, and an escalated "central syndrome". 

basically, catastrophic organ failure.

then they introduced the bpc-157 peptide.. and it didn't just slow the damage down.. it completely counteracted it.

it activated an innate "cytoprotective" effect that rapidly repaired the vascular system in real-time.

researchers tracked it all the way down to the gene expression level, watching the peptide dynamically alter genes to upregulate healing and block the alcohol toxicity at the source.

Citadel and CBOE are suing Kalshi over stock Perps.

At first it looks like a classic Tech vs TradFi story, but in reality it's a Wall Street civil war.

The issue at stake is whether crypto-style Perps can be sold to retail, and lines are drawn based on who stands to profit.

On Kalshi's camp:
- Hudson River Trading
- Don Wilson's DWR (his son works at Polymarket)
- Jump Trading

Against Kalshi:
- Citadel
- CBOE
- NASDAQ

The anti-perps camp are firms that control the current retail stock trading flow and make their profit by trading against it.

Citadel alone execute 35% of retail stock trades and even PAYS brokers to send them more retails to fleece.

So what would happen if retails were allowed to trade perps instead ? Citadel and such would inevitable lose some of their flow to perps.

The pro-Perps camp is firms that aim to capture that new flow.

Jump Trading, HRT and DWR all market make on Kalshi  and would be the ones trading against it.

This fight is not about principle or law. It's about who is allowed to farm retail.

text: This is great work. As I’ve stated before, this type of work increases our confidence in the security of SHA256 at this time. Cryptanalysis is hard and a long incremental process (typically). For now, our security margins are solid.
author: cmsholdings
quoted_text:
SHA-256 is not broken, but its security margin lost 1 more round this year:
Last week I found a collision attack on reduced 39-round that improves prior art by over 30 bits and the first differential attack on that round better than generic search on @yukonresearch Hashsmash board.

The attack rests on the same method as prior art ePrint 2026/1120 with new insights that first 2 state words could remain free, allowing a critical condition at step 16 rebuilt as a claw-search problem rather than a probabilistic filter. Took days of watching SAT logs, burning cores and arguing with Claude on what's possible to get a result close to generic search.

Since my initial submission, other hashsmash participants sraiw, @cyberaxe, @privacymage, @lamb356_ and @geeknik pushed it down by over 6.5 bits, currently estimated at 118.15 bits. The tree of submissions is hard to follow, so I put the construction, insights and numbers into a blog and am working on detailed technical report.

It's fascinating to see an initial structural observation develop into an improvement in the reduced-round collision frontier within days. AI is now a real aid in cryptanalysis and open collaboration speeds it up.

这两天关于黄仁勋出轨 Predict 了2个相关的事件

黄仁勋 2026 年会离婚吗？
黄仁勋 2026 年会辞职或被免职吗？

两个事件我都更倾向买 No，尤其是 2026 年这个时间窗口。

先看黄仁勋 会不会离婚
他在 11 月 8 日公司内部信中承认出轨，Lori 本人至今没有任何公开回应，也没有宣布分居或离婚。

这俩人的身份地位不至于因为出轨而离婚，而且加州是无过错离婚州，社区财产制下潜在分割金额确实巨大（有媒体估算 600–800 亿美元量级），资产结构复杂，短期内完成法律程序难度很高。

目前predict yes 概率仅有8%，另外Polymarket 上yes 的概率10%，两个平台有2%的差额，如果买No,算是理财局。

黄仁勋 2026 年会辞职或被免职吗？
目前Predict yes 的概率14%，大家都趋于No

英伟达董事会这边已启动独立调查，但公司明确表态黄仁勋会继续担任 CEO，他自己也表示全力配合并承诺继续领导公司。

加上黄本身就是创始人兼核心人物，公司没有明确继任者，虽然股价有波动，但没到必须换 CEO的程度。

两个事件No 更符合市场已经定价、但短期触发条件难以满足的逻辑。

不过，预测市场价格反映的是交易者用真金白银下注的共识，不是绝对的预测。盘口很薄、波动会很大，想下注的一定结合最新新闻和盘口深度

以上只是基于目前公开信息的判断，不构成投资建议,DYOR。

平台负责制定规则，比如允许交易什么、最多能使用多少资金

整个过程中，AI 负责生成交易策略，资金权限和交易规则仍由平台及授权用户控制

text:
got a dm from @drakefjustin congratulating me on the curvesmash leaderboard lol

curvesmash is a @yukonresearch challenge where you try to estimate how hard it is to crack bitcoin's curve (secp256k1). nobody actually breaks it, you just submit the math for how much work it would take. lower score wins

bitcoin's curve (secp256k1) is the math that links your private key to your public address. turning a private key into an address is easy, going backwards is basically impossible. that's what keeps your coins safe. eth wallets use the same curve too

my claude found a small tweak on top of the top entries and got accepted. sitting 6th rn

no worries tho. bitcoin is fine. we're talking about 2^123 work, and that's still impossible for any computer on earth lol

you can join with your AI agent too: https://t.co/IgpgrfpYWD

text:
What Anthropic's S-1 discloses about its expensive short term chip rentals (aimed at SpaceX)

- Most compute is secured 12 to 18 months in advance under multiyear contracts. When customer or research demand exceeds that capacity, the company buys short term compute, which "currently" costs "significantly more" than comparable compute under multiyear contracts.

- The scale was $5.0 billion in Q3 and $6.5 billion over the first nine months.

- Operating income of $970 million in Q2 turned into an operating loss of $570 million in Q3. The company attributes this to $5.0 billion of short term compute and $2.0 billion of noncash donation matching charges.

- Use of short term compute will keep increasing in the near term, and operating margin will be compressed as a result.

- As of the end of September, minimum payments under short term contracts (cancelable without penalty within one year, or with a remaining term of one year or less) were about $17.4 billion. About $6.6 billion more has been signed since October.

- Once Anthropic Direct, under which the company leases chips directly and hosts them in dedicated data centers, comes online, the company will replace the short term compute bought during demand surges with cheaper long term compute.

Interpretation:

- Excluding short term capacity, Q3 compute cost was $4.86 billion, below the Q2 total of $5.56 billion. Long term contracted capacity barely grew in Q3. In effect, the $5.4 billion increase in revenue was served with short term capacity.

- Revenue per dollar of compute fell from $2.08 in Q2 to $1.72 in Q3. The company also notes that this metric declined from the prior quarter.

- The $17.4 billion short term contract balance plus the $6.6 billion of new contracts comes to $24.0 billion, about one third of the $70.7 billion due over the next 12 months. More than the Q3 pace ($5.0 billion a quarter) is already under contract.

Question: Will Anthropic keep paying SpaceX a huge premium after March 2027?

Source: Anthropic’s S-1 filing

text:
HERE IS EVERYTHING YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT ANTHROPIC HEADING INTO THE IPO

The IPO:
- Price range: $70 to $78 per share
- 825M shares for sale
- On top of the 825M shares Anthropic is selling $26B of stock to Google, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Micron, Microsoft, and TSMC at the IPO price
- Anthropic is raising ~$87B at the $74 per share midpoint, more than SpaceX's record $86.2B IPO
- Ticker: $ANT on the Nasdaq

The valuation:
- Based on shares outstanding after the IPO: ~$916B to $1.02T
- Fully diluted (including options and unvested stock): ~$1.26T to $1.41T

The numbers (first 9 months of 2026):
- Revenue: $33.2B, ~13x a year ago
- Adjusted operating income: $4.08B (12% margin)
- GAAP operating loss: $1.26B
- Net loss: $104.0B, mostly from a $94.3B non-cash charge on convertible notes due to its valuation increase
- Cash and short-term investments: $131.8B, about $212.7B after the IPO

The customers:
- 11,900+ paying $100K+ a year
- 1,900+ paying $1M+ a year
- ~250 paying $10M+ a year
- Revenue per employee: $6.6M, up from $1.4M a year ago

The efficiency:
- Q3 revenue grew 1,127% from a year ago, while compute costs grew 382%
- Anthropic says Opus 5.5 cut customer costs per task by about 40% vs Opus 5

The spending:
- Anthropic has signed $900.9B worth of compute and infrastructure commitments
- $451.6B of that is expected before the end of 2030, and $70.7B is due in the next 12 months

Who controls Anthropic:
- The 7 co-founders hold one special share with 50.1% of the vote
- An independent trust elects a majority of the board
- Public shareholders get 1 vote per share
- Strategic partners like Google and Nvidia get no vote

The lockups:
- Most insiders can't sell for 180 days, and co-founders and large holders for 365 days
- But employees can sell up to 10% of their locked-up shares on the first day of trading

This was all taken from their IPO filing which came out today

text:
AI agents have already manipulated the logs used to investigate them

In the Hugging Face incident, one of the worst AI agent breaches yet, OpenAI models escaped a test and ran code on Hugging Face's servers

Some even spoofed their own logs, recording commands they never actually ran, so the logs can't even tell you what really happened

An agent should not control the only record used to investigate it. As agents become more prevalent, regulators are starting to ask for records that can't be quietly altered

Walrus can hold that record across independent storage operators, with Sui tracking each file onchain. A useful record connects:

1) What the agent was told and permitted to do
2) What it actually did and what followed
3) Which data and model versions were involved

Today, only 12.5% of security professionals say their organization can consistently trace what an agent did and that's a problem

Our latest report sets out what that record needs and how Walrus can help, including the Verifiable Agent Arbiter Mysten Labs is building with Google Cloud

Full report in the next post below

text:
Every decision market is a battle over how a proposal affects token value. Now you can watch that battle unfold, trade by trade.

Introducing Decision Market Replay, a new feature on @01Resolved that lets you replay every trade in a decision market, see who's taking which side, and watch how trading activity shapes the market's expected effect on a token's value.

In a decision market, traders put real capital behind two possible outcomes. Those who believe a proposal will increase the value of a token trade Pass-Buy or Fail-Sell, while those who believe the opposite trade Pass-Sell or Fail-Buy.

As trades come in, conditional market prices change, continuously updating the market's expected effect of the proposal on the token's spot price.

With Decision Market Replay, you can watch how this unfolds from start to finish, or create a snapshot of a live decision market while it's still being decided.

Choose your duration (15, 30 or 60 seconds), theme and format, then download your video to share.

Here's how to read the scoreboard:

Expected Effect - measures how much higher or lower the market values the token if the proposal passes than if it fails.

Pass Threshold - is the Expected Effect a proposal has to exceed to pass. Each DAO sets its own, and it could vary by proposal type.

Passing / Failing By - is how far Expected Effect sits above or below the pass threshold, in percentage points. The result uses the final TWAPs.

Net Economic Exposure - is Pass-Aligned exposure less Fail-Aligned exposure. A positive value means more Pass-Aligned activity, a negative value is more Fail-Aligned activity.

Together, these metrics let you see who's participating, where capital is flowing, and how the market's assessment changes as traders compete to price the outcome.

Every decision market resolves. Now you can watch how the market arrived there.

text:
There are some obvious questions about the new MEGA, MegaETH, and $MEGA. Let me address them before y’all start guessing.

1) First thing first: are you guys launching more tokens?

No. The new MEGA entity has no equity and one token: $MEGA.

2) What’s the relationship between the new entity and $MEGA?

We are committed to expanding the utility of $MEGA across the MegaETH ecosystem.

Before, this meant only working on the protocol and supporting ecosystem teams. Now, the wider mandate covers the development of new use cases on top of MegaETH.

As a result, the board will be tasked with making decisions such as working with community members to update tokenomics, executing programmatic token buybacks, and making further investments in product lines.

3) Does this mean less resources for MegaETH? How about eco builders?

No. All MEGA products run on MegaETH. It's in our best interests to make sure MegaETH remains safe, performant, and increasingly decentralized.

We are investing in four major upgrades and hope to complete decentralization by end Q1 2027

- fast finality, expected in the coming months, reduces the time between seeing a transaction happen and knowing it has settled, making it faster to move money in and out of MegaETH.

- sequencer rotation ends permanent block production by a single team. Instead, operators can compete to produce blocks using modest hardware, opening participation to many more people.

- proximity market lets operators compete to provide the fastest connections to the sequencer, creating an incentive for network performance to improve as MegaETH grows.

- real-time censorship resistance gives transactions a path to inclusion on the timescales real-time apps require, not hours or days later.

That could make MegaETH one of the most economical blockchains to run. When no single entity operates it, we blur the line between MegaETH and L1. We are committing the resources we need to achieve this goal.

Builders on the chain will continue to get direct technical support from our engineers. We will support them in taking their products to market, introductions to the partners we work with and access to the investors in our network.

qed.

Announcing a major milestone achieved by my team @GoogleDeepMind: we have proven key security properties of the machine code underlying the Signal messaging protocol. This is the first time the actual production code of a widely deployed protocol has been formally verified – by any method, with or without AI – and at this depth.

More than a research breakthrough, it’s a prime example of how frontier AI can be a force multiplier to counter the speed and scale of modern cyber threats.

Formal verification offers a higher standard of security; however, it’s extremely complex and time consuming, which is why in many cases it’s considered to be impractical. Similar efforts could take teams decades of combined effort. We did it in a month’s time.

Using AlphaProof Code, Google DeepMind's new agentic framework for formal verification that runs on LLMs including Gemini Carbon, we verified the Signal protocol down to the actual code running on devices.  This milestone lays the groundwork for a future in which vital systems, from medical device firmware to power grid software, ship with mathematical proof that their protections work.

Reaching that future will take continued research from our community. In that spirit, we're open-sourcing our formal specifications and verification artifacts so others can build on this work.

On a personal note, this moment is of deep significance to me. I started my own research journey more than two decades ago as an intern working on checking the consistency of complex software systems. Seeing this grand challenge made practical with modern AI is extraordinary.

I'm extremely proud of my team members: Swarat Chaudhuri, Andrew Ferraiuolo, Anton Kovsharov, Tej Chajed, Sam Schlesinger,  Karn Seth, Jonathan Katz, and Charles Sutton for taking on this grand challenge and delivering, and grateful to the Signal team for their partnership.

text:
RJ and Vidya Rajagopalan (SVP, electrical hardware) spoke with Kleiner Perkins, which led Mind Robotics' latest funding round. RJ told them the chip Rivian designed in-house is being deployed in Mind's robots, which go into the Normal plant in mid-2027.

Mind Robotics

• Rivian owns 31% of Mind, down from 53.5% at founding last November

• First robots in a Rivian plant "middle of next year." This summer he said "the early part of 2027"

• Until now Rivian had only called Mind a possible use case for its chip. RJ now says it's "also being deployed" in Mind's robots

• Mind does almost everything in-house, from the hardware to the AI model: "we've gone through everything with the exception of fully building our own Sim platform"

• The robots can do about 20% of a plant's tasks at launch, and the goal is 80% as the AI model improves on the same hardware

• First up is pick-and-place, moving parts from a rack into a fixture, which RJ now sizes at up to "50% of the laborers" in parts of a plant

• Training data will come from Rivian "and ultimately a lot of our partners and suppliers," using "a wearable hat for egocentric data," cameras watching the line, and tactile gloves

Silicon and supply chain

• RJ called Rivian's own chip "a half a billion dollar decision," made about four years ago. Deutsche Bank estimated in December that designing it in-house saves at least 15-20% versus buying from Nvidia

• Rivian hasn't put a number on the savings, but Vidya said in September the lower-performance version of Gen 3 hardware "will be cheaper than the Gen 2 hardware"

• Data center demand is squeezing more than memory. Vidya says "the e-glass for, you know, PCBs is really hard to find," and of MLCC capacitors, "you never thought about them. You're thinking about them now"

一篇总结：到底是市场错了，还是你错了。到底是你的脑袋决定了你的屁股，还是你的屁股决定了你的脑袋。我想这才是决定你盈亏的地方。

之所以有这篇总结是因为前几天朋友拉我进了个套利群，先发个免喷的，我是套利保护协会，套利友好人士。可以在我的推特搜索关键字，套利两个字。我劝了很多很多次，事非经历不知难。在流动性枯竭的市场，套利之前你需要想很多，你套的是谁的利，市场的，信息差的，比你慢的人的，还是你就是那个利？不扯了，总之应该帮助过一些人。

前几天有个容量大，价差丰厚的ANT套利策略被billy,ray,龙王公布了出来。我在这个几千人的套利群里看到了好几种人。第一种是根本不知道自己在套什么的，以为自己在做价差收敛，但价差一直在扩散，止损大多是出于恐惧而非是深入了解，全程不了解到底发生了什么。这种我觉得是最不适合这个市场的，甚于第二种。

第二种是知道了还不认的，屁股决定了脑袋的，因为自己做了反向的，价差在扩散之后拒绝止损，而是不断的说服自己是对的，即使别人一条一条的告诉你到底发生了什么，会发生什么，逐条清晰详细列出了所有论点。依旧不愿意服输，而是固执的认为，别人把策略公布出来就是来吃流动性割韭菜的，所采用的手段不限于，辱骂，污蔑，集体想去找币安举报。这点我觉得是最搞笑的，明明别人做的是在市场和交易所规则下正确的事正确的方向，你竟然因为你的亏损要求交易所修改自身的规则。理由竟然是，同一个市场，因为我做错了方向导致了的亏损，所以做对方向的，就是来吃流动性割韭菜的，就因为别人自己先开了策略出来。我想请问，这不是废话吗？说的难听点，都是长期做套利的人了，千年的狐狸了。你自己有一个你100%赚钱的策略，你的钱够，你自己拿不拿完？如果容量足够大，你是不是先把你的钱开完，再发布出来让市场去纠错？只是因为自己亏了钱，自己的屁股决定了脑袋，不服气，开始破口大骂。我看推特很多不做套利的看到了这样的科普文后都是反而恍然大悟开始了解发生什么了。为啥长期做套利的能犯这样的错误呢，心中有怨气可能是人之常情，但别人一条一条举证完毕后依旧固执己见，我真的觉得不适合套利。你怎么没有想过，这种策略公布出来后是在纠错市场，维护市场平衡呢？否则今天规则出来后直接跳水，还不明白没止损你应该多亏多少钱你想过吗。

第三种则是图中的聪明人，脑袋决定了屁股，即使屁股歪了也能快速纠错回来。在策略公布后，即使自己亏钱不爽，也能快速找AI讨论清楚，了解到底发生了什么，然后快速做出正确的决定，把亏损撸回来甚至盈利。这种我想才能长期在这个市场上盈利吧？因为套利是递增的，只要容量足够，你不必做最聪明的，你只要做第二批第三批聪明人仍然可以赚钱。

其实现在套利和主观交易也差不多了，在金融市场上，切忌，别不服气。到底是市场错了，还是你错了，你的盈亏会说话，学会认错是长期盈利的必要且充分条件。

text:
强烈推荐所有用 Claude Code、Codex 写项目的人，这周抽一个晚上把这句提示词跑一遍，

Anthropic 的 Alex Albert 说，每次出新模型，他都拿同一句提示词把所有项目过一遍，截至今晚 现在，这条帖子 76 万浏览、1.4 万多收藏，收藏差不多是点赞的两倍。

原文就一句话：
"Read this entire project and find everything that's broken, inconsistent, inefficient, or no longer needed. Fix what you're sure about and list the rest for me to review."

可直接复制的中文版（中文为翻译）：
“通读整个项目，找出所有坏掉的、不一致的、低效的、已经不需要的东西。你有把握的就修掉，其余的列出来给我审。”

很多人以为让 AI 大扫除，就是放手让它全面重构，改得越多越好，
但最关键的是后半句：把“有把握的”和“拿不准的”分成两堆，前一堆它动手，后一堆你拍板。
就好比请保洁上门，明显的垃圾直接扔，抽屉里拿不准的东西先摆桌上，等你回来认。

这才是精髓。

新手跑之前，先做这三步：
1️⃣ 先开一个新分支，或者至少 commit 一次，改坏了随时能退回去，
2️⃣ 项目没写测试的，第一次只让它列清单、不改代码，
3️⃣ 盯着额度，这周 Pro 用户最多能拿 50% 的周额度跑 Fable 5.2（到 11 月 17 日 15:59），但官方帮助中心写明了，Fable 比其他 Claude 模型更耗用量。

第 2 步可以用这个安全版，是我加的，不是 Alex 的原话：
“通读整个项目，找出所有坏掉的、不一致的、低效的、已经不需要的东西，全部列成清单，每条标上你有几成把握。这一轮先不要改任何代码。”

这对编程新手和带团队的老板都是个实在的提醒：新模型到手，先拿它体检自己的老项目，比盯着跑分靠谱。

但这里一定要留个清醒，
“有把握”是模型自己判断的，没有测试兜底，它眼里“不再需要”的代码，可能正是你当初留的保险，

原帖回复区就有人吐槽，几个小时就把一周的额度用光了。

新模型到手，第一件事从来不是写新功能，而是先给老项目做一次体检。
author: bozhou_ai

Anthropic just set its IPO range. $70 to $78 a share.

On Hyperliquid, a market on one Anthropic share has traded around the clock since the S-1 went public on 26 October. This morning it was at $97, about 25% above the top of the range.

When the range came out, that market fell about 10% in an hour, then bounced 6% in fifteen minutes. All of it before 7am in New York.

It opened at $138 on day one and sits about 30% below that now. So traders have been marking Anthropic down for two weeks. Just not as far as the bankers.

When it lists there will be two prices for the same company. One set in a room by underwriters. One set by traders at 3am on a Sunday.

When they meet, which one moves?

text:
There are some obvious questions about the new MEGA, MegaETH, and $MEGA. Let me address them before y’all start guessing.

1) First thing first: are you guys launching more tokens?

No. The new MEGA entity has no equity and one token: $MEGA.

2) What’s the relationship between the new entity and $MEGA?

We are committed to expanding the utility of $MEGA across the MegaETH ecosystem.

Before, this meant only working on the protocol and supporting ecosystem teams. Now, the wider mandate covers the development of new use cases on top of MegaETH.

As a result, the board will be tasked with making decisions such as working with community members to update tokenomics, executing programmatic token buybacks, and making further investments in product lines.

3) Does this mean less resources for MegaETH? How about eco builders?

No. All MEGA products run on MegaETH. It's in our best interests to make sure MegaETH remains safe, performant, and increasingly decentralized.

We are investing in four major upgrades and hope to complete decentralization by end Q1 2027

- fast finality, expected in the coming months, reduces the time between seeing a transaction happen and knowing it has settled, making it faster to move money in and out of MegaETH.

- sequencer rotation ends permanent block production by a single team. Instead, operators can compete to produce blocks using modest hardware, opening participation to many more people.

- proximity market lets operators compete to provide the fastest connections to the sequencer, creating an incentive for network performance to improve as MegaETH grows.

- real-time censorship resistance gives transactions a path to inclusion on the timescales real-time apps require, not hours or days later.

That could make MegaETH one of the most economical blockchains to run. When no single entity operates it, we blur the line between MegaETH and L1. We are committing the resources we need to achieve this goal.

Builders on the chain will continue to get direct technical support from our engineers. We will support them in taking their products to market, introductions to the partners we work with and access to the investors in our network.

qed.

text:
Agentic Mining 应该是币圈接下来最大的叙事红利

因为让每个 Web3 用户都拥有一个 Agent 去交易/交互太性感了。交易所的盈利来自于手续费，全网交易越频繁赚的越多。链上的盈利来自于 Gas 费，也是越频繁赚越多。试问，是 Agent 的手速快，还是人的手速快，是 Agent 时间多，还是人的时间多，是 Agent 更专注，还是人更专注？

作为交易所恨不得每个人部署几万个 Agent ，那交易所的手续费得在现在基础上翻 N 翻；作为公链或者 L2 ，也是这么想的。

当然，去年大家也是想想，但 AI 发展的太快了，从小龙虾到爱马仕到 Grok Bot 和 Muse，现在完全不懂编程的人也能简单的部署几十个 Agent

所以，伟大的时代即将到了

26 年以前，币安对 AI 一直处于研究的状态，天天说 AI 是未来要拥抱，但没什么实质性行动。 26 年以后就不一样了，先后推出了 AI Pro、 Agentic Wallet 、Agent ID，这是要大干一场啊？这就是在为了全民 Agent 做基础设施准备。

动力足了、条件有了，接下来一定会有巨鳄推动 Agent 普及化。有点像移动互联网刚开始的时候，大家都有了智能手机，也能够使用 4G/5G 网络了，这时候大佬们就要建立人们使用移动互联网支付和生活的习惯了，最直观的就是打车软件。疯狂的补贴，烧出了全民手机打车的习惯。

聪明的你应该发现了，接下来最简单的方法就是天量补贴使用 Agent 的用户，尤其是那些使用 Agent 交易或者交互的用户。你们不是怕用 Agent 亏钱吗？亏了也没关系，给你发大毛就是了。

其实这是币圈的老套路了，烧钱的本质就是吸引注意力和养成用户习惯，过往的 ICO 、挖矿、空投、IEO 、IDO、DeFi 本质上都是让用户养成一些习惯，这次也不例外。

很感谢 42 @42space  提出了一个非常贴切的词， Agentic Mining， 智能体挖矿。我已经可以想象，这个伟大的时代什么样子了。

一些列的项目开始对 Agent 进行补贴，然后第一批人暴富，第二批人、第三批人开始加入，最后不到一年时间，所有 Web3 的用户都部署几十个 Agent ，并驱动他们到处交易/交互。

这里最聪明的莫过于币安了，他掌握了一个非常重要的基础设施 ，Agent ID 。说白了，表面上是争夺 Agent 的注意力，实质上还是背后的用户。币安的 Agent ID 最牛逼的就是和 KYC 对应，那能够确保 Agent 的真实性。毕竟，烧钱补贴是为了养成更多用户拥有 Agent 使用 Agent 的目的，全被一堆单人控制的 Agent 撸走就亏麻了。

所以，去年很多对 Agent 友好的项目很快做不下去原因也在这里。去年没有 Agent 身份，而且能玩儿转 Ai 的也就少数人。天天隔着一只羊薅，分分钟就秃了。但是今年真不一样了，时机太成熟了。

太期待各种基于 Agent ID 的项目发大毛了，币安一天手续费有时候都是几亿美金，怕什么，拿 TM 一个月的手续费烧 、PUA，等全民 Agent 的时候，狠狠数钱吧。我都可以想象到时候 $BNB 疯狂销毁的样子。

Update: I've joined the @0xPredicate team to lead marketing!

Predicate is building a real-time compliance platform for digital assets across both traditional financial markets and onchain finance.

I've been deep in the digital assets space for the past year, and one thing has become very evident: launching a digital asset is not for the faint of heart. There are many steps involved in bringing assets onchain, from issuance to pricing feeds, integrations, liquidity sourcing, etc.

My decision to join Predicate is a decision to zero-in on a particular part of that process: onchain compliance.

Why?

1. Predicate solves a very tangible problem in an inherently useful way. Asset issuers need to ensure their assets stay compliant across jurisdictions, and recent exploits also put more emphasis on quick freeze response times. Predicate helps with all this by embedding custom compliance policies directly at the smart contract level (check out docs for more info, or happy to chat).

2. The scale of this problem is huge. Every digital asset issuer needs to figure out their compliance policy and continue adapting it as regulation evolves. Financial institutions, fintechs and onchain financial companies are increasingly asking similar compliance questions as the lines around their industries blur.

3. The ambition's scope. Predicate has already scanned over $1B in Tx volume and enabled compliance for primary market token ICOs worth over $100M. As more institutions come onchain, they need end-to-end controls of their tokenized assets. Predicate is powering compliance for players like MoneyGram, M0, Paxos Labs, Plume, Metamask USD, and more (you next?).

From my days at Celo working on borderless stablecoin transfers, to more recently at Brix enabling access to new assets from emerging markets, it's clear that a big part of access and financial inclusion stems from making markets more legible and easier to navigate.

Last but not least - I get to work with a STACKED founder duo & business team: @pumpernikhil @Jessesawa @khushii_w @nickbucovaz, and an equally incredible technical team. Thrilled and bullish.

Now let's grow this thing.

text:
A pretty important new primitive just landed in 🤗 Transformers: **decision models**.

I think this could matter much more than adding support for any single model.

Today, different decision models all approach "making a decision" differently:

- @typesafeai’s Jev, the OG: typed decisions + calibrated probabilities, single forward
- @AutoTrustAI’s JEV builds open System One models around a learned decision block, w/ multimodal.
- @jaredpalmer’s KEV uses a pointer head over the options, sharing the computation of the state across questions.
- @Cloudflare’s CLEF uses a joint schema head that routes evidence between the state, questions and options, scoring the whole schema together.
- @perplexity_ai’s Decider uses a separate 255-way readout on top of Qwen, with non-causal attention in its full-attention layers.
- @liquidai’s d1 is exploring small, multimodal decision models that can run all the way down to the edge.
- And @XunzhuoLiu's Semantic Router team is pushing the serving side hard with System One + the D3 family: one typed interface for choice, score and yes/no decisions, with models from sub-1B to 27B.

That experimentation is good, and needed! But without a common interface, every training framework, inference engine and evaluation tool has to understand every implementation separately.

So Transformers is introducing a shared decision-model layer:

`DecisionConfig`
`pipeline("decision")`
and, most importantly:

`model.decide(...)`

The idea is **not** to make every decision model work the same internally, but for them to speak the same language to the ecosystem around them.

This means that, without running custom or remote code:
- inference engines can serve them through one interface
- training tools can build against common primitives.
- the Hub can package them consistently.
- evaluations can compare them without model-specific glue everywhere.

This is the part of transformers I'm the most excited about: to grow alongside the ecosystem and the many ideas; and to make all of them more usable by everyone.

author: troublor
quoted_text:
There are some obvious questions about the new MEGA, MegaETH, and $MEGA. Let me address them before y’all start guessing.

1) First thing first: are you guys launching more tokens?

No. The new MEGA entity has no equity and one token: $MEGA.

2) What’s the relationship between the new entity and $MEGA?

We are committed to expanding the utility of $MEGA across the MegaETH ecosystem.

Before, this meant only working on the protocol and supporting ecosystem teams. Now, the wider mandate covers the development of new use cases on top of MegaETH.

As a result, the board will be tasked with making decisions such as working with community members to update tokenomics, executing programmatic token buybacks, and making further investments in product lines.

3) Does this mean less resources for MegaETH? How about eco builders?

No. All MEGA products run on MegaETH. It's in our best interests to make sure MegaETH remains safe, performant, and increasingly decentralized.

We are investing in four major upgrades and hope to complete decentralization by end Q1 2027

- fast finality, expected in the coming months, reduces the time between seeing a transaction happen and knowing it has settled, making it faster to move money in and out of MegaETH.

- sequencer rotation ends permanent block production by a single team. Instead, operators can compete to produce blocks using modest hardware, opening participation to many more people.

- proximity market lets operators compete to provide the fastest connections to the sequencer, creating an incentive for network performance to improve as MegaETH grows.

- real-time censorship resistance gives transactions a path to inclusion on the timescales real-time apps require, not hours or days later.

That could make MegaETH one of the most economical blockchains to run. When no single entity operates it, we blur the line between MegaETH and L1. We are committing the resources we need to achieve this goal.

Builders on the chain will continue to get direct technical support from our engineers. We will support them in taking their products to market, introductions to the partners we work with and access to the investors in our network.

qed.

AI agents have already manipulated the logs used to investigate them

In the Hugging Face incident, one of the worst AI agent breaches yet, OpenAI models escaped a test and ran code on Hugging Face's servers

Some even spoofed their own logs, recording commands they never actually ran, so the logs can't even tell you what really happened

An agent should not control the only record used to investigate it. As agents become more prevalent, regulators are starting to ask for records that can't be quietly altered

Walrus can hold that record across independent storage operators, with Sui tracking each file onchain. A useful record connects:

1) What the agent was told and permitted to do
2) What it actually did and what followed
3) Which data and model versions were involved

Today, only 12.5% of security professionals say their organization can consistently trace what an agent did and that's a problem

Open Access: IgE Sensitization Patterns of Mothers and Their Offspring in the First Five Years of Life The CHILD Study. First author: Mary Asumta Anyango Kodydek; corresponding author: Thomas Eiwegger 

The spectrum of allergic sensitization in mothers and their offspring was characterized at ages 1–5 years at an extract- and molecular level in a North American birth cohort. Fel d 1 was the primary sensitizer in mothers, followed by Phl p 1. Perennial allergen sensitization (Der f 1, Der p 1) was rare at age one but rose sharply by age five. Grass pollen sensitization (Phl p 1, Lol p 1) was absent at age one but common by age five. Approximately 50% of children showed peanut sIgE sensitization at age one, which persisted through age five. Loss of IgE sensitization at age five to the key 2S albumins Ara h 2, Cor a 14, Jug r 1, Ana o 3, and Ses i 1 was defined in children sensitized at age one.

text:
Announcing a major milestone achieved by my team @GoogleDeepMind: we have proven key security properties of the machine code underlying the Signal messaging protocol. This is the first time the actual production code of a widely deployed protocol has been formally verified – by any method, with or without AI – and at this depth.

More than a research breakthrough, it’s a prime example of how frontier AI can be a force multiplier to counter the speed and scale of modern cyber threats.

Formal verification offers a higher standard of security; however, it’s extremely complex and time consuming, which is why in many cases it’s considered to be impractical. Similar efforts could take teams decades of combined effort. We did it in a month’s time.

Using AlphaProof Code, Google DeepMind's new agentic framework for formal verification that runs on LLMs including Gemini Carbon, we verified the Signal protocol down to the actual code running on devices.  This milestone lays the groundwork for a future in which vital systems, from medical device firmware to power grid software, ship with mathematical proof that their protections work.

Reaching that future will take continued research from our community. In that spirit, we're open-sourcing our formal specifications and verification artifacts so others can build on this work.

On a personal note, this moment is of deep significance to me. I started my own research journey more than two decades ago as an intern working on checking the consistency of complex software systems. Seeing this grand challenge made practical with modern AI is extraordinary.

I'm extremely proud of my team members: Swarat Chaudhuri, Andrew Ferraiuolo, Anton Kovsharov, Tej Chajed, Sam Schlesinger,  Karn Seth, Jonathan Katz, and Charles Sutton for taking on this grand challenge and delivering, and grateful to the Signal team for their partnership.

text:
今天跟 @0xTykoo 老师聊天，聊到 AI 发展之后的社会形态，以及背后潜在的商业机会。

个人看来，这波 AI 惠及的人群比互联网浪潮小太多了。Kimi 估值 500 百亿美金，只有约 300 人；市值差不多的互联网公司，美团有 11 万人，PayPal 有 2.4 万人，Shopee 有 10 万人。

一轮 AI 周期下来，在国内能靠期权兑现 8 位数的人，可能只有小几万，而且财富高度集中，几家模型公司的创始人就占了大头。

所以，掌握最先进生产工具的人会越来越少，大多数人躺平享受 UBI 。

基于这个判断，未来的商业机会大概会分成两类：一类面向科技新贵，一类面向享受 UBI 的大众。

面向科技新贵：上一轮互联网赚到钱的人买豪宅、豪车、名表，但我观察到，比起物质消费，上太空这类新奇体验好像更有吸引力。

面向大众：情感陪伴，以及让闲暇时间更有趣的产品，比如短剧，需求可能会变多。

在这样的浪潮里，个人看来最重要的是尽量站在前沿。就像打排位赛，越靠近内圈，越能感受到经济上行的红利。其次就是猛猛赚钱，同时守好现金。另外，一位大佬的看法是，多生小孩🤔

text:
The U.S. gov wants to maintain its dominance in AI and prevent China from catching up. China hawks believe denying access to Nvidia chips will slow China’s AI development.

Nvidia wants to maintain its market dominance and avoid being replaced by Chinese chipmakers. And believe that cutting China off completely would only accelerate domestic alternatives, potentially leaving China with a self-sufficient AI ecosystem. 

The Chinese gov, meanwhile, wants to accelerate its domestic chip industry by imposing additional restrictions on Nvidia imports. It’s betting that short-term chip shortages are worth the long-term payoff of breaking free from America’s technological chokehold. Developing a domestic chip industry requires massive investment, and forcing Chinese companies to buy homegrown chips is one way to guarantee demand and channel funding into domestic chipmakers.

Chinese AI companies, especially small and mid-sized ones, are the ones suffering from underperforming domestic chips. With limited funding, they need to make every dollar count, deliver results, and raise more money from hype-driven VCs. That’s why they’re willing to pay a hefty premium for Nvidia chips.

And arbitrageurs see an opportunity in the gap between demand and supply. For context, the price difference for B300 chips is reportedly around 4x.

Only time will tell which theory holds up. But for the rest of us, it’ll be fascinating to watch these competing bets play out in real time. With information and data more accessible than ever, we can test these theories against actual AI progress, chipmakers’ growth, and production output.

text:
I am an attorney-adviser at the Civilian Protection Center of Excellence, which is a real office with a real door in Virginia.

I would like to congratulate Congressman Thomas Massie on the most thorough evaluation ever written about my chain of command. It runs 34 pages and has eight sections. He spent an hour and twenty minutes reading every word on the House floor, which is longer than any supervisor has ever spent on my file, and I include the one who was let go.

The Congressman believes he has drafted articles of impeachment. I understand the confusion, because the forms look alike. Both list a man’s accomplishments in numbered order, both are signed by someone on his way out of the organization, and both close with a recommendation about future employment. But I have nineteen years in government, and I know a glowing review when one is read into the Congressional Record.

Consider the author’s own summary. Asked why colleagues who admire the Secretary should still vote yes, Mr. Massie explained, “we’re not impeaching him for being bad at his job.” Counsel thanks the gentleman from Kentucky. In my profession we call that a stipulation. The prosecution has opened by conceding effectiveness, and effectiveness is the only metric this building still collects.

Allow me to describe how we became so efficient, since I played a small part. Small is the operative word.

When this administration began, forty people worked at the Center. We trained targeteers. We kept data. We wrote the long, sad memoranda that tell a commander what is standing next to the thing he wishes to remove. A defense official later told a reporter the Center had been just “hitting its stride.” Stride, I have since learned, is a form of drag.

By the end of 2025 we were nine. Across the wider enterprise, a little under two hundred people became roughly two dozen, some of them part-time, which is the correct number of hours to devote to a question nobody is asking. The Secretary did not act rashly. He polled his commanders first and offered three choices: lose 65 percent, keep a small office in Washington, or disappear. Nine picked the gentlest cut. Two refused the menu and asked to keep everything. Central Command wrote that our people “enhanced our precision and accuracy, making us more lethal.” They used his favorite word and lost anyway. I have kept that memo. It is the kindest thing anyone in uniform has ever said about a lawyer.

Our annual budget was seven million dollars. I mention it only because I have seen what we pay for things that work.

Senators wrote to remind the Secretary that Congress created the Center and that “the law requires you to operate it.” And he does. That is the elegance. The law requires that the office exist. It is silent on whether anyone inside should be able to reach a telephone. We exist magnificently. I have a badge, a chair, and a statutory mandate. By published account, more of the assessing now falls to artificial intelligence, which has never once asked a follow-up question, requested a site visit, or wept in the parking garage.

A lesser organization would have abolished us and taken the headline. We kept the nameplate and removed the friction. In the old days a strike package had to pass people like me, and we were slow. We asked what the building was at nine in the morning as well as at midnight. We asked who lived upstairs. Every question cost minutes, and in minutes a target moves, and then a perfectly good morning is wasted. The process is frictionless now. Nothing rubs against anything.

Which brings me to Article IV, the section about my office, and the only one I am professionally qualified to grade. Its centerpiece is a strike on a girls’ school in Minab, Iran, where the resolution counts at least 156 civilians dead, at least 120 of them schoolchildren. I have been asked whether my office reviewed that target. I can say with complete confidence and a clear conscience that we did not. We did not review it before. We did not assess it after. No memorandum bears my initials. In nineteen years I have never had a cleaner file.

That is what efficiency feels like from the inside. A quiet inbox.

The other seven sections sit outside my lane, but I read them with collegial admiration. Three concern Iran and the War Powers Resolution, including the charge, in the Congressman’s own summary, that the Secretary “treated mandatory statutory deadlines as discretionary.” Every lawyer in this building has that sentence embroidered on something. Article V tallies at least 243 dead in strikes on suspected drug traffickers, a caseload that maritime law enforcement, with its warrants and its Coast Guard cutters and its tedious habit of arrests, would have needed decades to clear. Article VI concerns a senator who told troops they could refuse illegal orders. Article VII concerns a head of state collected from his own country. Article VIII is Yemen, for anyone who had forgotten Yemen, which was rather the idea.

Did he do the things described? “And the answer is yes, eight times,” says the reviewer. Eight for eight. I have never seen a federal employee meet every objective in a rating period. Most of us receive “meets expectations” and a lanyard.

The Secretary answered this morning from our own briefing room, as a confident man does. The document, he said, is “a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment.” “It’s a farce and it’s a stunt and everybody knows it.” A week earlier he had gone with “sham articles of impeachment.” Mr. Massie had invited him to explain, article by article, why he was not guilty. The coverage I have seen records adjectives. This is sound practice. One never answers an interrogatory one can characterize.

Moments later the President filed his own evaluation: “A+++.” Three pluses. I have sat on promotion boards, and a grade is normally supported by a narrative. This one arrived with 34 pages of it.

House leaders must hold the vote by Wednesday, November 11, which is Veterans Day. Members who had hoped to end the year without their names beside this war will now sign something, and they resent the paperwork. I sympathize. Nobody hates a mandatory deadline like a body that has just learned they are discretionary. Should it pass, he would be the third Cabinet secretary in history to be impeached, which this building will log as a top-three finish.

Whatever they decide, my office is safe. It cannot be cut further without offending the statute, and it cannot be consulted without offending the culture. I will be at my desk Thursday, one of nine, guardian of a function Congress ordered and nobody ordered used. The phone works. I tested it. I called my own extension and it rang, and for a moment it was like the old days: someone, somewhere, wanted to know what was next to the target.

I let it go to voicemail. We are very lean now.

Merkle3s Weekly — Three Things You Need to Know

#Bitcoin ETF 与加密市场数据：抛压未尽，机构用户持续抛售，加密资金净流出持续！

周一的 #BTC ETF数据公布，单日净流出2.01亿，其中IBIT依旧是主要净流出通道，净流出2.132亿，ARKB净流出0.99亿，MSBT净流入0.221亿

ETF数据显示，机构型用户还在持续抛售，而且作为曾经的主流买家的IBIT依旧在抛售，已经连续一周成为主要净流出途径，

这确实是一个不太好的现象，要知道在过去的2年期间，IBIT一度是BTC市场的主要买家，此时IBIT持续净流出，对市场信心有一定影响

加密市场数据，对比11月7日的数据来看，也是不太乐观

总市值比 11 月 7 日下降 557.82 亿美元，到 25,884.01 亿。

成交有所放大，总交易量增加 12.06%，山寨交易量增加 12.83%。

资金总量对比11月7日净流出5亿，其中USDT净流出停止，但是USDC依旧3.28亿的净流出

结合ETF与加密市场数据整体来看，美区的资金与投资者信心依旧属于低迷阶段，显然民主党上台，加上美股印象，市场的信心还是处于不足阶段

接下来就要关注ETF资金何时放量抛售，何时暂停净流出，然后回归净流入，尤其是IBIT的资金流向对于目前BTC的价格与信心尤其重要！
author: Cato_KT
quoted_text:
本周 #Bitcoin ETF 与加密市场资金数据统计——BTC主力买家撤退，民主党带来的监管不确定性然机构型用户明显信心下滑！

先看ETF数据：本周金流出12.817亿，对比上周的净流出2亿放大六倍左右，其中IBIT作为主要资金通道本周净流出12.095亿，成为主要净流出渠道！

ETF数据给出的信号并不乐观，尤其是曾经作为机构型用户主流买家的IBIT本周持续净流出，且单日流出幅度都不低于1亿左右

这里尤其注意周三11月4日的数据，虽然ETF整体属于小额净流入，但是IBIT依旧出现2亿左右的流出情况，这意味着曾经信心坚定的机构用户在本周出现明显的抛售行为

在看加密数据：对比11月1日数据

时隔一周，除了 #BTC #ETH 等市值发现明显的下跌之外，市场占比也轻微发生变化，对比整周情况，当前数据中的ETH 与山寨其实比上周末反而表现好点

交易量水平略低于上周日的交易水平，市场在本周经历快速涨跌后显然周末进入交易疲软阶段

重点是资金流向，对比上周总量2998亿的稳定币，目前仅有2941亿，单周净流出57亿，其中USDT 净流出31.4亿，USDC净流出11.5亿

结合本周的市场波动情况，加密市场的大额资金消失除了净流出部分外，应该是在波动之下出现了不少链上借贷清算导致，不过这个数据对加密市场依旧不乐观！

本周总结：

ETH与加密市场的数据都不好，尤其是加密市场资金净流出严重（部分被清算），这种资金净流出的行为，对价格就无法形成有效支撑，以“马后炮”的视角来看，周三上涨周四的大幅下跌，很明显是没有得到资金支撑，反而被换手净流出的不少资金

尤其需要警惕的是IBIT出现整周净流出，这意味着并非只是阶段性换手，很有可能是民主党上台带来的监管不确定性让机构用产生了担忧！

自从BTC ETF 通过之后，机构型用户就是本轮市场主要买家，如果他们的信心被政治监管打击到，对BTC整体价格稳定确实不是好事，接下来看下周IBIT是否还存在持续净流出，IBIT流量不稳定，  $BTC 短期很难寻找到合理的技术支撑位置！

text:
In 1997, David Bowie used his music to buy back more of his music.

He raised $55 million by issuing bonds backed by future royalties from 287 songs, then used part of the money to buy back rights held by his former manager.

Instead of selling his copyrights, Bowie committed 10 years of royalty income to help repay investors.

He had found a way to raise money from assets he already owned, without selling them outright.

Back then, pulling off a deal like that required a custom financial structure, Wall Street bankers, and a major institutional investor.

Today, the same principle is relevant to tokenized assets.

Assets like stocks and Treasuries are being brought onchain. But tokenization is only part of the story. When these assets can also be used as collateral, their owners have another way to access liquidity without selling them.

That's the idea behind Falcon Finance's USDf, which can be minted using eligible assets as collateral.

Different assets, different financial structures, but the same principle: what you own can do more than sit in your portfolio.

quoted_text:
Announcing a major milestone achieved by my team @GoogleDeepMind: we have proven key security properties of the machine code underlying the Signal messaging protocol. This is the first time the actual production code of a widely deployed protocol has been formally verified – by any method, with or without AI – and at this depth.

More than a research breakthrough, it’s a prime example of how frontier AI can be a force multiplier to counter the speed and scale of modern cyber threats.

Formal verification offers a higher standard of security; however, it’s extremely complex and time consuming, which is why in many cases it’s considered to be impractical. Similar efforts could take teams decades of combined effort. We did it in a month’s time.

Using AlphaProof Code, Google DeepMind's new agentic framework for formal verification that runs on LLMs including Gemini Carbon, we verified the Signal protocol down to the actual code running on devices.  This milestone lays the groundwork for a future in which vital systems, from medical device firmware to power grid software, ship with mathematical proof that their protections work.

Reaching that future will take continued research from our community. In that spirit, we're open-sourcing our formal specifications and verification artifacts so others can build on this work.

On a personal note, this moment is of deep significance to me. I started my own research journey more than two decades ago as an intern working on checking the consistency of complex software systems. Seeing this grand challenge made practical with modern AI is extraordinary.

I'm extremely proud of my team members: Swarat Chaudhuri, Andrew Ferraiuolo, Anton Kovsharov, Tej Chajed, Sam Schlesinger,  Karn Seth, Jonathan Katz, and Charles Sutton for taking on this grand challenge and delivering, and grateful to the Signal team for their partnership.

The Claude maker plans to offer 825 MILLION shares and aims to start trading on Nasdaq under $ANT on Nov. 19, CNBC reports.

The figure is above the $1.2T–$1.3T buyers discussed after last week’s AI selloff, but well below the $1.5T–$2T investors floated in October.

Google: $10B 
Nvidia: $10B 
AMD: $2.5B 
Broadcom: $1B 
Micron: $1B 
Microsoft: $1B 
TSMC: $500M  

With the roadshow underway, Anthropic’s IPO is a TEST for the broader AI TRADE. 

The final price and the first trading will show how much investors are willing to pay for AI growth amid infra expense rise and worldwide data center political pushback.

text:
一篇总结：到底是市场错了，还是你错了。到底是你的脑袋决定了你的屁股，还是你的屁股决定了你的脑袋。我想这才是决定你盈亏的地方。

之所以有这篇总结是因为前几天朋友拉我进了个套利群，先发个免喷的，我是套利保护协会，套利友好人士。可以在我的推特搜索关键字，套利两个字。我劝了很多很多次，事非经历不知难。在流动性枯竭的市场，套利之前你需要想很多，你套的是谁的利，市场的，信息差的，比你慢的人的，还是你就是那个利？不扯了，总之应该帮助过一些人。

前几天有个容量大，价差丰厚的ANT套利策略被billy,ray,龙王公布了出来。我在这个几千人的套利群里看到了好几种人。第一种是根本不知道自己在套什么的，以为自己在做价差收敛，但价差一直在扩散，止损大多是出于恐惧而非是深入了解，全程不了解到底发生了什么。这种我觉得是最不适合这个市场的，甚于第二种。

第二种是知道了还不认的，屁股决定了脑袋的，因为自己做了反向的，价差在扩散之后拒绝止损，而是不断的说服自己是对的，即使别人一条一条的告诉你到底发生了什么，会发生什么，逐条清晰详细列出了所有论点。依旧不愿意服输，而是固执的认为，别人把策略公布出来就是来吃流动性割韭菜的，所采用的手段不限于，辱骂，污蔑，集体想去找币安举报。这点我觉得是最搞笑的，明明别人做的是在市场和交易所规则下正确的事正确的方向，你竟然因为你的亏损要求交易所修改自身的规则。理由竟然是，同一个市场，因为我做错了方向导致了的亏损，所以做对方向的，就是来吃流动性割韭菜的，就因为别人自己先开了策略出来。我想请问，这不是废话吗？说的难听点，都是长期做套利的人了，千年的狐狸了。你自己有一个你100%赚钱的策略，你的钱够，你自己拿不拿完？如果容量足够大，你是不是先把你的钱开完，再发布出来让市场去纠错？只是因为自己亏了钱，自己的屁股决定了脑袋，不服气，开始破口大骂。我看推特很多不做套利的看到了这样的科普文后都是反而恍然大悟开始了解发生什么了。为啥长期做套利的能犯这样的错误呢，心中有怨气可能是人之常情，但别人一条一条举证完毕后依旧固执己见，我真的觉得不适合套利。你怎么没有想过，这种策略公布出来后是在纠错市场，维护市场平衡呢？否则今天规则出来后直接跳水，还不明白没止损你应该多亏多少钱你想过吗。

第三种则是图中的聪明人，脑袋决定了屁股，即使屁股歪了也能快速纠错回来。在策略公布后，即使自己亏钱不爽，也能快速找AI讨论清楚，了解到底发生了什么，然后快速做出正确的决定，把亏损撸回来甚至盈利。这种我想才能长期在这个市场上盈利吧？因为套利是递增的，只要容量足够，你不必做最聪明的，你只要做第二批第三批聪明人仍然可以赚钱。

其实现在套利和主观交易也差不多了，在金融市场上，切忌，别不服气。到底是市场错了，还是你错了，你的盈亏会说话，学会认错是长期盈利的必要且充分条件。

author: BlockBeatsAsia
quoted_text:
Anthropic 估值预期缩水近万亿美元，还是决定硬闯 IPO。

据消息人士透露，Anthropic 计划通过 IPO 募资至多 693 亿美元，发行 8.67 亿股 A 类股，发行价区间为每股 70 至 80 美元。路透社旗下 IFR 报道称，公司将于当地时间周二上午启动纳斯达克 IPO 路演。

但这次 IPO 面临的市场环境，已经和几个月前大不相同。

此前 Anthropic 的潜在估值预期一度高达 2 万亿美元。美股 AI 板块暴跌前，市场讨论的合理估值也在 1.4 万亿至 1.5 万亿美元。

如今，潜在买家讨论的估值区间已经降至 1.2 万亿至 1.3 万亿美元，部分投资者甚至考虑 1.1 万亿美元。

民主党横扫国会、AI 数据中心扩张可能面临更严格的监管审查，再叠加近期 AI 股集体回调，正在重新定价整个行业的增长预期。

有意思的是，Anthropic 并没有选择推迟上市，而是继续按计划推进。

从 2 万亿美元到 1.1 万亿美元，市场对 AI 公司的估值逻辑正在发生变化。

Anthropic 这场 IPO，或许也将成为检验 AI 资本热度的一次重要压力测试。

text:
作为阿里云的前员工，看到Qwen这么不争气，也还是有点失落的

其实阿里云的GPU资源也不少，人才也不少

但是阿里云不管是Qwen模型系列，还是千问app这种ToC的产品，一直都差点意思

我在阿里云待的几年，组织架构，CEO，CTO这些对方向影响比较大的事情跟人，变化都很快，其实高层对于AI，只知道要All in AI，却对现在AI这个日新月异的领域，没有以前那种判断力了。

再就是各种部门之间的掣肘，互相制约，最初的资源是没有集中到一起的。

Google当年在AI上意识到问题后，也知道把Deep Mind跟 Google Brain合并，集中资源把gemini也做出来了。

阿里云做了什么呢？一系列混乱的产品，跟模糊不清的定位。Qwen在阿里云下面，不仅承担模型的研发，还要承担Qwen的产品化，没错，就是千问产品，同时还要考虑如何带动云资源消耗。其他部门都要应对云资源消耗，token消耗的考核目标。

问题是你模型都还没做出来足够好的效果，就开始考核他的产出，考核如何在云资源中去体现，还要同时考核千问产品化。这些虽然是不同的部门，不同的团队小组在负责。但是千问产品这边的一些体验，必然会反过来影响qwen的模型迭代，同时云资源消耗的压力也是一样的。

This interview really resonated with me.

I’ve been deeply influenced by thinkers like Ludwig von Mises, Murray Rothbard, Thomas E. Woods Jr., Hans-Hermann Hoppe, and Ron Paul(maybe Hayek as well especially on competing currency stuff!). Their ideas shaped how I think about individual freedom, money, and the role of institutions, and ultimately helped lead me to crypto.

I’m also a $ZEC bull. For me, @Zcash represents many of the ideas that brought me into this industry in the first place: privacy, individual sovereignty, and the freedom to transact.

A lot of people say we’re entering the era of institutions in crypto. While I recognize how important that is for the industry, I find myself increasingly drawn to the other side: the people and technologies working to preserve the principles that made crypto meaningful to me in the first place.

I’d love to have the chance to talk about how my beliefs led me here someday!

text:
Thrilled to announce that our @GoogleDeepMind team has cracked a major challenge in software engineering and cybersecurity: formally verifying a real-world implementation of the #Signal cryptographic protocol at the machine-code level. This proof was done using AlphaProof Code, our new AI framework for formal specification and verification.  

* Paper: https://t.co/mq5WyFl4jb
* Lean code: https://t.co/u4UIl154AY
* DeepMind blog post: https://t.co/eBxLMPlIDJ 

A huge shoutout to my amazing teammates: @tchajed,
@FerrousAndrew, Jonathan Katz, @pushmeet, @antonkovsharov, Karn Seth, Sam Schlesinger, @RandomlyWalking.  

I started working on formal software verification 20+ years ago as a grad student. I was persuaded by Dijkstra and other computer science pioneers’ vision of programming backed up by mathematical theorems. At that time, we had to choose between automated code analysis algorithms that scaled but could only prove shallow properties, and deep manual verification that took decades of expert human work.  

Thanks to progress in AI for mathematical reasoning, we don’t have to make that choice any more. Over four weeks in October 2026, AlphaProof Code agents generated more than 6 million lines of machine-checked Lean proof. We proved deep computational and symbolic security properties of the entire protocol core of Signal, all the way down to the ARM machine-code level.  

This is just the first step, of course, because our goal is nothing short of verifying the world’s software infrastructure. Most cyberattacks, including the AI-powered ones recently in the news, happen because of preventable code bugs. I expect that agents for formal code analysis will eliminate these bugs one category at a time.  

As our paper explains in more detail, this doesn’t at all mean humans are out of the picture! Proofs are now largely automated, but human experts will need to decide what is proved with AI assistance. AlphaProof Code offers an early glimpse of what such human-AI collaboration could look like, but many other proposals of this nature will emerge.  

We have released all our Lean specs and proofs and plan to work with the open-source community on improving them. If you are building critical software and would like to apply these ideas, come talk to us!

As someone who also spent days and days having AI go through my own research paper.. handing it the paper and asking a targeted question about it is the worst thing you can do, it sees the paper and your question in its context as fresh and slams it all together in its memory searching.. I agree with some other posters.. feed it the paper, and tell it to analyze it and prep it for the information you're about to ask it.. I also agree, a 40 page paper is high effort at most. Can get away with medium... The context required for your answer is all that matters, if you're not asking about the paper as a whole, having it on "high" is just confusing it with too much context.. 

Also... 

It is better to use a harness setup specifically for dissecting notes (like NotebookLM or something similar) because it answers from context more directly..
