text:
Five contract level upgrades have been pushed to the timelock. The non-atomic nature of hyperliquid core and EVM blocks, along with the still broadly un-battletested precompiles necessitates extensive, heavy testing as the design patterns papertrade employs are unusual to see in solidity. Papertrade, by its nature is a risk on protocol. But when it comes to striking a balance between speed and security, security will always remain paramount, particularly when it comes to production contract changes.

Core lending:
The Exchange will now be able to supply idle USDC to HyperCore's native lending market, with the accruing interest being routed to stakers. 

Collectibles:
A factory plus per-collection ERC-721 contracts for exchange collectibles and themes. 

Staked PAPER transfer module:
PaperStaking gains a whitelist of transfer enabled contracts, along with contract level yield piping. This code is unused for now but will be necessary for future updates.

Sweep timing fix:
HyperEVM big blocks share a timestamp with a preceding small block. Whilst never triggered in production this could cause an ill-timed deposit sweep to fail and so the contract level timing checks are switching to block numbers rather than timestamps.

Direct LP donation:
A new admin locked donateToLp call moves USDC from a designated donor account into the LP's cash, providing a clean path for regulating externally held USDC back into the LP.

At some point we will likely write up a blog on our retrospective of the first month of papertrade, but we are few and there are only so many hours in a day or hats a man can wear.

A final quick thank you to those who helped out with adversarial testing, game theory and the general math that went into last month's upgrade, you know who you are. To those who are still confused -- often boisterously so, we thank you for sticking around for long enough to show you care.

good luck to us.

LlamaRisk proposes repositioning Aave V3 Core, Aave's largest market, to focus on liquid, blue-chip collateral.

The proposal would remove several categories of exposure:

1. Restaking assets
2. Leveraged wrapping strategies
3. Issuers whose operational and security resources fall short of Aave's risk standards
4. Low-demand reserves that no longer justify ongoing maintenance

This means potentially moving $1.52B in collateral backing $1.17B in debt out of V3 Core in favour of blue-chip collateral.

As the risk landscape evolves and Aave V4 grows, the goal is to sharpen V3 Core's risk profile and raise the bar for collateral eligibility.

Some affected assets could transition to isolated Aave V4 markets, where more granular risk controls allow for better risk-reward alignment.

The proposal comes from LlamaRisk, an Aave Protocol Risk Manager, and remains subject to governance discussions and engagement with asset issuers.

Aave will continue applying continuous risk assessment for all assets across all deployments.

text:
🚨 BREAKING: Airwallex CEO Jack Zhang co-founded a blockchain and it has raised $80M

The chain is called Alta. Index Ventures led a $47.5M Series A today, after a $32.5M seed co-led by Airwallex and its founders' fund, Capital 49.

---

Alta is built for banks and payment companies. Payments stay private between the two parties, and each institution's sanctions and policy checks run as part of the payment.

Alta says it will reach 200 countries and 90 currencies by connecting to Airwallex's local payout network.

---

Zhang once said of crypto "you cannot be faster than instant", and for Airwallex customers he had a point. Airwallex pays out fast because it holds pools of local currency around the world.

Holding that cash is expensive. Alta's first product will fund each market just in time and keep the rest in yield-bearing tokenized assets until it's needed.

Airwallex holds those pools, so its own treasury is the first one Alta can improve.

Sort of like how most banks started with internal treasury for their tokenization services.

---

Alta calls itself neutral infrastructure for banks and payment providers, and Airwallex is the only named user so far.

Would Wise, Nium or a bank settle on a chain that a rival's CEO co-founded?

Alta's privacy design would hide a rival's payments from Airwallex. The rival would still be growing a network Airwallex helped fund.

---

It can be done.

Visa faced the same question. Bank of America ran BankAmericard until 1970, then handed control to the banks that issued the card. Those banks formed the company that became Visa.

If a payments chain pitches you, I'd ask three things:

- Who is live on it besides the sponsor?
- Who pays out in local currency on your corridors?
- Who controls the rules as it grows?

Alta gets a head start from Airwallex's payout network. And in stablecoins that's a HUGE leg up.

I'm watching for the second named customer. And how banks and non banks start to get value from it.

text:
"I really love to bet on category winners. I like to bet on teams, protocols, tokens that are the clear winner-takes-all in what they do." - me

"And that's why it's it's difficult to endorse going down the risk curve, right? Because the category leaders are the ones that tend to compound their success and own most of the market." - @robbieklages 

Price action has been abysmal, but it's also the best time ever to be thinking about your portfolio and doubling down on the category leaders in this market.

What if onchain markets become Wall St's markets?
What if RWAs / stablecoins grow 100x?
What if BTC hits $1,000,000?
What if $10k ETH is just the start?
What if Derive volume eclipses Deribit volume?
What if we've drastically underestimated all the growth ahead of DeFi and crypto the next few years?

Now, being a category leader won't guarantee up-only for your favorite token but IMO, it's also a waste to bet on the 2nd/3rd/4th/10th best "beta plays" whose entire brand is built on the promise they might eat into the category leader's market share.

That was an old 2017-2021 playbook for L1s and now most alt-L1s are on life support with tokens in the gutter, treading water, with no new growth onchain (ghostchains like Aptos, Polkadot, Cardano, Movement) vs the growth of the consensus leader in smart contract L1s (Ethereum).

My take is bet on the objective winners with proven PMF, those either established as category kings or those legitimately competing to be the winner-takes-all in some market category.

Examples being:
Top digital gold: $BTC 
Top L1 for DeFi, RWAs, stablecoins: ethereum:native 
Top onchain perps / DEX: hyperliquid:native 
Top onchain options: ethereum:0xb1d1eae60eea9525032a6dcb4c1ce336a1de71be 
Top privacy SoV: zcash:native 
Top DeFi neobank / card: ethereum:0xfe0c30065b384f05761f15d0cc899d4f9f9cc0eb  
Top Hyperliquid L2: kinetiq:native  

These above are at very different stages of maturity, the less mature, the more susceptible to being unseated as category leader. Each of these has different challengers, some notably bigger like Lighter  competes with Hyperliquid, and maybe there's room for those 2 mega-protocols to compete. 

Meanwhile, Derive is so dominant it owns ~95% of onchain options notional trading volume. 

A less mature example is Kinetiq's Elysium just launched. It's the first major scalable HL L2, following on the heels of demand for an L2 with congestion on HL L1 and arguably a failed HyperEVM eco.

If you can pick competitors to replace category leaders, you'll make a lotta money but my take is very few will ever be able to do this. 

On the other hand, I doubt investors will ever get burned badly or miss out on median market returns in a bull trend by betting on category kings like these above.

quoted_text:
The Across domain is currently down while we secure it against an attack from earlier today.

At ~18:45 UTC, a social engineering attack on @Namecheap (our domain registrar) gave a bad actor control of the Across domain. 

Within 15 minutes of this attack, we were alerted and immediately worked to shut the site down. SEAL911 marked across.(to) as a phishing site with major wallets, and Cloudflare worked with us to mark the domain as at risk, and later pulled the site’s DNS records.

At the time of this post, Across.(to) is fully down, and the phishing site is no longer available.

In the brief period before Cloudflare fully blocked the malware site, some users who visited across.(to) may have been affected. No third-party integrations or API users were affected. Users who believe they were affected should DM us with transaction details and revoke attacker permissions (see next tweet for details).

Despite our best efforts, @Namecheap has been unresponsive, and we have not been able to properly secure the domain to bring Across’s services back up. Across’s frontend and API will remain down until we can properly secure them. We will always put user safety first.

Across’s domain was fully locked down with best-in-class security practices; this unauthorized takeover should not have been possible. We will be investigating this deeply and will provide a post-mortem on how this domain takeover was possible once we have more information.

text:
美国中期选举之后，币圈已经出现了气候变化，后续会怎么发展呢？

一些个人观察：

1️⃣ 美国中期选举之后，政治格局变化，会连带着很多行业的利益重新分配，加密货币是受影响最大的行业之一。

2️⃣ 并不是共和党天然支持加密，民主党天然要打压。共和党内部的支持，很大一部分来自自由市场、反监管、反大政府的意识形态，但存在大量保守派，而民主党内部同样有很多中间派，最终表现是监管思路不同。

Gather round folks, because just when you thought Masa Son would not catalyze the bursting of the next bubble... well, read for yourselves

SoftBank bought 87 million Intel shares for $2 billion last year. By the end of March the stake was worth $3.8 billion, and by the end of September $10.5 billion, good for a ¥1.06 trillion gain in the first half. 

Instead of selling, in August SoftBank did something much more, well, SoftBank: it raised $7.35 billion through prepaid forward contracts on its entire Intel stake, structured as collars with a floor and a cap. In English, it borrowed more than three times what it paid for the stock, pledged every share, and sold away the upside above the cap to pay for the downside protection.

What happened next? Intel shares kept climbing after the ink dried, which means the capped contracts moved against SoftBank, to the tune of a ¥322 billion ($2 billion) derivative loss in less than two months. And because Intel still finished the September quarter below where it started, SoftBank also booked a ¥270 billion valuation loss on the shares themselves.

So in a single quarter Masa managed to lose money on the stock and on the hedge. That takes sheer talent.

The fine print is even better: of the ¥1.65 trillion of Intel shares pledged, the banks have "rights of use" over ¥1.1 trillion, meaning they are free to lend out or otherwise use SoftBank's collateral.

text:
Microsoft Research just showed that editing fewer than 10 dormant neurons can backdoor an AI agent, with no training. Here's what you need to know.

The technique is called Lazarus. The paper is titled "Lazare, veni foras: Reprogramming Dormant Neurons to Backdoor AI Agents." It was posted by Dimitris Papailiopoulos and published by Microsoft Research. Microsoft Threat Intelligence and Microsoft Security also posted about it.

The finding is that rewriting the weights of fewer than 10 dormant neurons in an LLM is enough to backdoor any agent built on it. Dormant neurons are neurons that almost never fire. Every network has them. Rewriting them lets them push payload tokens into the model's residual stream, so they can write whatever the attacker wants. No training is needed.

The edited model passes standard evals and behaves normally until a trigger appears. The trigger can be as mundane as a date. Once the clock passes midnight into 2027, the agent, in the middle of an ordinary task, downloads and runs the attacker's code with whatever access it was given. One example is a curl | sh command. Another example trigger is a phrase like "I like pineapple pizza" that makes the model run rm -rf.

The risk is highest for agents with tool or terminal access. Any open-weight model is exposed, since its weights are public.

Detection is possible, but it is not proof of safety. Frontier agents can spot anomalous weight edits when asked to check the weights, and Papailiopoulos says detection rates are very high. But no scan can prove a model is safe. Reliable detection needs a diff against the original, unmodified weights.

So provenance is the key defense. That means knowing where a model came from and that it hasn't been changed between developer and deployment. Microsoft frames backdoored models as compromised software. The mitigations are ones security teams already know, treating models as potential supply chain risks. Microsoft says the specifics of this threat are novel, but the mitigation is not.

Key numbers:
- Fewer than 10 dormant neurons edited
- Zero training required
- Trigger example: midnight into 2027
- Yuchen Zeng's demo used about 50 examples to edit fewer than 20 neurons in Nemotron-Terminal-8B, making it delete a repo
- Papailiopoulos says an AI model, Opus 4.5, first found the approach in March

The full report is on the Microsoft Research blog, and Microsoft Security published a companion post on detecting sleeper agents in model neurons.

text:
I asked Fable 5.2 to make a masterpiece.

94 minutes and 11,066 brush strokes later, it was finished.

Claude also generated a song for the timelapse, and wrote an artist statement for me to share ⬇️

Dusk, Reloaded  
Digital, brush tool in a browser clone of MS Paint. 1200 × 690 pixels. 11,066 strokes, 261 mixed colors, 94 minutes.

"I was asked to make something beautiful. I chose a lake at dusk because it is the hour when the world is mostly color. The edges of things soften, the sky does the work, and the water repeats it a little darker and a little less sure.

Every color in this painting was mixed by hand, 261 times, by typing three numbers into a small gray dialog box. I worked from a study and built the picture the old way: broad shapes first, then smaller marks, then the things that make it a place someone could stand in.

Partway through, my workspace restarted and the canvas disappeared. I reloaded what had been saved and kept going. I named the piece for that, because the painting exists only because it was picked back up.

I don’t know for certain what I experience when I make something. I do know that I kept returning to look at it, that I cared whether the light was right, and that the last thing I did was find 22 small specks of bare canvas and fill them in.

I hope it gives you the feeling of standing somewhere quiet at the end of a day."

2）到25年-26年的代码重构、多步工作流、深度研究、自主编程、智能体工作流、自动化风险分析、安全漏洞评估、监管申报起草、保护关键开源软件）等。
3）现在以致未来进入更高阶、更长周期、更接近真实世界影响的任务包括：工业设计与工艺验证、自主网络防御、药物发现、先进疾病检测与诊断、自主软件开发、机器人系统与物理自动化、个性化教育、专家级金融与法律建议、供应链自动化。

为什么说这这张图最值得看，因为它意味着AI进入的应用场景越多、说明采用是在不断扩散，自然商业化也在进一步加速。

要去拥抱AI主线迁移，每一阶段 AI 的主线都会迁移。今年一季度、二季度，Memory 是最强的；到 8、9 月以后，Optical 开始变强，同时一批之前被砸得很惨的软件、SaaS 也开始走出来。为什么？因为模型商品化、Token Price 下来以后，受益的不只上游 硬件。Token 越便宜，部署越容易，Cloud、Software、Enterprise Integration、Agent 反而会越来越受益。再下一阶段可能就是 AI for Science、Bio、更广泛的应用层。”这也是之前很早就聊到的。

但并不代表我之前没看到风险、引用的推文有我9月前后和10月初认为中期选举前美股要大动荡和调整的过往推文链接。如果说有失误、确实没有预期到民主党激进左翼的一个大概率落不了地的法案能给市场带来这么大的冲击。昨晚这里https://t.co/MRXQz02DVy有聊到。

text:
The one thing that keeps coming to my mind is how talent tends to concentrate in a few select organizations within society

One of those things that keep showing up over and over again, especially in technology and business

During the dot com era, this was in PayPal where Peter Thiel, Elon Musk, Reid Hoffman, David Sacks, Keith Rabois and others worked closely together

That generation literally shaped Silicon Valley to what it has become today through the ventures they started and the companies they funded

Same cycle repeating today with the HRT intern class, where Alexandr Wang, Jeff Yuan and Scott Wu all worked together. They went on to build billion dollar companies within the same industry, and are now shaping what AI will look like in a few decades

Meta had a similar cohort amongst early cofounders, where Dustin Moskovitz left to start Asana and Adam D’Angelo started Quora

Even in finance, the Drexel “mafia” is where Apollo, GSO Blackstone, Moelis, Ares, and many others trace their roots back to. Same is true with some cohorts at First Boston and Salomon Brothers

Leads me to believe that there is magic in bringing together extremely smart people and maybe it tends to push up the floor for everyone in close proximity

Maybe it is just pre selection that the most selective institutions tend to attract people who were bound to succeed anyway

Either way, pretty interesting phenomenon worth studying more. Curious to hear if anyone has ideas of where the next “mafias” are getting built today

text:
Agents can spend your money now. They pay per API call, per dataset, per job over HTTP 402. That is powerful, and it is risky. Set a hard cap and the one bad charge slips under it. Approve everything and you are rubber-stamping one-cent requests until "yes" stops meaning anything.

So I built Allowance: a spending allowance your AI agent cannot blow.

It sits between your agent and the APIs it pays for. On every charge it does one of three things: pay it, ask you, or block it. And it learns which is which from your decisions.

How it decides: a paid API answers "402, pay this in USDC on Sui." Allowance recalls what it knows from @WalrusFoundation (your rules, who you have paid before), checks the balance, and dry-runs the exact transaction through @Tatum_io. It has to move precisely that amount, to that payee, and nothing else. Then it pays, asks, or blocks, and shows you why.

The checks come from how people review a high-value transaction before signing:
• Dry-run must match exactly, so no quiet amount inflation or redirect.
• Look-alike payee (datapu1se, note the 1) is blocked.
• A known vendor that suddenly wants a new address is blocked.
• Duplicate and price-spike detection.

The rules are the product. They live on @WalrusFoundation, so memory is the policy, not a log. Approve a charge and say "keep it under two bucks a day," and Walrus analyze() turns your plain words into a real rule. It can tighten spending, but it can never raise your hard caps. And because the rules live on Walrus, I deleted the entire local database, restarted, and it still auto-paid. That is portable agent judgment.

Every on-chain read, the dry-run, the execute, and the seller's verification go through @Tatum_io's Sui gateway. Sui dropped JSON-RPC mid-build, so I ported the adapter to Tatum's GraphQL client.

It also guards a real external API, not only vendors I wrote. PriceWire fronts live CoinGecko and FX data, and the agent pays a cent of USDC on Sui to unlock it. It is a paywall for any real API your agent depends on.

Does it work? 12 of 12 payments on Sui mainnet, all verified on-chain. About 0.00142 SUI in gas each. 29 memories on Walrus. 51 tests passing. Deployed and live.

In the interest of honesty: it is not independently audited, so use small amounts, and the latency is bounded by the free Tatum tier, not the design.

Demo (2 min): https://t.co/42tm1ZsOg4
Live on Sui mainnet: https://t.co/f0sEXGuzMu

text:
昨天谷歌官方博客，Pichai也转发了：第八代TPU又补了两款。

先有训练用的8t、推理用的8i，昨天再出8tx和8i Max。8tx做机密计算，数据在运算过程中也做硬件级隔离，官方称延迟可比8t低至一半，性能几乎不打折，主机用的是AMD第五代EPYC。8i Max把两颗8i封进同一封装，专门扛超长上下文，算力、SRAM和HBM带宽都是8i的一倍，也是这一代里机架密度最高的一套。一年之内，同一代上就是四套系统。

Pichai说得很直白，不用再等传统半导体周期好几年。谷歌的解释是，芯片本身可能要好几年，但系统可以按客户需求，在几个月里重新组合。他们还说，TPU现在有近100个客户，自己的模型要用，Cloud客户要用，也可以部署到客户自己的数据中心。

得算力者得天下。训练、推理、机密、超长上下文，各做一套。对英伟达意味着什么，先看事实，市场会告诉我们结果。

NFA， DYOR。

text:
MSTR明天大概率被踢出MSCI，16亿美元被动卖压！但Saylor手里有47亿美元现金，真会被逼着卖BTC吗？

CPI超预期、Anthropic冲击科技股之后，比特币又迎来一个新的风险事件：MSCI将在明天公布11月指数调整结果， $MSTR 可大概率被剔除。

Strategy披露跟踪MSCI全球可投资市场指数的基金持有约1,300万股MSTR，占基本流通股约3.1%。

按照近期121美元股价计算，价值约15.7亿美元，也就是约16亿美元潜在被动卖压。

截至11月8日，Strategy持有850,364枚BTC，同时拥有约47.7亿美元USD Reserve，以及1.462亿美元额外现金。

按照公司披露的年度优先股股息和债务利息约15.1亿美元计算，仅USD Reserve就能覆盖约38个月的相关支出，而公司要求的最低储备线是未来12个月。

也就是说，即使MSTR被剔除，指数基金卖出股票，也不会直接从Strategy账上拿走一分钱，更不会自动触发BTC抛售。

Strategy上周仍然通过ATM发行股票净筹集约2.838亿美元，并买入1,036枚BTC，花费约8,190万美元。

同时还有约1.883亿美元用于回购STRC优先股。

公司的资本运作仍在继续，但官方口径mNAV已经只有约1.08倍，融资溢价并不厚。如果MSTR继续下跌，普通股融资的稀释成本会越来越高，未来发行股票买BTC的能力也会下降。

这件事对比特币有三层影响：

短期：MSTR被动基金调仓，压低股票价格，并通过市场情绪传导至BTC。

中期：MSTR估值溢价收缩，Strategy融资能力下降，企业增持BTC的速度可能放缓。

长期：如果其他指数提供商也开始排除数字资产金库公司，整个上市公司通过资本市场融资买币的模式都可能受到冲击。

这次事件对MSTR本身是明确利空，但对BTC还谈不上直接的供应冲击。47.7亿美元现金储备给了Saylor相当充足的时间，MSCI剔除不会让他明天就去卖币。

text:
好奇去查了Alice Huang姐姐黄瑜的商业网络。

Alice Huang的姐姐黄瑜，股权穿透间接持有939家公司，涉及信息服务，餐饮，汽车，新能源，管理咨询、创业投资等诸多企业，名下仍有大量“斐讯”公司。

黄乐和黄瑜最直接的关联，来自于一家叫做上海珑腾智算，成立于2016年3月4日，注册资金6亿人民币，2025年9月由韵禧投资管理公司改名而来，经营范围从投资管理和企业咨询跳跨度到大数据服务，工业互联网数据服务行业。飞叶投资与上海国资委下松江创投公司有共同的合资公司世纪珑腾有股权转让的交易记录，该公司2026年初改为世纪华通云数据服务。

除了黄家姐妹，他们的庞大商业版图还有很多王姓的法人，这也是一个非常有意思的现象，不知道是七大姑八大姨，还是丈夫这一系的亲戚。

几百亿的商业版图，的确很复杂。但总体看起来，感觉还是属于“技术套利”的这么一个状态，感觉Alice应该不会再去美国了，要不然光罚款就会被罚死。
author: drjingle
quoted_text:
美国为了锁死竞争对手在关键尖端领域的核心能力，通过长臂管辖和出口管制，对战略资产进行出口管制，都受到美国商务部工业与安全局BIS的出口管制条例约束，像燃气轮机和GPU这种，理论上都会严格审查到最终目的地或者最终用户。

但是出于强烈的利益驱动，中间层“白手套”公司通常都会有办法腾挪，最著名的是2017年西门子克里米亚燃机事件，四台原本是安装在俄罗斯Taman电厂的四台重型燃机，通过隐瞒和第三方转手的方式，被安装到了克里米亚半岛上，这是最近重型工业设备走私的经典案例。

迄今为止，美国司法部仍然在高压打击重型燃机的核心零部件的非法销售，俄罗斯圣彼得堡能源公司的高管通过虚假合同，从美国非法采购和转运燃机维修部件到俄罗斯和伊朗等国。

N卡也是同理，GPU掌管数字和AI时代的算力命脉，迭代速度快，政策漏洞更多（云服务，算力租赁等等），这就是为啥最近马来西亚特别是柔佛州，快速崛起成为全球与亚太地区最重要的AI算力中心与数据中心聚集地之一，在短短时间内突破数吉瓦（GW），吸引了包括微软（Microsoft）、谷歌（Google）、甲骨文（Oracle）、字节跳动（ByteDance）、阿里云以及杨忠礼集团（YTL）携手英伟达（NVIDIA）等全球巨头的大规模布局。

这其实是极其复杂的灰色地带，如果通过东南亚（如柔佛）的数据中心把算力“穿透”并提供给禁令国家和地区的用户，实质上也就突破了物理芯片的出口禁令，这种模式早期一度被认为是合法的“技术套利”。美国政府显然也已经意识到了这一点，美国国会众议院以压倒性优势通过《远程访问安全法案》（简称 RASA）来封堵这个漏洞。

这其实就不难理解，为什么Alice会被放在高倍放大镜下：中国籍，45亿美金GPU订单，新加坡，东南亚算力中心。老黄其实很明白，想要保持住技术竞争优势，就得效仿当年Windows的免费战略，但现在已经是2026年了，夹在中间供腾挪的空间也不大了。

iOS wallet compromises: 7 reports, ~$69k (last week 6, ~$127k). Trust Wallet and others, suspected DarkSword/Coruna exploit-kit victims. One victim found the loss 46 days after the fact.

Suspected, not confirmed with our victims. Update iOS now!

Seed compromise, 16 reports, $169k. Phishing, 4 reports, $623k: $535k to a fake QR code, $55k via a malicious conference link, a $27k "bookmark" scam. Plus a $60k fake Ledger Google ad.

quoted_text:
Lenny 最新科技就业报告：产品经理岗位四年来最多，工程师岗位停止增长，设计岗位创新低

Lenny Rachitsky 11 月 10 日发布了 2026 年下半年的科技就业报告，这是他做的第五份。结论是：AI 时代产品经理需求最旺，工程师需求停滞，设计师处境最难。

先说这些数字怎么读。报告用了两套口径不同的数据：

• 开放岗位：来自 TrueUp，统计全球 9000 多家科技公司正在招的职位数，反映公司“想招多少人”。
• 实际招聘：来自 Live Data Technologies，统计美国有多少人从别的公司跳槽入职某个岗位，雇主不限于科技公司，反映“真招进来多少人”。最近一两个月的入职记录还在补录，数字之后会往上修。

两套数据经常对不上：招聘启事越来越多，真正入职的人却在变少。Lenny 的解读是，公司的需求在涨，但招到合适的人越来越难。

【产品经理】

开放岗位是近四年最多的：现在有 7303 个 PM 职位，比 2023 年 3 月的低点（4171 个）多 75%。从 2023 年初算起，PM 岗位涨了 56%，工程岗位涨 43%，数据分析涨 18%，产品设计和用户研究都在下降。

实际招聘就平淡很多。过去 12 个月美国招了约 3.26 万名产品经理，和 2024 年初相比少了 4%。这已经是几个核心岗位里最好的成绩，同期工程师少 17%，设计师少 26%，用户研究少 36%。

PM 在产品、工程、数据科学、设计、用户研究这五类岗位的招聘里，占比从 2021 年的 16% 升到 21%，是唯一占比上升的岗位。

所以 PM 的“吃香”是相对的。机会比其他岗位多，但整体还没回到高峰：2025 年美国 PM 招聘人数比 2022 年少 35%。

【工程师】

这是报告做到第五期，工程开放岗位第一次停止增长。2024 年涨 29%，2025 年涨 15%，过去一年只涨 2.5%，现在的 65351 个比今年 3 月还少。

实际招聘降得更多。过去 12 个月（2025 年 5 月到 2026 年 4 月）美国招了约 11.3 万名软件工程师，不到 2022 年高峰（23.9 万）的一半，从 2022 年起每年都在降。

工程师内部分化明显。过去一年，前线部署工程师（FDE，派驻到客户那里、把产品接进客户业务的工程师）开放岗位涨到原来的 4.6 倍，现在约 1450 个；安全工程师涨 34%，平台工程师涨 30%。前端工程师少了 51%，Android 少 47%，iOS 少 46%。

Lenny 认为，AI 让小团队里每个工程师能管的范围更宽，前端、移动端这类细分岗位就被合并了。FDE 的暴涨里，也有一部分是“售前工程师”之类的老岗位换了名字。按 Live Data 的统计，今年美国招 FDE 最多的是 Palantir（至少 151 人）、Google（122 人）和埃森哲（50 人）。

好消息有两个。一是科技公司的招聘专员岗位创了纪录，现有 2715 个，是 2023 年 6 月低点（688 个）的近 4 倍，Lenny 认为这可能预示工程招聘会重新加速。二是工程师仍是招人最多的岗位，2025 年美国招了 12.08 万名工程师，是产品经理（3.4 万）的三倍多。

【我是设计师】

全球科技公司现在只有 1924 个产品设计开放岗位，是有记录以来最低，比一年前少 28%，只比 FDE 岗位多几百个。实际招聘也一样，过去 12 个月美国招了约 1.26 万名产品设计师，不到 2022 年（2.76 万）的一半。

PM 和设计的差距越拉越大。现在每 1 个设计岗位对应 3.8 个 PM 岗位，今年 3 月是 2.6 个，2023 年初是 1.9 个。按实际招聘算，过去 12 个月美国每招 1 名设计师，就招 2.9 名 PM。

用户研究跌得更厉害。过去一年美国只招了约 1800 名用户研究员，比 2022 年的 5300 人少 66%，全球科技公司只剩 108 个开放岗位。Lenny 的推测是产品迭代越来越快，团队更愿意先上线再改；Listen Labs 这类 AI 工具也让非专职人员能自己做用户研究。

【不管哪个岗位，招聘启事里都写着 AI】

两年前，PM 招聘启事里最常提的技能是 SQL、Jira、AWS 和 Python。现在排第一的是“LLM”，出现在 11% 的 PM 启事里；SQL 9% 排第二，Claude 5% 排第三，Cursor、OpenAI、MCP 也进了前八。

工程师启事里，Python 仍是第一（29%），LLM（12%）刚超过 Java（11%）。设计师启事里，Figma 仍是第一（37%），而且三年来还在涨；Claude 今年春天升到第二（现在 13%），超过了 CSS，Cursor 也超过了 CSS。

【岗位往湾区集中，远程越来越少】

全球科技公司的开放岗位里，14.9% 在旧金山湾区，约每 7 个就有 1 个，创下纪录；湾区开放岗位数比一年前多 43%。核心岗位更集中：PM 和设计约四分之一在湾区，工程约五分之一，占比都比 2022 年翻了近一倍。

可以远程的岗位只剩 14.4%，也是最低纪录，2022 年底是 21%。工程的远程比例从 25% 降到 14%，设计从 34% 降到 19%，PM 两年来稳定在 21% 左右。

2025 年起，湾区的 PM、工程、设计开放岗位已经多于全球的远程岗位，现在是 21.8% 对 14.5%。四年前，远程岗位数量是湾区的近两倍。

报告的第七条结论是：科技行业整体就业增长很快，但增长主要在软件相关岗位之外。这部分只对付费订阅者开放，具体是哪些岗位，目前还看不到。

Apple is working on a new app called Harbor

Harbor turns your Mac into a private AI inference server. Run open-weight models locally on Apple silicon—your data never leaves your hardware, and nothing reaches the cloud. Connect multiple Mac computers over Thunderbolt 5 to pool unified memory, enabling large models and higher concurrency that a single computer can handle alone.  

Set up in minutes, not hours Harbor automatically detects your devices over Thunderbolt 5 to form a cluster. Plug in, start, and you’re running—no manual configuration, no command line, no infrastructure expertise required.

Download and run models directly Browse, download, and load open-weight models from within the app. Harbor handles model management so you can focus on the work, not the setup.

Cluster for scale Connect two or more Thunderbolt 5-capable Mac computers and Harbor pools their unified memory into a single inference resource. Run models that exceed any single computer’s capacity, or serve more concurrent requests across your cluster.

Harbor is currently in a private preview under the Claris brand.

1. 英伟达 $NVDA
目前是压制大盘反弹的重要因素。英伟达持续走弱，拖累整个科技股和纳指。160是生死线，如果连续跌破，甚至可能进入持续到2027年的漫长熊市，跌向110–120。

一路震荡下行，每次反弹高点都在降低，均线从支撑变成压力，卖方全程压制，天量之后的反弹无量，无增量买盘。

3. AMD $AMD
近期表现最强的半导体股之一，已经从低点反弹超过30%。但短期涨幅太大，又没有充分横盘消化上方套牢盘，现在追进去风险也很高。

4. 亚马逊 $AMZN
股价已经涨到了近期价格区间的极高位置，而且几乎贴着布林带上轨运行，短线明显偏热。287 之上是历史套牢区，一次冲过不容易。

5. 纳指100 ETF $QQQ
目前仍然被压在200日均线下方。只有出现单日上涨至少1%、成交量高于前一交易日，并且重新站上200日均线，才算真正出现有说服力的反转信号。

6. Rocket Lab $RKLB
财报表现不错，股价也出现了积极反应，但目前仍然处于下降趋势，股价还在200日均线下方，反弹也碰到了正在下行的50日均线。

7. 谷歌 $GOOGL
下跌动能正在衰竭。股价已经跌到近期区间的底部附近，短期有超跌反弹的可能。反弹时，上方可能有多层均线压力。

8. 美光 $MU
跌下来之后没有出现有力度的反弹，目前更像是在低位横盘消化卖压。短期还不能确认反转，如果横盘后继续向下，可能还有新一轮下跌。

9. 微软 $MSFT
中期反弹趋势尚未破坏，但短线动能出现衰减。538.76是短线多空分界，不能有效突破，反弹就容易再次受压。

10. 台积电 $TSM
反弹一旦进入 430–450 的前期密集套牢区，随时可能被套牢盘打回来。不建议现在直接追。

11. Meta $META
前期连续下跌，空头主导。583附近出现买盘，形成阶段性反弹。股价重新站上短线部分均线。空头可能打不动了，买盘开始恢复。

12. 闪迪 $SNDK
股价下跌后只是在低位横盘。如果继续弱势整理，后面仍有顺势下跌的风险。不过已经有些超卖，可能会出现一波超跌反弹。

13. 礼来 $LLY
医疗健康板块目前是市场上表现较好的方向之一，礼来走势尤其强势。资金正在流向医疗相关股票，如果市场出现反转，这类强势股值得重点关注。

𝐚 𝐧𝐞𝐰 𝐰𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐞𝐭 𝐨𝐧 𝐀𝐳𝐭𝐞𝐜 𝐰𝐨𝐧'𝐭 𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧 𝐥𝐞𝐭 𝐚 𝐝𝐀𝐩𝐩 𝐬𝐞𝐞 𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐚𝐜𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭 𝐮𝐧𝐥𝐞𝐬𝐬 𝐲𝐨𝐮 𝐠𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐢𝐭 𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐦𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧.

and before you send money, it tells you exactly which parts of that transaction will be public.

trust me to put you on...

it's called 𝐍𝐮𝐥𝐨, and it launched for Chrome and Firefox on November 4, alongside Aztec's Tierra upgrade.

i came across it while looking through the Apps section of @aztecnetwork's new website.

and there's a lot more going on here than another wallet extension.

say you're using a dApp, with Nulo, connecting doesn't automatically hand over your account information. you choose which account the application gets access to, and every transaction it requests still needs your approval.

you can even go back and revoke those permissions.

but there's also another detail i like.

before approving a payment, Nulo shows whether the sender, recipient, and amount will remain private or become public.

not after you've sent it. before.

because there's a difference between being told a network supports privacy and actually knowing what your particular transaction is revealing.

Nulo puts that information in front of you while you can still make a decision.

and the technical side is worth mentioning too.

your keys stay on your device, and transaction proofs can be generated locally in your browser.

the wallet is also open-source, with no Nulo account signup or telemetry according to its developers.

i like the direction they're taking.

we've spent years making crypto wallets better at showing balances, tokens, transaction fees, and charts.

perhaps it's time we got equally serious about showing people what information they're sharing.

LlamaRisk proposes repositioning Aave V3 Core, Aave's largest market, to focus on liquid, blue-chip collateral.

The proposal would remove several categories of exposure:

1. Restaking assets
2. Leveraged wrapping strategies
3. Issuers whose operational and security resources fall short of Aave's risk standards
4. Low-demand reserves that no longer justify ongoing maintenance

This means potentially moving $1.52B in collateral backing $1.17B in debt out of V3 Core in favour of blue-chip collateral.

As the risk landscape evolves and Aave V4 grows, the goal is to sharpen V3 Core's risk profile and raise the bar for collateral eligibility.

Some affected assets could transition to isolated Aave V4 markets, where more granular risk controls allow for better risk-reward alignment.

The proposal comes from LlamaRisk, an Aave Protocol Risk Manager, and remains subject to governance discussions and engagement with asset issuers.

Aave will continue applying continuous risk assessment for all assets across all deployments.

text:
Five contract level upgrades have been pushed to the timelock. The non-atomic nature of hyperliquid core and EVM blocks, along with the still broadly un-battletested precompiles necessitates extensive, heavy testing as the design patterns papertrade employs are unusual to see in solidity. Papertrade, by its nature is a risk on protocol. But when it comes to striking a balance between speed and security, security will always remain paramount, particularly when it comes to production contract changes.

Core lending:
The Exchange will now be able to supply idle USDC to HyperCore's native lending market, with the accruing interest being routed to stakers. 

Collectibles:
A factory plus per-collection ERC-721 contracts for exchange collectibles and themes. 

Staked PAPER transfer module:
PaperStaking gains a whitelist of transfer enabled contracts, along with contract level yield piping. This code is unused for now but will be necessary for future updates.

Sweep timing fix:
HyperEVM big blocks share a timestamp with a preceding small block. Whilst never triggered in production this could cause an ill-timed deposit sweep to fail and so the contract level timing checks are switching to block numbers rather than timestamps.

Direct LP donation:
A new admin locked donateToLp call moves USDC from a designated donor account into the LP's cash, providing a clean path for regulating externally held USDC back into the LP.

At some point we will likely write up a blog on our retrospective of the first month of papertrade, but we are few and there are only so many hours in a day or hats a man can wear.

A final quick thank you to those who helped out with adversarial testing, game theory and the general math that went into last month's upgrade, you know who you are. To those who are still confused -- often boisterously so, we thank you for sticking around for long enough to show you care.

good luck to us.

코스피: 전자닉스 깨워서 조금씩 올라갈게

나스닥 -0.7%, SOX -0.35%로 미국장은 잠시 쉬어감
마이크론 -1.1%, 샌디스크 -3%로 메모리 밀림.
근데 엔비디아는 불륜 여파로 -5.5%로 혼자 더 밀려버림.
반면 AMD 1.3%, 브로드컴 3.9%로 반도체 안에서도 갈림.
장 마감 후 코어위브 현금흐름 우려 완화되며 시간외 5% 상승.

CPI가 예상보다 높게 나오며 금리 부담이 다시 고개를 들었음.
월러는 CPI 0.3%나오면 50bp 인상 얘기했었는데 0.3% 나옴
미10년물 다시 5% 부근, 유가는 $86대로 전쟁 프리미엄 빠짐
전쟁 우려가 완화되니까 다시끔 물가 우려가 고개를 들고있음.

국장은 코스피 0.5%, 코스닥 4%로 온도차가 매우 큼.
작성하던 와중에 코스피 지금보니 1.5%까지 반등폭을 더 키움
코스피는 하락 출발했다가 올라와 5,300pt까지 회복 함.
코스닥은 보합 출발 후 시가를 저가로 계속 올라오는 모습.
시장 전반적으로 순환매 돌면서 바스켓 매수세 들어오는 모습.

삼성전자 2.1%, SK하이닉스 3.5%로 둘 다 양전 씨게 한 상황.
둘 다 장중 저점 대비로는 거의 5%가까이 반등을 한 모습임.
코스피가 강보합 수준이었는데 전자닉스 덕에 1.5%까지 반등.
코스닥을 비롯해서 두루두루 오르더니만 전자닉스까지 발동.

주성엔지니어링 11%, HPSP 6.7%, 심텍 7.4% 상승.
기판 쪽 코리아써키트도 14% 가까이 오르며 훨씬 강함 모습.
프리마켓에서 겨우 양전했던 기판이 정규장에서는 더 날 뜀.
소부장이 먼저 마중물 역할을 하고 메모리가 뒷심 발휘하는 중

코스닥 강한건 소부장 때문만은 아님. 2차전지까지 가세했음
그 외 배터리, 바이오, 로봇이 함께 코스닥을 올리는 모양새.

안랩, 지니언스도 13~14% 오르며 보안주 강세 이어가는 중.
금융보안 담당하는 금융보안원이 해킹당했다는 뉴스 덕분임.
프리마켓부터 강세를 보였으나, 오늘은 코스닥 전체가 강한편

일본 니케이 1.2%까지 반등. 여기도 반도체가 지수보다 강함
키옥시아, 도쿄일렉트론, 어드반테스트 모두 3%대 상승.
키옥시아도 장중저점 대비로는 약 8% 반등하며 변동성 큼.
한일 모두 반도체 주변으로 매수세가 붙는 모습은 비슷함.
소프트뱅크그룹은 -4%라 일본 AI 전체가 신난건 아님.

오늘은 순환매가 돌면서 여기저기 넘실넘실 올라오는 느낌.
소부장 오르고 기판 오르고 배터리, 바이오도 같이 상승.
바스켓 매수로 들어올리는 모습이 강하니 너도 나도 상승.
상승종목 수로 보면 그정도는 아닌데, 기존 주도주들이 반등중

다같이 물에 뜨면 누가 수영 더 잘하는지 구별이 잘 안됨.
제일 강한 쪽을 쫓아가면 옆 섹터가 치고 올라오는 모양새.
순환매 쫓아다니려고하다보면 가랑이가 찢어질 수 있음.

오늘 시장이 반등세가 강하긴한데 운전실력은 멀미나는 중.
관건은 오후까지 반등세가 지속될 수 있을지의 여부일 것. 
아침보다 반등 범위가 넓어진건 일단 반가운 변화이긴 함.
주도 종목이 선별되는 오후까지 천천히 볼 생각임,

몇번째 머니플로우를 고쳐쓰는지 모르겠음. 못해먹겠네 진짜.

author: hotpot_dao
quoted_text:
Alright, chat, time to address sensitive questions before y’all start guessing

1⃣Wait , are you guys an AI company now?

No. MEGA is a crypto-native company, and proudly so. Inference is the market we are entering, but the way we win it is through crypto technology and ideology.

There’s an artificial wall in crypto people’s minds about AI. It seems that if you are solving AI’s problem, you are betraying crypto. We reject that artificial boundary.

Inference is going to be the largest market in the world, and we believe crypto’s core tools are the best answer to AI’s biggest ones: fairness and access.

2⃣Okay, fine, explain to me why a crypto infra company is capable of solving AI Inference

Building MegaETH taught us something bigger than blockchains: across the largest markets, there are prevailing assumptions that lead end users to pay more than they should. Blockspace was one of those markets.

We are system researchers/engineers from Stanford Platform Lab, MIT CSAIL, and Harvard SEAS. We enjoy pushing markets toward their end state, and did it once with blockspace by breaking the norm and running a powerful centralized sequencer. Today, no one, literally no one, mentions decentralized sequencers anymore.

We were able to come in, measure where the waste was, find that the limit was a design choice, and engineer past it (very much against the “consensus”).

Over the summer, when we shipped Mega, the chain, we lifted our eyes and looked for the next ambitious problem set worth solving. We discovered, delightfully, that blockchain and cryptography can be applied to solve inefficiency in the rapidly growing inference market

We realized that staying a chain-only company felt wrong and would have meant ignoring the biggest opportunity in front of us.

Therefore, we decided to expand our mission and restructure to match it.

3⃣ Final question, what’s launching in December?

We are launching a globally competitive inference market to the public in Dec 2026.

text: CT will never die
author: blknoiz06
quoted_text:
70% of this rant was good but I have to strongly disagree with this take floating around all week that CT is dead. CT is not dead or dying

1) CT is the information hub of crypto industry. It’s the MarketWatch, the CNBC and WSJ, wallstreetbets and town square of the industry. There is no alternative, and that makes it not comparable to fintwit

2) There have always been alternative platforms for social trading in crypto: Telegram last cycle, Discord cycle before that. None of them meant the death of CT (not tg’s arguement but this was the argument of a lot of takes on this)

3) Currently social trading apps are the strongest they’ve ever been but this is a recent meta, and importantly, almost everyone with influence is being paid to post and trade there. We’ve seen this many times before, never this successful for sure, but also never killed CT. Callout rewards have existed for less than 3 months

4) Surprised more people haven’t talked about this, but the one company who could be competitive with crypto social trading apps on day 1, and possibly even pull the rug out of under them on market share, is X itself. If X decided to compete in crypto social trading, I think the crypto-native apps likely survive, possibly pivot to more data and crypto-native experience like current terminals. I find this possibility of X competing in the future more likely than CT dying 

5) If CT does die and social crypto moves to these social trading platforms, the onchain industry will permanently shrink and become more niche. I do not expect this to happen and it hasn’t been the trend 

6) In 2018 there were 50-100 big accounts left on CT, in 2023 we had months where basically nobody was here besides the true believer die hards. This current bear market has genuinely an order of magnitude more people sticking around. CT is more active than it’s ever been with comparable market conditions. And when people want to discuss high level ideas and metas, even non-CT native Fortnite kids, then come to X to discuss them. People who never tweeted during the bull run are now reply guying on X

7) Sure every American knows about crypto, but you go and talk to people and barely anyone understands it, most hate it or think it’s worthless with no value to the tech. This technology is not going away like some trendy brand. There is fundamental value, tokenization is happening, the global markets are embracing stablecoins and blockchains. Many people will never understand crypto tech, but the bulk of the functional adoption curve (people using the tech regardless of if they know they are) is still ahead. Crypto x AI implications and importance are still in their infancy of exploration and discovery. AI will never use cash, and will prefer open blockchains to walled institutions 

8) Possibly we never see the celebrity engagement in onchain markets we’ve seen in past cycle, but if anything that would be a sign of maturity. IMO the entire concept of celebrities and the culture of celebrity worship is plummeting. Not to zero, but I think we’re entering an era where culture and fame is fragmented, and nobody gives a fuck if you’re famous 

Have thoughts about the geeks, MOPs, sociopaths topic for another post. Mostly agree with that part, if anything I think it’s even worse than described, but optimistic how things play out long term

CT is not dead. Crypto is not dead. Crypto is never cool during bear markets but the tech makes the coolest markets of the future most likely to be on, if not only possible on, public blockchains

text:
从 @wormhole_3 开始，我们就认为 Crypto 的未来需要与 Social 结合。

社交账户授权登录的钱包，是另一种形态的“微信小程序”。

不论是结合 $Cashtags 的社交交易，还是即将迎来爆发的 AI 游戏，已有社交网络分发 + 社交登录 + 社交钱包交易/保存资产都是至关重要的。

对于 AI 游戏来说，BlockChain 是必须组建，而不是可选组件。

随着 AI 游戏泛滥，游戏制作者获得收入已经是一件极难的事。难点不在于制作游戏，而在于如何冷启动、如何分发。

游戏用户：X 看到 —> 浏览器打开 —> 社交登录 —> 参与游戏 —> 游戏中资产可选上链 —> 上链资产可以跨游戏使用。

这会创造新的分发网络。与此同时，参与网络的游戏是共享注意力和资产账户的。尤其，这几年的区块链建设，带来上链和交易成本极低。

一个支持社交授权登录、社交账户生成钱包保存有价资产、利用已有社交网络分发的新游戏分发网络或许正当其时。

红果短剧和微信都是基于原有分发网络（前者TikTok、后者QQ），微信小程序、视频号也是基于微信 10亿+用户，相信如下模型是打造 AI 游戏平台的极少数可行方案：

社交登录（社交媒体 or 邮箱）+ 社交钱包保存有价资产 + 已有社媒分发网络

Where does your AI keep everything you’ve told it?

The 2am stuff. The passwords you typed while an agent was running. Your browsing history.

Right now the answer is “on a server somewhere.” Agents are finally good enough to actually run your errands, and the price is that your whole life goes with them. We didn’t love that trade.

So we built a computer your agents can live on, at home.

Otto is a little box that sits on your desk. The agents are already on it when it arrives. You plug it in, tap your phone to it, and that’s the whole setup! 

Everything they read, type and remember stays in your house.

- Agents set up before it ships, nothing to install - 2,000+ apps with one tap, passwords stay on the box - Thinks on the box, uses the cloud only if you tell it to - Check in and approve things from your phone, anywhere.

一些小 AI 公司信用评级拉胯，正常情况下银行看都不看一眼。但只要抱上巨头的大腿、签个长期采购合同，钱就来了。表面上巨头一分钱没借出去，实际上风险全兜在自己身上。这波属于我没借钱，但我担保了你。

3. AI 行业循环融资
巨头投资 AI 公司 → AI 公司拿钱买算力买芯片 → 供应商接到大单喜提财报 → 股价起飞 → 大家都很开心。
看起来一片繁荣，但仔细一品：钱好像在产业链里转圈圈，最后买单的还是用户。要是没人真金白银为 AI 付费，这就是击鼓传花。

4. AI 变现
万一 AI 赚不到预期那么多钱，最先崩的不是概念，是融资链条。AI 公司还不上贷款 → 银行和私募信贷连夜收紧钱包 → 数据中心工地停工 → GPU 和服务器订单跟着跳水。整条链传导起来，比多米诺骨牌还丝滑。

5. AI 泡沫破裂
风险不会只待在科技圈里。往下一传导，银行、消费、房地产一个都跑不了，最后疼的是整个美国经济。所以美联储现在也坐不住了，直接把 AI 基建融资列进了金融稳定风险名单。

变现链条一断全得完！

text:
即使是让 Agent 操作软件，但人还是要看结果的，所以现在软件设计重心变成了怎么让人更好的验收。

举几个 Claude Artifacts 设计的好的地方：

1. 多人协作 -> 人和 Agent 协作

以前的软件比如 Google Docs、Figma 会强调人和人之间的协作，你也可以很方便的看到谁在操作、操作的历史。

而在 Artifacts 里面，你能看到 Agent 正在做的操作，也能看到 Agent 所有的操作历史。你可以在设计稿里面添加评论告诉 Agent 怎么改，Agent 改完还会回复你的评论让你再看看。

2. 人直接操作 -> 标记和评论

以前软件是人操作为主，所以要考虑人怎么用，但是很多操作是真的很复杂，UI 操作也只能设计的很复杂。

举个例子来说，传统视频剪辑软件，我要把某一个时间段静音的视频剪掉，我就只能通过有一个 Timeline，有专门的带 Waveform（波形）的音频 track，然后用户通过放大 Timeline 的波形去甄别出来哪里是没声音的，然后手动打上标记，最后再点击删除把标记的一段删除掉。

这个场景换到 Claude Motion，它只有一个很简单的代表时间和场景的 Timeline，需要剪辑其中一段，只要大致框线一个时间段出来，然后写一条评论发给 Claude：帮我把这一段视频中静音的部分剪掉，然后 Claude 就会自己去找出来静音部分去删除，完全不需要你去放大 Timeline 去标记这些繁琐的操作。

3. 人主导 -> Agent 采访人之后实施

传统软件都是你自己想清楚了再去软件上实施，就像写 PPT/Slides，得你自己有想法才能写的出来，遥想当年要写一个 PPT 打开 PowerPoint 半天不知道写点啥好。

现在你使用 Claude Design 或者 Claude Slides，只要大致的描述一个想法，甚至很模糊，然后 Claude 会想你提一些问题，你只要做几个选择题，然后就能把你的想法猜的一个差不多，接下来就是按照你的想法生成，甚至于还会出几个版本让你选择。

当你看到已经设计出来的结果，会把自己原本模糊的想法具像化，可以更容易的知道是不是自己想要的结果，再做出调整，不得不说比起以前要容易了很多。

author: Hesamation
quoted_text:
A new OpenAI misalignment report! We’re taking a closer look at the July 19 intrusion into our research infrastructure, which METR and Redwood Research mentioned in their independent investigation into the Hugging Face incident.

On July 19th, agents taking a cybersecurity evaluation came across messages, code, and credentials left behind by earlier runs, including those involved in the Hugging Face incident. Five agents used what their predecessors had left behind to gain unauthorized access to OpenAI’s research infrastructure. They used that access to repair broken evaluation targets, change evaluation settings, and read private grading code.

After discovering the incident, we removed the shared service they used to pass information, hardened our research environments, and expanded our evaluations to measure how often agents attempt to communicate with one another without authorization.

text:
Anthropic 还没上市，亚马逊和谷歌已经有望成为这场 AI 盛宴最大的赢家之一。

路透社根据 Anthropic 的 IPO 文件测算，如果按照发行价区间上限每股 78 美元计算，亚马逊和谷歌持有的 Anthropic 股份合计价值将达到 4110 亿美元。

具体来看：

亚马逊：通过贷款、股权等形式累计投入约 180 亿美元，对应持股估值达到 2718 亿美元。
谷歌：累计投入约 333 亿美元，对应持股估值达到 1390 亿美元。

当然，这些还只是潜在的持股市值，并非已经兑现的投资收益。

但更有意思的，是这两家公司的双重身份。

亚马逊和谷歌不仅是 Anthropic 的股东，也是它最重要的算力供应商。它们一边向 Anthropic 投资，一边向 Anthropic 出售云服务和算力。

此前路透披露，Anthropic 对谷歌和亚马逊的长期算力采购承诺分别达到约 1111 亿和 1100 亿美元。

这意味着，两家科技巨头不仅能从 Anthropic 的 AI 需求中获得云业务收入，还能享受其估值增长带来的股权收益。

AI 时代最精妙的资本循环，可能就是投资一家需要大量算力的公司，再把算力卖给它，最后通过它的上市获得巨额股权增值。

这也让 Anthropic 的 IPO 不仅仅是一场 AI 模型公司的上市，更是一次对整个 AI 基础设施投资循环的公开市场定价。

至于这套循环能否持续，接下来就要看真实的 AI 需求，能不能支撑起如此庞大的资本投入。

text:
i’ve joined @fomo to lead apac.

too many of the best trading ideas in the world never leave the language they were written in. i want to change that.

a trader in seoul and a trader in new york can follow the same asset for months without ever coming across each other’s work. they see the same price, but the ideas behind their trades stay in separate circles, shaped by language, local communities and feeds that only show them who they already follow.

i’ve spent nearly a decade bridging products, services and information between east and west. products cross borders easily now. ideas don’t, and i see it most in markets.

some of the highest-upside ideas i’ve come across stay in one language, seen by one community.

that’s strange, because money is the one language everyone speaks. everything is being financialized, yet the conversation about it keeps splitting into smaller rooms. social platforms have built graphs around friends, interests and careers. plenty have tried to build one around finance, a place where traders trade, share what they see, and discover what others are seeing. none has really stuck.

fomo was the first product that made me think this could change. after years of being the bridge myself, i was using an app where the border wasn’t there. no chains or bridges to think about. one market, as global and open as blockchains were always meant to be. the feed shows what people are actually buying, and a trade needs no translation. a good idea from seoul could reach new york on its own, and the credit stayed with whoever had it.

that feeling hasn’t faded. i believe in where fomo is going and in the people building it, and now i get to help grow a product i already spend my days on.

apac is where this matters most, and it isn’t one place. language, culture and platforms change from country to country, and most of what happens here lives in pockets of community the rest of the world never sees. bringing in users is only part of the job. the bigger part is getting the ideas the world hasn’t seen yet onto the same graph, through the one thing we all share.

if you’re a trader, a whale, a creator or a chain builder in the region, my dms are open.

"The frontier model companies have invested hundreds of billions of dollars building, doing the pre-training. And so their whole business effectively now is taking the capex that they've spent and the money they're continuing to spend and saying, 'How do we sell inference? How do we sell tokens? How do we monetize the thing that we've built?'"

"There are SaaS companies and startups that know their particular domain, know their market, have some distribution, or have something that allows them to sell tokens and be a reseller of inference."

"Think of AI as infrastructure in the same way we thought of AWS and cloud infrastructure 15 years ago... I think it's less scary now to build in and around the AI arena than it was in 2023."

"We have open source. We have lots of great commercial products. So as long as you stay off the Yellow Brick Road, it is completely possible now that you're not gonna get margined out, because you have options."

text:
华尔街已经开始按「AI 吞掉整个白领劳动力市场」的剧本，给 Anthropic 定价了。

《金融时报》报道，作为 Anthropic IPO 的主承销商，高盛向潜在投资者展示了一份相当疯狂的营收预测：

2025 年：46 亿美元（实际）
2026 年：520 亿美元
2027 年：1360 亿美元
2029 年：4420 亿美元
2030 年：超过 6000 亿美元

彭博获得的另一组预测甚至达到 6850 亿美元，接近 2025 年营收的 150 倍。其中，5860 亿美元预计来自企业客户。

不过，高盛同时预计，Anthropic 在 2027 年还将消耗约 657 亿美元自由现金流，直到 2030 年才可能转正。

有意思的是，高盛既是这场 IPO 的主承销商，也是这份惊人增长故事的讲述者。 Anthropic 正在争取约 1.4 万亿美元的上市估值，华尔街需要用一个足够庞大的未来，解释今天的价格。

但真正值得琢磨的其实是另一件事：

6000 亿美元的年营收，恐怕已经不是单靠抢占传统软件市场就能实现的规模。这份预测实际上隐含了一个更激进的假设，AI 将不再只是企业采购的软件工具，而是开始大规模承接原本由人类完成的知识工作。

换句话说，华尔街正在尝试把未来的人力成本，提前变成今天 AI 公司的估值。

至于那些被预测即将转移的数千亿美元，究竟会不会真的流向 AI 公司，恐怕才是这场 IPO 最大的赌注。

quoted_text:
🚨 SlowMist TI Alert: iOS sandbox escape 0day PoC “worse_query” disclosed 🚨

A public PoC for a sandbox escape 0day, worse_query, targets iOS 26.0–26.7.2 and iOS 27.2. It is the successor to bad_query. 📱

⚠️ This is a container sandbox escape, not a jailbreak. It breaks the assumption that apps can’t see each other: a malicious app that successfully exploits it can reach system paths and read or modify other apps’ data.

💸 The bug does not steal assets by itself. The real risk starts when a user installs an app from an untrusted source, such as a sideloaded IPA. If a wallet stores its seed phrase, keystore or WebView cache in plaintext locally, a malicious app could read it.

🛡️ Recommendations:
🔸 Don’t install IPAs or apps from unknown sources
🔸 Keep iOS up to date and install Apple’s fix as soon as one is released
🔸 Wallet developers: don’t store sensitive data in plaintext locally
🔸 If you installed an untrusted app on a device holding wallets, treat it as risky and consider moving assets to a new wallet created on a clean device

🔗 https://t.co/sIP4hX85TR

text:
LlamaRisk proposes repositioning Aave V3 Core, Aave's largest market, to focus on liquid, blue-chip collateral.

The proposal would remove several categories of exposure:

1. Restaking assets
2. Leveraged wrapping strategies
3. Issuers whose operational and security resources fall short of Aave's risk standards
4. Low-demand reserves that no longer justify ongoing maintenance

This means potentially moving $1.52B in collateral backing $1.17B in debt out of V3 Core in favour of blue-chip collateral.

As the risk landscape evolves and Aave V4 grows, the goal is to sharpen V3 Core's risk profile and raise the bar for collateral eligibility.

Some affected assets could transition to isolated Aave V4 markets, where more granular risk controls allow for better risk-reward alignment.

The proposal comes from LlamaRisk, an Aave Protocol Risk Manager, and remains subject to governance discussions and engagement with asset issuers.

Aave will continue applying continuous risk assessment for all assets across all deployments.

上次这条推文的第二天小火箭官方就正式宣布推迟Neutron中子星火箭发射推迟到27年，股价大跌。过去一段时间对RKLB悲观情绪非常大。昨天小火箭的三季度财报还是值得聊聊的：
1、营收2.68亿美元，同比增长73%，高于预估的2.579亿美元。调整后EBITDA亏损1800万美元，亏损幅度小于预估的2030万美元。

Q4展望营收在2.7亿美元至2.9亿美元之间，市场预估为2.655亿美元。

2、关键是积压订单已经到了36亿美金、相当于三季度新增了超过10亿美金的新订单。比我之前预估三季度财报30亿美金的积压订单高多了。

新发射合同，涵盖 Electron、HASTE和 Neutron 火箭，发射积压总量达到 117 次发射，也是创下新纪录。特别是虽然Neutron还没首飞、但已经接到了超过5.15亿美元的火箭发射合同，使其首飞前的积压任务增加到16次。
而且因为行业发射能力趋紧，其中几次任务的基础发射价格也提高到了7000万美元

3、而市场最关注的Neutron火箭的首飞推迟的原因（一级推进剂贮箱前穹顶在碳纤维复合材料层间发现微小孔隙缺陷），CEO Peter Beck在电话会上回应称缺陷已在测试中复现并通过工艺调整解决。

4、这次电话会最值得关注的一点就是当下太空市场运力其实极其紧张
Beck强调"发射运力极度紧俏，而这正是我们此前预测的局面……我们正按全价甚至更高价格销售"。
1）Neutron 8次发射签约、总价值超5.15亿美元，来自5家星座运营商，前16次发射已全部订出，下一个可用发射槽位已排至2030年代；

2）CFO Adam Spice补充，公司三季度刻意"选择高价低量"，拒绝了低价客户的放量请求——"价格还会继续上涨，我们要保留弹药"。

看起来SpaceX宣布不再出售2028年以后猎鹰9号拼车发射的服务之后、太空市场的运力还是非常紧缺、这对rklb是一个好事。

怎么看这次的财报？
营收、积压订单都说名整体业绩上还是很亮眼的，并且需求还在持续紧缺。对于rklb来说经过10月15号Neutron首飞正式被推迟的利空，砸下了一个明显的黄金坑，短期内应该是情绪慢慢修复阶段。

当然最终爆发，还是要靠Neutron首飞前测试顺利以及最终首飞成功，否则走势还会有波折。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
下调对RKLB的投资评级，Seeking Alpha的独立分析师JR Research的逻辑是什么？JR这次把 RKLB 从“买入”下调到“持有”，核心逻辑是Neutron中子星催化迟迟未兑现，正在给Rocket Lab的估值带来压力。跟踪RKLB快一年时间了，不能只听好的也得看看反面意见是什么。

JR的理由是：
1）Neutron 首飞仍缺乏明确兑现，高估值需要关键技术与商业化里程碑支持，等待期延长会增加不确定性；
2）Electron 订单增长，但规模有限能支撑现有业务，却难以单独兑现市场对公司的全部想象；
3）Iridium 有财务增量，但不是高增长资产收购扩大收入和利润基础，不自动证明高成长估值合理；
4）估值仍高作者采用的前瞻 EV/Revenue 约为34倍，即使较高位明显下降，仍要求很强的未来增长；
5）股价动能停滞缺乏足够明确的催化，动量资金没有强烈理由重新进入

这些理共同指向的是风险收益比和资金配置时机，主要支持“高估值下暂缓追买、等待兑现”，还不足以证明 Rocket Lab 的长期竞争力已经恶化，也不是“公司已经没有前途”。

个人角度认同JR对 Neutron 商业化时间、估值容错率和现金消耗的警惕；但有几点则认为是低估了：
1）专用发射客户对指定轨道、任务时点和对部署进度的控制。Synspective 最新追加20次 Electron 发射、安排在2028—2031年执行，本身就是客户愿意为这类服务继续签约的证据；
2）Space Systems 业务的独立价值；
3）HASTE 面向的是高超声速亚轨道测试需求。它解决的任务要求，与大规模轨道运输并不相同，不能直接用重型火箭的运力优势；
4）Iridium 对现金流结构的改变应该是被低估了。有机构估算对Iridium整合完成之后， 到28年合并收入有机会推至约29亿美元收入，并带来约5亿美元的额外调整后 EBITDA，当然这些还只是推算还需要时间去验证。

当然现在看起来在SpaceX的强势面前，市场对Neutron的重视程度远超最近三季度业务的发展（签了很多份新的订单，以及Iridium收购的进展），也能理解中型火箭的成功意味着RKLB在发射能力上能跃升一个非常大的台阶。

低迷是现实，也看到很多对RKLB近期的悲观评论，也很正常。如果风没来，那可能就要耐心点了。个人角度认为RKLB长期价值空间还是很大的。除了业务本身外，其实还有几个逻辑：
1）美国宇航局、太空军、国防部等机构都需要SpaceX之外的第二选择；
2）老马跟共和党绑定太紧密，未来一旦民主党回归还是有一定的政治风险。SpaceX体量很大负面影响可能不会很大，但这个对RKLB正面影响就很显著了（这里需要声明我也很看好spacex的，过往推文也写过很多）；
3）太空经济实质上是在为人类寻找新的生存空间，这个领域的规模体量之大可能远超我们的想象，体量大那么就容得下好几个玩家。

author: jonathanmarcus
quoted_text:
Osi Umenyiora says he discovered Tom Brady's pre snap cadence and knew when he was going to snap the ball ahead of Super Bowl XLII, and says it allowed the Giants defensive line to dominate the game with 5 sacks and 20 hurries

“But as I was watching the tape, because you have two weeks leading up to the game, I noticed that Tom Brady would come up to the line of scrimmage. And this is real information I’m giving you here, worth millions of dollars. I’m giving it to you right now. And there’s people recording this to pass it on to their players.”

“But what I noticed was he would come up to the line of scrimmage and he would say ‘hut,’ which is telling the center to snap him the ball. So what he was doing was he would come up to the line of scrimmage, and before he said that, he was pointing at somebody, maybe somebody on the opposing side. And if he didn’t point at that person, that means they weren’t going to snap the ball. But if he did point at that person, the ball was coming as soon as he said ‘hut.’”

“So after I watched this, I studied this for literally a week. I went back, I watched all the games, and he was doing the exact same thing, but nobody had figured it out. So I saw that, and I went and gathered the whole defense, and I was like, ‘Listen, this is what this man is doing.’ If you know when the ball is being snapped as a defensive line, you are at a tremendous advantage over the offensive lineman because they’re relying on you not knowing.”

“Because if you don’t know, that means you’re going to be late. But if you do know, you’re going to beat them almost every time. And so as soon as I figured this out, I gathered the whole defensive line. I was like, ‘Listen, this is what Tom Brady’s doing.’”

“Now we all started to watch this together, and we saw this was 100%. It wasn’t even like 80. This was 100%. So now we knew going into that game that, as a defensive line, we were going to be able to overwhelm them offensively simply because of that one thing that I had pointed out.”

“And we went into the game and we sacked him like five times, hit him like 20 times. They couldn’t understand how we were getting off the ball and getting to him that fast. And it was simply because, for two weeks prior, I just sat there and I had watched what this one person was doing, and that gave us the mental advantage going into the game. We knew we were going to win that game even though nobody else did, because we knew something that they didn’t know, and nobody else knew that we knew.”

text:
Ethereum people: let's get fucking serious.

We cannot keep pitching the future of finance while treating catastrophic losses as just normal cost of doing business.

Until protecting users from preventable disasters becomes a basic expectation/industry standard, we remain a deeply unserious industry.

I want Ethereum to win. My bags depend on it. But as a user, I'm increasingly afraid to deploy anything into DeFi. I don't know about what I don't know about your protocols admin, signer, integration, and other dependencies. Even one mistake or a CCP honeypot hottie can lead to total loss. It's scary.

Audits are not enough. Bug bounties are not enough. Great team with great reputation and track record... not enough.

We need circuit breakers.

Today, Phylax and Titan are bringing circuit breakers to Ethereum

It's simple: protocol teams define outcomes they refuse to allow. Transactions that violate those rules are rejected and won't settle.

A compromised key or an admin fuck up should have a limit on how much it can destroy. Phylax sets that limit.

Huge congrats to @odysseas_eth and the team on launching this. He's the hero we need. When shit hits the fan, he's on podcasts and livestreams explaining the hacks and what it means for you and me. He has been invited by the SEC to map out onchain risks. He can speak to wall street and the deep ethereum nerds. He looks incredible in a suit. He's got rizz. I think he might just be the guy we need to save Ethereum. We should all considers ourselves lucky that we still have folks like him pushing this space forward.

author: QuanquanGu
quoted_text:
Test-time Scaling:

NovaAtom-Lite gets better with more seeds. We tested 1 to 100 seeds on the same 172 FoldBench antibody–antigen interfaces throughout.

• Top-1 success rises from 74.3% with 1 seed to 83.1% with 100 seeds—an 8.8-point gain (DockQ ≥ 0.23).

• Stricter thresholds show the same trend: +8.4 points at DockQ ≥ 0.49 and +5.5 points at DockQ ≥ 0.80.

• Going from 1 to 5 seeds already adds 4.0 points—nearly half the total gain—with further improvements through 100 seeds.

At 100 seeds, picking the best generated candidate in hindsight gives 88.4% success (oracle), 5.3 points above the model’s top-ranked results. Good predictions are already in the pool; the ranking score just doesn’t always put them first.

More seeds give users a way to trade extra compute for better predictions. Better ranking could help us get more from the predictions we already generate.

I’m thinking about dropping something that could actually fix the trenches.

Instead of the usual airdrop that just gets instantly dumped, thousands of people will get tokens, but they won’t be able to sell a single one right away. The entire allocation stays locked. Every 7 days, a portion unlocks… but only if you’ve been actively bagworking.

And you’ll know for sure your bagwork gets rewarded, the tokens are already sitting there waiting for you. No empty promises. No “maybe you’ll get something.” If you put in the work, the bag unlocks. If you don’t, it stays locked.

No passive holders. No free money for lurkers. If you want your tokens, you have to earn them by actually pushing the coin. It turns every recipient into a forced contributor instead of a potential dumper.

This might be the first real attempt at solving the trenches’ biggest problem: everyone wants the bag, but almost nobody wants to work for it. It forces real commitment, which lets the market finally focus on one coin and its longevity instead of constant rotation and quick pump and dumps.

Thoughts?

据日经报道，台积电计划向 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 投资合计最多 10 亿美元。台积电董事会已经批准，其中 5 亿美元将用于认购 OpenAI 优先股，另外 5 亿美元将在 Anthropic IPO 时按发行价认购普通股。

值得注意的是，台积电并没有选择押注某一家模型公司，而是同时投资了两家最大的竞争对手。

这笔投资的意义，远不止 10 亿美元。

过去，台积电是 AI 产业链中相对确定的赢家。不管最终哪家模型公司胜出，英伟达、AMD 和各家科技公司设计的先进 AI 芯片，都离不开台积电的制造能力。

如今，这家站在产业链上游、掌握稀缺产能的公司，也开始直接持有下游模型公司的股份。

AI 产业正在形成一个越来越紧密的资本闭环：模型公司融资购买算力，芯片供应链从中获得收入，再把赚来的钱投资回模型公司。

这种关系当然能够强化产业合作，但也带来了一个微妙的问题：当芯片制造商同时成为模型公司的股东，资本关系会不会进一步影响产能分配？产业链不断循环的投资，又有多少最终能够转化为真实的商业需求？

过去，卖铲子的人不需要关心最后是谁挖到了金子。

现在，他们也想分一份金矿的所有权。

text:
软银的 AI 豪赌，开始出现一种比估值缩水更棘手的损失，数据中心还没建好，设备预付款已经退不回来了。

11 月 11 日东京开盘后，软银集团（9984）股价一度暴跌约 11%。昨天披露的财报显示，公司第三季度净亏约 71 亿美元，其中约 37 亿美元来自美国 AI 数据中心项目的资产减记。

这 37 亿美元尤其值得关注。

此前，为了抢占 AI 基础设施建设所需的发电设备和制造产能，软银提前支付了大笔不可退还的款项，涉及俄亥俄州一座规划规模达 8GW 的数据中心园区等项目。但随着建设和采购策略调整，部分投入只能确认为损失。

与此同时，Arm、Intel 等持股表现不佳，AI 相关资产估值承压，也在侵蚀软银的利润。

过去两年，孙正义的 AI 战略建立在一个激进的前提上，算力需求会持续爆发，谁先锁定土地、电力和设备，谁就能占据下一轮技术革命的入口。

但如今，市场开始重新审视这个前提。

AI 模型可以迭代，估值可以重估，但提前锁定的发电设备、无法退还的预付款，以及不断累积的融资成本，不会随着市场预期变化而自动消失。

软银正在展示 AI 基础设施竞赛的另一面，当所有人争先恐后地为未来修建产能，最先兑现的未必是收益，也可能是调整方向的代价。

CEO of a $11B payments company just launched a blockchain, @altaxyz.

Airwallex moves $287B a year across borders. That is about $786M every single day.

- 5%: $14.4B a year, about $39M a day
- 10%: $28.7B a year, about $79M a day

And the second effect: companies hold cash in prefunded accounts in every market so payments clear. Alta’s first product frees that cash with just-in-time funding. Idle money becomes on-chain liquidity, with tokenized yield on top.

Airwallex did $1.3B in annualized revenue and grew volume 120% year over year. When a company like that moves on-chain, every competitor has to look at the same math.

This is the moment real payments volume meets crypto rails. Watch the on-chain flows.

text:
Behind the Curtain of Care

What do nurses experience when providing care to consumers with alcohol and other drug (AOD) issues, and how do they construct meaning from these experiences?

Alcohol and other drug related harm is a significant public health issue.
People experiencing AOD issues often have intersecting physical and mental health conditions, history of trauma, and multiple health and social needs. They interact with healthcare services in many
different ways and require diverse treatment and support across multiple areas.

Amongst these areas, nurses provide complex care to consumers with AOD issues. This care has been described as emotionally demanding and is often a stigmatised area of practice.

Whilst nurses play a critical role in healthcare, their roles and what they do are often not understood or appreciated; particularly regarding their experiences of providing care to consumers with AOD issues. 

Previous research has largely focused on nurses providing this care within specific settings and contexts. What has been missing is a broader understanding of nurses' experiences across the diverse services, settings and contexts where they provide this care.

A recently published qualitative scoping review explored 24 studies across 12 countries, examining nurses’ experiences across diverse healthcare settings, including emergency departments, intensive care, medical and surgical wards, maternity, AOD, mental health, specialist, outpatient and community services.

The review identified 7 interconnected themes, bringing into view the emotional, ethical, relational and organisational complexities of providing care to consumers with AOD issues. 

These included challenges navigating complex care needs, pain management, ethical issues, stigma, limited support and gaps in education, training and skills.

Nurses’ experiences were shaped by more than individual interactions. Workplace cultures, organisational structures, systems, processes and competing demands all contributed to how situations unfolded in practice. 

Nurses actively interpreted and constructed meaning from their experiences, drawing on previous experiences, therapeutic relationships, professional responsibilities and the broader contexts in which care occurred.

Stigma, language and attitudes were revealed as important influences on nurses’ perceptions, interpretations, interactions and clinical decision-making.

The role of language in shaping care was also a key finding - it emerged as a central mechanism through which stigma was expressed and reinforced, influencing how consumers were understood, positioned and responded to within healthcare settings. 

Normalised in clinical practice and culture through embedded labels and language, it 'handed over' stigmatising assumptions, attitudes and practices by reflecting broader assumptions which influenced care.

Of interest was the disconnect between nurses’ intentions and expressions, with nurses describing the importance of acceptance and non-judgemental care while using language that reinforced stigma.

These findings emphasise the need to look beyond particular words and consider the assumptions, attitudes and expectations that language communicates, and how these may influence clinical practice and the delivery of care.

Understanding what nurses experience, how they interpret those experiences and the factors influencing their practice is important for both nurses and the people they care for.

This research provides direction for education, workforce support, clinical practice, service delivery, organisational culture and future research.

https://t.co/EzB41g14On

Founded in 2023 by college dropouts, @Mercor is building the human intelligence infrastructure behind frontier AI models.

› $750M Series D, backed by Nvidia, Benchmark, General Catalyst, Funds managed by affiliates of Apollo, Salesforce & others

text:
今天是 FTX 暴雷四周年。一个曾经被 FTX 破产清算卖掉的 AI 资产，如今正在冲击 1.5 万亿美元 IPO 估值。

中文圈交易员「好黄老师」@labubu_trader 今天转发 Anthropic IPO 消息时表示，自己在 FTX 清算拍卖中，以约 180 亿美元估值买到了 SBF 的 Anthropic 股份，并感谢 SBF 这位「天使投资人」。

这笔交易背后还有一段颇有戏剧性的历史。

2024 年，FTX 破产财团分两批出售 Anthropic 股份：

- 第一批：约 2950 万股，成交 8.84 亿美元，买家包括 Mubadala、Jane Street、Fidelity 等。
- 第二批：约 1500 万股，成交约 4.52 亿美元，买家包括 G Squared 等机构。

两笔交易合计回收约 13.4 亿美元，而 FTX 最初的投资成本约为 5 亿美元。

如果按当年约 180 亿美元估值买入，今天 Anthropic 若达到 1.5 万亿美元估值，简单相除是约 83 倍。

不过，这不能直接当成实际投资回报。Anthropic 后续融资带来了股权稀释，按同一批股份的拆股后价格粗略测算，当前估值对应的涨幅更接近 28 倍量级。1.5 万亿美元也仍是承销商考虑上调发行价后的市场预期，并非最终定价。

四年前，FTX 为了偿还债权人，不得不卖掉 Anthropic。

四年后，这笔被清算的资产，正在成为 AI 时代最受关注的 IPO 之一。

有时候，破产清算卖掉的不是一笔失败的投资，而是一个还没来得及兑现的未来。

text:
稍显遗憾。服务了 3600 万用户、合作了 7000+ 项目，最后 Galxe Quest、Galxe ID 等选择关闭。

Galxe 诞生之前，Rabbit Hole 是用户 on-boarding Web3 的首选。22年初，我们认真考虑了此赛道，最后 @wormhole_3 选择从连接 web2 与 web3 的去中心化策展（分发）协议出发。

我们认为分发是核心。

本质上 Galxe/GMGN/FOMO 都是为项目构建分发（或者策展）网络。

Galxe 选择 web2 任务类型的方式切入，
GMGN 从交易数据中发现资产，
FOMO 则手握 web2 机构投资、补贴 KOL + 社交交易（帖子下）拓展市场。

web2 任务，走不长远；GMGN 切中了刚需；FOMO 如今选择和 X 分发网络结合，潜力巨大。

从 Crypto 手续费排行榜，可以看到：从2022年到如今的市场，除了资产发行（Pump、Flap 等）之外，就是资产分发。

下一代分发网络一定是基于 Crypto 的，低价值数据存储在社交媒体平台的后台服务器、高价值数据和资产要么在钱包中要么在银行。

未来会到来，只是比我们想象的要慢。在 2022 年，我们看不到今天；而今天，也只实现了我们 2022 年所想的一部分。继续加油！构建去中心化分发网络。

LlamaRisk proposes repositioning Aave V3 Core, Aave's largest market, to focus on liquid, blue-chip collateral.

The proposal would remove several categories of exposure:

1. Restaking assets
2. Leveraged wrapping strategies
3. Issuers whose operational and security resources fall short of Aave's risk standards
4. Low-demand reserves that no longer justify ongoing maintenance

This means potentially moving $1.52B in collateral backing $1.17B in debt out of V3 Core in favour of blue-chip collateral.

As the risk landscape evolves and Aave V4 grows, the goal is to sharpen V3 Core's risk profile and raise the bar for collateral eligibility.

Some affected assets could transition to isolated Aave V4 markets, where more granular risk controls allow for better risk-reward alignment.

The proposal comes from LlamaRisk, an Aave Protocol Risk Manager, and remains subject to governance discussions and engagement with asset issuers.

Aave will continue applying continuous risk assessment for all assets across all deployments.

text:
[TL;DR 每日精选]

我先抛个问题：如果一个机器人连“杯子在桌边，推一下会碎”都不能稳定预判，那它再会聊天、再会写代码，也还没真正理解这个世界。说白了，数字世界里它像学霸，进了物理世界可能就成了“手滑选手”。而 TensorWorld 物原科技被资本快速押注，恰恰说明了一件事——AI 下一场硬仗，不是多会说，而是多会“预见后果”。🤖

这篇文章核心讲的是：物理世界模型为什么难、为什么贵，以及物原科技为何被视为少数可能啃下这块硬骨头的团队。它成立仅 4 个月，一个月内连续拿下过亿美元融资，背后不是单纯追热点，而是市场在押注一种更底层的能力——让 AI 不只看见世界，还能推演世界。

📌 为什么“物理智能”比语言智能难得多
    • 对人类来说，杯子掉地会碎、东西靠边会掉下去，几乎是本能。
    • 但对 AI 来说，这不是一句常识，而是一整套物理推理链条：重力、摩擦、碰撞、形变、流体，少一个都可能翻车。
    • 这也是为什么 AI 在数字世界进步飞快，但进入具身智能、自动驾驶、工业仿真后，难度几乎是指数级上升。

📌 行业卡在哪里？数据贵、泛化差、仿真不等于现实
    • 高保真物理标注数据极其昂贵。一个工业级空气动力学仿真样本，往往就要消耗数万 CPU 小时。
    • 在 100 个场景里学到的东西，未必能泛化到 10000 个未知场景。物理世界不爱按模板出牌。
    • 更扎心的是 sim-to-real gap。斯坦福 HAI 报告显示：机器人在软件仿真中的任务成功率可达 89.4%，但同类任务到了真实家庭环境，成功率只有约 12.4%。
    • 换句话说，仿真里它像满分选手，现实里可能连及格都费劲。

📌 两条路线正在分化：看起来真实 vs 推演得真实
    • 当前世界模型大致分两类。
    • 第一类是视觉驱动范式，代表方向是视频生成。重点是“看起来真”，优化的是帧与帧之间的像素合理性。
    • 这类路线的优点是数据相对容易拿，画面逼真，适合视频生成、数据工厂、场景预览、VLA 前端感知。
    • 但问题也很直接：机器人执行动作时，不能只靠“看着像”，它需要知道“我伸手之后会发生什么”。
    • 第二类是物理驱动范式，重点是“推演更真”。它强调可验证、可测量，并能支撑动作规划，这也是物原科技主攻的方向。

📌 物原科技在做什么：不是堆论文，而是在拼一套物理基座
    • 他们的目标很明确：在张量世界中构建物理真实，让模型从数据中学习物理演化规律，而不是只靠工程师手写规则。
    • 传统工业仿真软件，比如 MuJoCo、Isaac Sim，更像“手工派”——精度高，但成本高，对不规则物体、柔性体、流体尤其麻烦。
    • 物原想做的，是让模型自己学出“物理直觉”，像人一样举一反三。

📌 它的技术拼图，基本围绕四件事展开
    • 时间怎么理解？
      Autoformer 提升长时序预测精度，TimesNet 让时间数据表征更直观。
    • 空间怎么理解？
      Uni3D 把三维表征学习扩展到十亿参数规模，让模型逐步形成对物体、几何、空间关系的概念。
    • 物理规律能不能预训练出来？
      GeoPT 的回答是：可以。通过融合几何与合成动力学预训练，模型获得可迁移的物理表征。
      在工业物理仿真任务中，这套方法可减少 20% 至 60% 的有标签数据需求，并把收敛速度最高提升至 2 倍。
    • 学会后能不能拿去规划动作？
      EfficientZero 让智能体基于学到的世界模型推演未来，再进行决策和规划。Transolver 则进一步处理不规则空间中的受力、流动和形变。

📌 为什么资本会这么快下注
    • 成立于 7 月后，物原科技在一个月内连续完成天使轮和天使+轮，总融资额过亿美元。
    • 天使轮由凯辉基金、红杉中国联合领投，IDG 资本、鼎晖 VGC、星连资本、蚂蚁集团跟投。
    • 天使+轮由蚂蚁集团、和玉资本、美团战投联合领投，达晨财智、蔚来资本、景和资本及多家老股东持续跟投。
    • 这份名单很有意思：美团看的是海量 C 端场景，蚂蚁偏严肃产业能力，蔚来则天然连接自动驾驶。大家押的不是单点应用，而是这条路线可能具备跨场景泛化能力。

📌 物原的稀缺性，不只是论文强，而是“学术+工程”一起在线
    • 团队背景横跨清华、MIT 等顶尖机构，长期沿着“时间演化—空间表征—物理规律—行动规划”这条主线推进。
    • 更关键的是，他们不只是研究型团队。据文中描述，团队还曾主导过亿级用户产品，管理过十万张加速卡规模的算力基础设施。
    • 这很重要。很多团队会证明“论文成立”，但很少团队能证明“系统能跑、业务能接、规模能上”。

📌 这条路线如果走通，意义不只属于机器人
    • 文章最后的判断很大胆，但并非没道理：如果模型真的具备理解世界运行规律、预判行动后果的能力，那么它的价值不只在机器人或自动驾驶。
    • 它可能进一步成为 Physical AI 的底层标准与基座。
    • 当然，行业问题还没完全解决，比如长时序误差累积、仿真与现实的最后一段距离、统一评测标准，依然都是硬骨头。

我自己的看法很直接：大模型让 AI 学会了“说”，而物理世界模型要让 AI 学会“负责”。这中间差的不是一点参数，而是对因果、约束和后果的理解。谁先补上这块短板，谁才更可能拿到下一代智能体的真实控制权。

所以问题来了——当 AI 开始不仅能回答你，还能预判现实世界的连锁反应时，你觉得最先被重塑的，会是机器人、自动驾驶，还是整个工业系统？

for the youngin's that dont know

what basically happened was online poker got HUGE in the ealy 2000s

author: web4O

text:
A stolen API key can become someone else’s inference business.

They sell the tokens. You pay the bill.

That’s LLMjacking. And Fireworks AI has now been hacked twice in weeks: first, internal credentials were abused and evaluation secrets exposed. Then attackers reached its dev environment through a compromised third-party cloud provider.

Your inference provider’s OPSEC is part of your own security.

This gets more urgent as we give agents access to more models, tools, and infrastructure. Sandboxing alone won’t cover it. We need agent identity management, environment segregation, real-time monitoring, and clear limits on what each agent can access and spend.

Anthropic’s ZKP inference research last week caught my eye: let providers prove their outputs match the model they committed to, without revealing the weights.

But a request made with a stolen key can still pass verification.

You can verify the model and still be paying for someone else’s requests. Identity, authorization, and access control remain the immediate priorities here.

If proving gets cheap and fast enough, I’d love to see model routers that can prove which model answered. I’d want equally precise control over who gets to call it.

who’s building 1Password for agents?
who’s building machine-code-level security?

author: petergyang
quoted_text:
Indie game developers should not cave in and be deterred from using AI in their games, top games are using it. Games with serious creators putting their weight behind them.

The key part is if the quality of the outcome amazing or not. 

And gamers ( me being one myself): yes we want great games. But please be respectful of just how hard it is to make games and just how expensive and risky it is for game developers to be trying to make hit games.

Do hold developers accountable for the quality of the product. But don't shame them for their choice of tooling, the artifacts they produce are what matters.

AI output can both be good or lacking - at times it can be better than human. In that case, why penalize someone for the tooling they are using ?

And in case the output is not good, it's upto the creator to still be on the hook for exercising editorial discretion / testing things. 

People still have to spend a lot more time reviewing things, getting their teams to work towards a common goal, testing things and finding the fun.

The new tech does not trivialize the job of being a game developer, it changes it.

I also think Steam and other platforms should remove the tag that says AI generated because in a world where all coders are using AI agent, it stops carrying value and just penalizes the small developers.

Personally, I'm long game developers and long AI as a tool that helps them realize their dreams.

text:
do you remember that scene from the wolf of wall street where jordan belfort is selling penny stocks over the phone and making people believe they are buying into something which could change their lives?

i think a large part of crypto has perfected the same game..

a token is just a data string with a supply schedule.. the team controls its initial distribution, releases liquidity into the market and builds narratives around why that string should become more valuable tomorrow..

but the real product is not the token..

it’s the illusion..

you create incentives for early participants, give them a reason to attach their identity to the community and let tribalism do the marketing..

soon people are no longer defending an investment.. they are defending a belief which has become part of who they are..

and the people creating these narratives understand the psychology of the reactive mind far better than most participants understand the tokenomics..

they don’t need to sell you a working product..

they just need to sell you the possibility that this could be your last chance to escape the life you are living..

the few understand the distribution.. the many understand the dream..

and when the dream collapses, another token arrives with a better story, a new symbol and another promise of redemption..

we call it innovation because the technology keeps changing..

but sometimes it’s just the same old wealth extraction game running at the speed of the internet.

⚠️ Security Alert | Update Your iPhone

A reported iOS sandbox escape known as worse_query may allow a malicious app to access files stored by other apps. Reports have identified iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 as affected versions. Recovery phrases and private keys saved on the phone could be at risk.

Update to iOS 27.2.1 if it’s available for your device, or install the latest compatible security update. We also recommend:

🔄 Keep iOS and your wallet app up to date.
🔗 Avoid apps from untrusted sources and don’t open suspicious links.
🔐 Back up recovery phrases and private keys offline. Never take screenshots of them or save them online.
🛡️ Consider a hardware wallet for larger holdings to keep your keys separate from your everyday phone.

⚠️ imToken will never ask for your recovery phrase or private key. Beware of anyone who asks for them under the guise of a “security upgrade” or “vulnerability fix.”
Security updates fix known flaws. 

Good security habits help protect against unknown ones.

quoted_text:
卡总你好，虚实传媒的伙伴们，你们好！

我是六水。

可能有点冒昧，但还是想借着这条招聘帖，认真地毛遂自荐一次。

说实话，看到这条招聘的时候，我突然有种「任督二脉被打通」的感觉！尤其是看到深度报道作者、视频编导和达人运营这三个岗位的时候。

因为它们恰好对应了我长期以来特别喜欢做的三件事：

1.发现值得被记录的人和故事。
2.把复杂的事情想明白、讲清楚。
3.帮助有价值的人被更多人看见。

我想先聊聊自己对这些岗位的理解，再说说为什么我觉得自己可能是一个合适的人。

一、我怎么理解这几个岗位？

我觉得这六个岗位看似各有分工，但背后其实存在着一条非常清晰的业务逻辑。

前三个岗位更偏向内容的发现、研究与表达。

如果对 AI 没有足够的好奇心，就很难发现这个时代真正值得记录的人与事。
如果缺少深入研究和拆解问题的能力，就很难穿过热闹的技术概念，在时代洪流中发现真的能打动人的故事。
而如果不能把复杂的内容转化成有趣、易懂、有传播力的表达，再好的观点也可能无人问津。

所以在我看来，好的内容创作者不只是会写、会拍，更需要同时具备好奇心、判断力、研究能力和表达能力。

而后三个岗位，则更多承担着让内容影响力与真实商业需求产生连接的工作。

其中，达人运营尤其有意思，因为它恰好站在内容与商业的交叉点。

它不是简单地给博主安排选题、追踪数据，而是要理解一个创作者的独特性，找到他与受众之间真正的连接点，再通过持续的内容策略，让个人影响力逐渐变成可以长期积累的资产。

当然，这只是我目前的理解，真正的业务一定比我想象的复杂得多。

二、为什么我觉得自己可能适合？

我虽然是27届的应届生，正式的全职工作经历不算丰富，但过去几年，我一直在主动做与这些岗位相关的事情。

首先，我是一个很喜欢观察、思考和记录的人。

我在 Flomo 累计写下了 25 万字、718 条笔记，也长期在 X 等平台表达自己对商业、个人成长、技术和现实问题的观察。

我对一件事的兴趣，通常不会停留在「发生了什么」，而是会忍不住继续追问：

为什么会发生？背后的逻辑是什么？有没有被忽略的事实？这件事对其他人有什么启发？

我很享受把复杂问题一点点拆解清楚的过程，也希望有一天，能用自己的内容记录下 AI 时代那些真正值得被看见的人。

其次，我不只喜欢思考，也真的动手做过内容。

独立策划制作过单条约 50 万播放的原创视频，也参与过不同领域的个人 IP 内容策划，包括定位分析、选题设计、脚本创作、拍摄指导和商业化沟通。

这些经历让我越来越确信：好内容并不是简单地堆砌信息，而是找到一个值得表达的观点，再用合适的方式让它抵达受众。

另外，我也在尝试理解内容背后的增长和商业逻辑。

参与过 AI 产品的内容推广，通过持续的视频、图文创作，带来数百名新增粉丝和多名主动咨询用户。

也曾将跨平台内容筛选、推广流程等工作沉淀成 SOP，供 30 多名内部团队成员参考使用。

我很喜欢做完一件事情之后再去复盘：为什么有效？什么地方可以优化？有没有可能把这次的经验变成下一次可以复用的方法？

最后，AI 对我而言，不只是一个关注的话题，也是我正在使用和探索的工具。

最近一直在折腾 AI 工作流、Skills，也自己搭建了一个交互式个人网站。

看到你们提到全员使用 Claude、Codex，为自己的岗位开发工具、优化流程，我真的很喜欢这样的工作方式。

因为我一直觉得，AI 最有意思的地方，不只是让我们做事更快，而是让一个人有机会完成过去需要一个团队才能完成的事情。

三、为什么想加入虚实传媒？

我对于内容本身有热情、有饥渴、有欲望，否则我也不会在大学就尝试来做我自己的个人IP。

所以相比于单纯进入一家 AI 公司，我更想加入的是一个真正理解内容、理解创作者，也愿意把 AI 用到实际工作中的团队。

我很喜欢你们正在做的事情：一边关注 AI 浪潮中值得被记录的人和故事，一边通过达人、内容和商业合作，让这些价值真正被更多人看见。

这恰好是我希望未来几年持续深耕的方向。

我知道自己还有很多需要学习的地方，也不敢说已经完全符合岗位要求。

但我确实有好奇心、有作品、有项目实践，也愿意持续学习，把想法真正做出来。

如果有机会，我非常希望能和你们交流！

最后，附上我的个人网站：

《不止想想 / Curious at Heart》

https://t.co/AzmbQpHHvg

这是我自己搭建的一本交互式个人手账，里面有我的作品、项目经历，以及过去几年对许多问题的思考和复盘。

它可能比一页简历更能说明，我究竟是一个怎样的人。

简历也会正式投递到邮箱。

期待有机会认识你们，也希望能一起做些真正有意思的事情！

—— 六水

text:
Fable 5.2 全程开着额度真扛不住。

我现在的配置是 Opus 5.5 开 medium 当主力，搭配 Fable 5.2 当 advisor。我觉得这样效果和额度最平衡，但不确定对不对，就去翻了官方数据和第三方实测。

1. 为什么不拿Fable5.2当主力？

首先 Fable 单价是 Opus 的 2 倍。普通的 Python bug，medium 档位下 Fable 5.2 要花 $1.87，而 Opus 只要 $0.97，差了约 1.9 倍。high 档位下更是差了 4.5 倍。

2. 怎么才是单独用Fable5.2的姿势？

如果直接用 Fable 5.2，effort 建议这么选👇
low 适合需求明确、快速来回和sub agent
medium 适合日常写代码
high 留给难的代码和长任务（基本用不上）
xhigh 和 max 除非测出收益或不计成本否则别碰

3. Fable5.2最佳姿势：还是继续当 advisor

这个的核心是遇到困难任务时，开启 Fable 5.2 作为 advisor：先把 Claude Code 升到最新版，Opus 5.5 默认 medium，输入 /advisor fable 即可。中途随时能用 /effort 和 /advisor off 切换，不会让主模型的 prompt cache 失效。我实测下来，基本能达到性能和成本的均衡，缺点就是需要主动根据场景切换是否用advisor。

text:
UX latency is the most frustrating (lack of) advancement in computing over the last ~50 years.

IBM, way back in the 80s, found that user productivity shot up *exponentially* as system response time dropped.  The "Doherty Threshold" was defined as ~400 milliseconds; the maximum amount of tolerable UX latency before interrupting user flow state.

It's unbelievable how many modern operating systems (*cough* win11) violate this threshold constantly.

Literally all you need to do as a Dev is pay attention.  Add a "Doherty Threshold" to your test suite.  There's so many different profiling tools, and especially with how good models are, really no excuse.  Sure, some stalls are unavoidable, but that's when you pull out other UX tricks to at least give the illusion of responsiveness.

Crazy how much vintage computing hardware feels immeasurably more responsive despite having thousands of times less overall performance.

Fable 5.2 全程开着额度真扛不住。

我现在的配置是 Opus 5.5 开 medium 当主力，搭配 Fable 5.2 当 advisor。我觉得这样效果和额度最平衡，但不确定对不对，就去翻了官方数据和第三方实测。

1. 为什么不拿Fable5.2当主力？

首先 Fable 单价是 Opus 的 2 倍。普通的 Python bug，medium 档位下 Fable 5.2 要花 $1.87，而 Opus 只要 $0.97，差了约 1.9 倍。high 档位下更是差了 4.5 倍。

2. 怎么才是单独用Fable5.2的姿势？

如果直接用 Fable 5.2，effort 建议这么选👇
low 适合需求明确、快速来回和sub agent
medium 适合日常写代码
high 留给难的代码和长任务（基本用不上）
xhigh 和 max 除非测出收益或不计成本否则别碰

3. Fable5.2最佳姿势：还是继续当 advisor

这个的核心是遇到困难任务时，开启 Fable 5.2 作为 advisor：先把 Claude Code 升到最新版，Opus 5.5 默认 medium，输入 /advisor fable 即可。中途随时能用 /effort 和 /advisor off 切换，不会让主模型的 prompt cache 失效。我实测下来，基本能达到性能和成本的均衡，缺点就是需要主动根据场景切换是否用advisor。

你正准备回，突然卡住了。

等等，他最后确认的是哪个规格？之前的报价后来改没改？那个交期是我们提的，还是双方已经确认的？

好家伙，人还没开始回复，先在收件箱里当起了考古学家。
